name: Renna Rundt Borredalen
description: The race has the same start and finish as Borredalen Rundt. A few hundred metres from the start are on a gravel road, before the rest of the course continues on a trail. There is a steep, uneven hill after the gravel-road section, followed by relatively flat terrain, apart from the downhill stretch towards the finish.

name: Refleksløpet Arendal, Fossbekk
description: Welcome to the Refleksløpet in Arendal, an atmospheric race in the dark held at Fossbekk in Arendal. The race offers two distances: a short 4.8 km course and a long 7.8 km course, as well as the option to walk without timing. The race starts early in the evening, and participants are encouraged to wear a headlamp for a safe and magical experience. This is a social event where friends, family and running buddies can get together for a fun and active evening.
course_highlights: Two distances: a 4.8 km short course and a 7.8 km long course
The race takes place in the dark, so a headlamp is recommended
Start at the Fossbekk parking area, a scenic location between Krøgenes and Longum
additional: The race office opens at 16:30 for registration and bib collection. The long course starts at 18:00, the short course at 18:05, and walkers without timing can start at 17:00. The first 30 people to register will have the chance to win a Mizuno bag. Registering before race day is recommended to avoid stress. Participants receive a 15% discount on headlamps at Brekke sport's physical store. The long course starts at 18:00 and the short course at 18:05. Walkers without timing can start at 17:00. The race office opens at 16:30, and a headlamp is recommended.

description: Dammekärr Dirt Dash is a trail-running series in Dammekärr organised by the orienteering club OK Alehof. The competition consists of three races with combined scoring, and participants can choose to run one, two or all three races. The courses run through hilly forest terrain and come in three different distances: 1.5 km, 3.5 km and 7.0 km. The short course follows the floodlit trail, while the longer courses require a headlamp. After the finish, runners can enjoy a hot sauna and refreshments in the club cabin, creating a pleasant and social atmosphere.
course_highlights: Hilly forest terrain around Dammekärr
Short course (1.5 km) on the floodlit trail
Longer courses (3.5 km and 7.0 km) require a headlamp
additional: The competition takes place in the evening. Participation is free for OK Alehof members. Timing is done using a SportIdent card, which can be borrowed on site. After the race, a hot sauna and refreshments are available in the club cabin. The series features results, live updates and an archive of previous races.

name: GIF Joggen
description: GIF Joggen is a challenging but friendly competition against yourself or others, an accessible race for everyone, or a wonderful walk in the Gressvik forest. This event is for everyone, from children in strollers to seniors nearing 100 years old. That’s how we can make the most of the day.

name: Begbyjoggen
description: Begbyjoggen is a weekly recreational run in Fredrikstad, offering an accessible event for everyone. The race takes place on gravel paths in the lit trail network. The main course is 6.8 km, starting at the Begbyporten clubhouse and passing Bjørneklova, heading down Alleen, going around the golf course, and returning via Bjørneklova. There is also a separate 4.6 km course for those who want to walk or jog. The event takes place every Wednesday at 18:00, and tickets are sold through Strava.com.
course_highlights: 6.8 km course on gravel paths in the lit trail network

name: Refleksløpet Kristiansand
description: The Reflective Run in Kristiansand invites you to a magical evening run with headlamps on Thursday, November 13. The start and finish are at Fant Olsen in Baneheia, with registration opening at 16:30. Participants can start from 17:00, while the mass start with timing is at 18:00. The course is 4.1 km long and follows the outer edge of Baneheia, marked with reflective markers. Participants must bring a headlamp, and mulled juice and porridge will be served after the finish.

name: Torsdagsløpet
description: The Thursday run in Sarpsborg was a real Easter treat on Maundy Thursday, with glorious weather and a well-deserved break from the long-forecast rain. The run, which takes place on Thursdays until mid-October, offers lovely routes through the extensive network of trails in Kalnesskogen. Although there were a few icy sections, conditions were generally excellent for both runners and organizers.

description: Registration is now open for the second race of the season in the Ålesund Winter Series, which takes place on 28 November. Participants can also register for the entire series until 20 February 2017. The Winter Series began in the mid-1980s in the Furmyra/Åse area, but has had a new course on Gamle Brusdals veg since 2001. From winter 2023, Ålesundløpene will be the organizer of this traditional race.

description: Arborettrimmen is a wonderful tradition that has been held since Einar Søndeland started it in 1978. It set a participation record in 1983 with 587 participants, including Grete Waitz. The race offers distances for everyone in the beautiful surroundings of the Arboretum, where you can choose to run one (2.7 km), two (5.4 km) or three (8.1 km) laps. A 600 m Mini Run for children starts at 14:00.

There will be seven races this season in total, with three before Christmas and four after New Year. The course is the usual route around Eikangervågen, and registration opens at 2:20 p.m.

name: Kristiansund Backyard Ultra
description: Welcome to Kristiansund Backyard Ultra, a unique endurance race taking place on Saturday, November 15, starting at Frei School. Participants must complete a 6.7 km loop every hour on the hour, and the race continues for 12 hours. If you cannot finish the loop within the hour or do not start the next loop, you are out of the race. This format tests both physical endurance and mental strength, pushing runners to complete “just one more loop.” Everyone who completes at least one loop receives a medal.

The race is suitable for anyone looking for an active and social experience in November.

organizer: Lørenskog Friidrettsklubb (Sørum IL er teknisk arrangør)
description: Vinterkarusellen på Romerike is a running series organized by Lørenskog Friidrettslag, offering races for different age groups, from children to veterans. The races take place during the winter months and provide a great opportunity for both recreational and competitive runners to compete and stay in shape. The event has a long tradition and includes several distances and classes suited to different levels. Participants aged 13 to 80 must have an athletics license, which also serves as insurance.

description: Blåmansløpene 2026 consists of three spectacular races from Fjellveien to Blåmanen, with the start and finish at the same location, but on different routes featuring trails, nearby mountains and varied running challenges. Stage 3, held on 14 November, follows a demanding, technical course on trails towards Blåmanen, finishing at Tindevann. The race is suited to runners who enjoy challenging terrain and technical sections, and trail shoes are recommended. Varegg IL welcomes everyone to a great running experience in beautiful surroundings in Bergen.
course_highlights: Start at Fjellveien by «Damen» and finish at Tindevann
Technically challenging trails up Blåmanen through varied terrain
The course includes trails such as Permisjonstien, Sandviksbatteriet, Rundemanen and Blåmansveien
additional: Trail shoes are recommended for the technical sections. The course includes challenging climbs and technical trails. The start and finish are at the same location for all three races. Entry fees are paid by bank transfer or VIPPS to Varegg Fleridrett. The organizer recommends trail shoes; the course is technical, and runners accustomed to trail terrain may have an advantage.

description: Sognefjord Backyard is a unique backyard ultra race held in Sogndal on Saturday, 14 November 2026, starting at 08:00 from Meieriet. The race consists of a 6.7 km loop with approximately 45 metres of elevation gain, run every hour on the hour. Participants have one hour to complete each loop. The competition continues until only one participant remains who has completed one more loop than everyone else. This race challenges both endurance and mental strength, and is suited to runners who want to test themselves in a unique format with no fixed distance.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop with approximately 45 metres of elevation gain
Start and finish at Meieriet in Sogndal
The course follows pavements and shared pedestrian and cycle paths, in both daylight and darkness
additional: Maximum 100 participants. Minimum age: 18. Start and finish at Meieriet, which also serves as a base with space for drop bags and rest. The café at Meieriet is open for food and drink purchases, but participants must arrange their own provisions. Assistance and provisions are only permitted in the start and finish area. Each participant may have one dedicated support person in the participant area. Registration is binding and non-refundable, but the entry can be transferred to another person via Racetracker. Warnings are given 3 and 1 minute before each start. One winner is declared: the participant who completes one more loop than everyone else; otherwise, there is no winner. Start at Meieriet in Sogndal at 08:00 on Saturday, 14 November 2026. If you cannot complete the loop within the hour, you are out of the race.

It is part of the Sør-Helgeland Running Series (SHLK) and offers runners of all ages and levels a great opportunity to take part in a social and active setting. Participants can enjoy a lovely running experience in the scenic surroundings of Viksjøen.

Part of the Sør-Helgeland Running Series (SHLK)

This race is part of Hvam Runners’ training and racing activities and offers a unique opportunity to test endurance and speed in a controlled indoor environment.

name: Gränsö Trailrun
description: Gränsö Trailrun is a running event in Gränsö Nature Reserve outside Västervik, offering technical and scenic trails, coastal rocky shorelines, and some of Sweden’s finest oak pastures around Gränsö Castle. Choose between 8 km and 15 km on well-marked courses, or let the children take part in Gränsö Kids Trail (up to age 12). The race offers both timed participation and Fun Run without timing, and encourages an enjoyable experience in nature—why not combine it with a spa visit at Gränsö Castle? Welcome to experience the Västervik archipelago at its best.
course_highlights: Coastal rocky shorelines and the cliffs of Skanvik along the course
Trails through sparse pine forest and valuable oak pastures, with technically varied sections
The 15 km course has a bonus loop on Ekholmen; the 8 km and 15 km courses join at the Kroken aid station
additional: The event center opens at 09:00 at Gränsö Castle. Start times: Gränsö Kids Trail 10:15, 8 km 11:00, 15 km 11:15. The first finishers are expected at approximately 11:35, and the finish closes at 13:45. Courses are marked with hanging red-and-white tape and signs; parts of the course follow existing hiking trails. Surface: mainly trails/hiking paths, with sections of rocky terrain, natural terrain, and short road stretches. Aid stations: one on the 8 km course and two on the 15 km course. All children receive a medal and refreshments after finishing. Registration is online and remains open until one hour before the start. 8 km and 15 km courses; online registration until one hour before the start; aid and hydration stations along the course; timed participation or Fun Run without timing; start times: 11:00 (8 km) and 11:15 (15 km); first finishers at approximately 11:35; finish closes at 13:45; spa option at Gränsö Castle.

description: Discover the magic of running in Svartedalen on a lovely 12 km trail through wilderness-like landscapes. The run takes you along winding forest paths, past mirror-still lakes and over hilly terrain that offers both a challenge and the joy of running. There are several stops along the way to enjoy the views and the special atmosphere of one of western Sweden’s most beloved natural areas. The run ends with a light lunch, a drink and cake at the shelter, creating a wonderful sense of community and an energizing morning for everyone taking part.
course_highlights: Winding forest paths through deep spruce forests
Mirror-still lakes and moss-covered sections
Hilly terrain with mountain-like landscapes
additional: The run is divided into 2–3 pace groups. Meet at the Bottenstugan parking area. After the run, a light lunch, a drink and cake are served at the shelter. Meet at 10:00 at the Bottenstugan parking area. 2–3 pace groups. A light lunch, a drink and cake are included.

description: Falktrailen is a trail race held at Falkenberg Motor Speedway in Falkenberg. The race offers lovely narrow trails and varied terrain suited to both experienced runners and recreational runners. There are several categories for women and men, as well as youth categories and children’s races. The course is mainly on trails, where trail shoes are recommended, but regular running shoes also work well. After the race, refreshments are available for purchase, and prizes are awarded to the top finishers in each category.

location: Garphyttans nationalpark entrance parking area, Lekeberg Municipality, Sweden
price_range: 250 kr för vuxna; 50 kr för deltagare under 18 år
description: Mörkertrail is a unique 10 km trail race run in total darkness in Garphyttan National Park in Lekeberg Municipality. Participants run along a reflective-marked course featuring both technical and easy-running trails, with the light from their headlamps as the only source of illumination. The race offers an atmospheric and challenging experience, with elevation gain and the quiet of the forest as companions. After finishing, participants can enjoy a grilled sausage by the fire. The start and finish are at the car park by the national park entrance, and the race starts at 17:00 on 14 November 2026.
course_highlights: 10 km trail in total darkness, with a headlamp as the only source of light
Reflective-marked course featuring both technical and easy-running trails
Course with elevation gain on the edge of Kilsbergen
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 16:00. A short briefing takes place 10 minutes before the start. No on-site registration. The national park car park has limited spaces, so please carpool. Outdoor toilets are available, but there are no changing facilities. You must bring your own headlamp with a fully charged battery. The course has muddy sections and a water station halfway. Race bibs can be collected from 16:00; sausage and a drink are included after the finish. Places are limited, and there is no on-site registration.

We’ll fill the stadium with runners of all ages and welcome you whether you’re an elite runner or a recreational runner. Together with the spectators, sponsors and activities, we’ll make it an unforgettable stadium experience.

Mustaschmilen in Malmö has three distances: 5 km, 10 km and 1 km for children. The two longer races will be run on a loop course filled with upbeat music and an encouraging commentator along the 1,000-metre course.

name: Fakkeltoget Løvstakken
description: The Løvstakken Torchlight Procession is an enjoyable mountain hike for all ages, held every year in support of the Norwegian Cancer Society. No particular level of fitness is required, and you’re welcome to come without children. The hike up Løvstakken begins as darkness falls and the city lights become visible. At the summit, there’s a medal ceremony, a barbecue and other fun activities, before everyone lights their torches for the group hike back down. Pizza, mulled wine and gingerbread are served at the finish.

Results are available immediately after the finish, and free parking is available.

description: Hamarkarusellen Vinter is the winter edition of Hamarkarusellen. Everyone is welcome, whatever their ambitions: walkers (untimed or timed), runners (untimed or timed), those who want to compete with themselves or beat the neighbour, and active super-runners.

name: Østmarka Trail Challenge
description: Østmarka Trail Challenge organizes tough and challenging trail races in Østmarka. This race, taking place on Saturday, August 23, 2025, is not for the faint-hearted, as it features 37 km of technically demanding terrain and nearly 1,000 metres of elevation gain. Participants will experience trails that cross rough, rocky ground, and after many hours of preparation, they will feel ready for this challenge.

name: Hodelyktløpet Østmarka
description: Østmarka Trail Challenge – The Headlamp Race is a technically demanding trail race of approximately 12 km, running mainly on blue- and red-marked trails in Østmarka. The route will be marked all the way by the organizers, but there is definitely a chance of taking a wrong turn, so it is important to pay close attention, especially at trail junctions. A good headlamp is essential! From the start at Skullerud, we follow the Flyktningeruta up to Rundvann, before taking the technically challenging blue trail downhill.

name: Hodelyktløpet i Østmarka
description: The Headlamp Run in Østmarka is a technically demanding trail race of approximately 12 km, mainly following blue- and red-marked trails in Østmarka. The race takes place in the evening, starting at 19:30, and a good headlamp is required to navigate in the dark. Runners face challenging terrain with 400 metres of elevation gain. The race offers a nature experience in beautiful surroundings, with demanding trails. There are no food or drink stations along the route, so runners must bring their own drinks.
course_highlights: Approximately 12 km of technically demanding trail running

400 metres of elevation gain and demanding trails, with a risk of going off course
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Skullerud park between 18:15 and 19:00 on race day. There are good parking options and public transport to the start area. Indoor changing facilities and luggage storage are available. The course is marked throughout, but runners are advised to pay close attention to avoid going off course. There are no food or drink stations during the race, so runners must bring their own drinks. Participation is at your own risk. The start and finish are by the entrance towards Østmarkaporten. Start at 19:30, with space for up to 200 participants.

The event attracts both experienced ultrarunners and beginners who want to test their limits in a supportive and motivating environment. The race is sold out, and prizes include a large achievement medal for those who reach 150 km (men) and 130 km (women).

name: 5 Km Sport Glexe
description: 5 Km Sport Glexe is a certified course offering a fast route along new pedestrian and cycle paths on the way to Gvarv. This race is perfect for both beginners and experienced runners looking to set new personal records.

name: Klubbmesterskap 5k
description: The Club Championship 5K is a running competition that is part of Tjøme Running Club’s events. The courses are officially measured, and the race is run over a distance of 5 km. This championship gives members the opportunity to compete for club championship titles and set club records. The race takes place at the beautiful Grønneset by Ånøya on Wednesday, June 25, with the start from 18:00, and is designed to challenge both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Bergen Cider Marathon
description: Bergen Cider Marathon is a unique race combining running, Bergen and cider for a different kind of marathon experience. The course goes through Fyllingsdalstunnelen, the world’s longest tunnel for pedestrians and cyclists, and continues through beautiful surroundings in Bergen. Half-marathon runners complete one lap, while marathon runners complete two laps and pass through the tunnel four times. After the race, participants are invited to a cider party featuring tastings of different ciders and food inspired by Bergen and Hardanger.

Three laps around Store Lungegårdsvannet in central Bergen
A measured course through beautiful surroundings in Bergen
additional: All participants receive a technical running shirt included in the price. There will be no medal, but a certificate can be printed after the race. Refreshments during the race are non-alcoholic, with non-alcoholic cider, water and squash/energy drink. After the race, a separate cider party will be held at Siderbaren, with tastings of at least seven different ciders and food. It requires a separate ticket and has limited capacity. Registration is for the selected distance, and it is possible to transfer your entry to someone else. Start at 09:00. A technical running shirt is included. Aid stations serve non-alcoholic cider, water and squash or energy drink. The cider party at Siderbaren requires separate registration and has limited capacity. Age limit: 18 years.

The event includes a 5 km distance on a flat route starting from the motorhome parking area at Grevestien and going around Illene National Park and Semslinna. The surface is gravel and asphalt. A children’s race is also held, and no advance registration is required to participate. Race numbers are collected from the race office on race day.

description: i Heiane ODDERØYA OPP is a mountain race held in Kristiansand on November 21, 2026. The race focuses on elevation gain and terrain, and is suitable for runners who want to challenge themselves on hilly ground. Treni offers training guidance tailored specifically to the race, focusing on proper training for both uphill and downhill elevation. The event is a great opportunity for both experienced and motivated runners seeking a demanding and rewarding racing experience in scenic surroundings.

description: Tyn_deg BARNEKARUSELL Odderøya is a children’s fun run held on Odderøya in Kristiansand. The race focuses on giving children a safe and enjoyable running experience without injuries, in an environment adapted to them. It is part of a series that encourages running and activity among children in the local area. The event is well suited to young runners who want to take part in a social and inclusive race.

A children’s race series focused on safety and injury prevention
A fun and inclusive running environment for children
additional: The race is part of a series that emphasizes running without injuries and builds training programs based on the runner’s actual activity. Participants are encouraged to register via affiliated timing systems, but no direct registration link is provided.

The event is open to all ages, with separate prices for under and over 18s, and includes a one-time license. The series continues with several races during the winter months, offering both recreational runners and competitive track and field athletes a great opportunity to compete in a social and inclusive environment.

Previous races have used timing by EQTiming. The listed price information is not specific.

We’ll fill the stadium with runners of all ages and welcome you whether you’re an elite runner or a recreational runner. Together with the spectators, sponsors, and activities, we’ll make it an unforgettable arena experience.

Mustaschmilen in Stockholm has three distances: 5 km, 10 km, and 1 km for children. The two longer races will be run on a loop course filled with upbeat music and an enthusiastic announcer along the 1,000-meter course.

name: Karmøy Marathon
description: Karmøy Marathon wraps up the running season in the fresh West Norwegian air. The marathon course takes you through three towns, along the coastline on both the east and west sides of Karmøy, with the North Sea as your closest neighbour. This year, IL Trio is strongly represented, with participants in both the full and half marathon, including Emil Solli Stafsnes, who is taking part in his first full marathon. Results will be posted on Trio’s Facebook page as they become available.

The courses are nationally certified in cooperation with AIMS & WA, and the start and finish are at Åkrahallen in Åkrehamn. The event offers marathon, half-marathon and 10 km distances, with several drink stations and pacers. There are also activities for children and a social running day ahead of the main event.

Preliminary race information and courses are published on the website, along with information about course previews ahead of the event. Organizer pages and the registration link are collected on the race website.

The race has a long tradition in Kristianstad, and information about this year’s edition is available in news articles and race information on Härlövs IF’s website and the RaceID page.

name: Geiteryggen-løpet
description: Join us for a magical evening run at Geiteryggen Airport on Tuesday, November 28, from 18:00. Maximum 1,000 places! Secure your spot and sign up now. Dress for lovely autumn weather, put on your headlamp, and join us. You’ll run among torches lighting the way through the dark forest and the runway’s colorful spotlights. Geiteryggen Run 2022 was a success, with as many as 700 people registered, and we’re really looking forward to this year’s race.

description: Rambo Mosse Night Trail is a unique trail race through the fascinating natural surroundings of Rambo Mosse Nature Reserve in Mölndal. The race, which is just over 11 km long, takes place at dusk, with headlamps and a course marked with reflectors, offering a special and challenging running experience on forest trails. The start and finish are at Herkulesgården, where participants can enjoy a sauna, showers and warming soup in the clubhouse after the race. The race is limited to 400 participants and includes a medal and awards for the top finishers in the women’s and men’s categories.
course_highlights: Just over 11 km on forest trails marked with reflectors
A gently undulating course featuring a mix of forest, bogs and rocky outcrops

additional: Maximum 400 participants. All participants receive a training hat from Ullmax (value: SEK 149). Aid stations with water and Umara sports drink at approximately 4 km and 8 km, and after the finish. Electronic timing with a split time. After the race, showers, a sauna and warming soup with bread and a drink are available in the clubhouse. Race bibs can be collected the day before or on race day. Recommended equipment includes a headlamp with sufficient battery life and trail shoes with good grip. Parking is limited; public transport is recommended. Start and finish at Herkulesgården. Registration is via RaceID from 1 September and remains open until 25 November or until all 400 places are filled. The entry fee includes refreshments, soup after the finish, a training hat, a medal for all finishers, and access to changing rooms, showers and a sauna.

name: Vinterkarusellen Ålesund - 2. løp

The next race in the 2025/2026 Winter Series is on Saturday, 8 November 2025. The race offers two distances, 5 and 10 km, on officially measured courses heading into Brusdalen, with turnarounds after 2.5 and 5 km. The 5 km distance includes a non-timed recreational class, and there is usually little traffic on Gamle Brusdals veg.

additional: Registration is via EasyRecord (as stated in the invitation). The race information and course maps are available as PDF files on the organiser’s pages (invitation, race information, course). The start list is published separately on the organiser’s website. Historically, the event has had changing facilities, refreshments and prize-giving in Idrottshallen. Historical information and course profile, including the start and finish points around Idrottshallen and Nya torget.

name: Nyårsmilen Halmstad
description: Nyårsmilen in Halmstad is a festive New Year’s race where you can choose between 5 or 10 km on a fast, easy-to-run course along cycle paths in Halmstad. The start and finish are at the athletics track at Halmstad Arena, and the race uses chip timing via the race bib. After the finish, participants are treated to a medal, sparkling drinks, snacks, music and a great atmosphere, whether they run fast or take it easy. The race is open to everyone and is a perfect start to the new running year.
course_highlights: Fast, easy-to-run course along cycle paths
The 10 km race consists of two laps
Start and finish at the athletics track at Halmstad Arena
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 9:00 to 10:10 at Halmstad Arena. Timing is provided by a chip in the race bib, and results are displayed immediately after the finish. Toilets and changing facilities are available at the venue. Valuables can be left in the covered grandstand (unattended). Parking is about 200 metres from the start. Water and Umara sports drink are available after 5 km for 10 km runners. All runners receive a medal; if you decline the medal, SEK 15 is donated to the organisation Aldrig Ensam. Prizes are awarded to the three fastest women and men in each category. Pacing for the 10 km is available on request by email. The race takes place on 31 December 2026, with the start and finish at Halmstad Arena. Provisional start times are 10:30 for 10 km and 10:35 for 5 km. Race bibs can be collected at the arena between 9:00 and 10:10. Chip timing; toilets, changing facilities and parking are available at the arena.

name: Grimstadvatnet Rundt
description: Grimstadvatnet Rundt is part of the Hareid winter series, with race 1 held on a Saturday in November, December, January and February, making 4 races in total. This is a 7.8 km road race, mostly on asphalt, and the course is relatively flat. The first race in the series was held on 5 December 1981, and the 110th race took place in November 2008.

name: Lierløpet
description: Lierløpet is one of Norway’s fastest courses, running along a wide footpath that is popular with runners and recreational exercisers in the Drammen area. The race offers distances of 5 km, 10 km and a half marathon (21 km), and is open to those who want to jog or walk as well as to fit, fast runners. There is also a children’s race, where all participants receive ice cream. Race numbers can be purchased at Lier Station, and the race starts at 12:00.

name: Bjørgene Løpskarusell 4. Løp
description: The athletics group welcomes you to a new running series in Bjørgene on February 4! The snow is gone and the trails in Bjørgene are in good condition. We hope to see you at the starting line!

name: Vinterkarusellen 5. løp
description: The 5th race of Vinterkarusellen was held at Fana Stadium, where the venue was crowded and 515 runners finished the 5 km, while 247 finished the 10 km. Participation increased considerably after the previous winter race, and conditions were good despite brisk winds in some places. Markus Galleberg and Eli Anne Dvergsdal were the fastest in the 5 km, while Andre Lenningsvik and Renate Galleberg won the 10 km. This race is part of Ålesund Vinterkarusell, which consists of 5 races suited to both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Sylvesterloppet Göteborg
description: The Sylvesterloppet in Gothenburg is a spectator-friendly 10 km race held on New Year's Eve, starting and finishing at Heden. The flat course covers two loops through central Gothenburg, including Avenyn, Ullevi, Gårda and the area around Svenska Mässan. The race is suitable for all runners who want to end the year with a fast and festive running experience. Everyone who finishes receives a medal and has a chance to win prizes in a draw.
course_highlights: Flat, two-loop 10 km course through central Gothenburg
Passes Avenyn, Ullevi, Gårda and Svenska Mässan
Spectator-friendly, festive atmosphere, with firefighters cheering runners on at Gårda fire station
additional: Start groups are assigned according to expected finish time: elite, start group 1 and start group 2. The warm-up begins 15 minutes before the start. Race bibs can be collected on 29–30 December and on race day from 09:00 to 11:30 at Exercishuset at Heden. Electronic chip timing using the chip on the race bib is used, and net times are shown in the results. The race starts at 12:00 on 31 December. Registration via MittLopp is available until one hour before the start, unless the race is full.

name: Samnanger Vinterkarusell - 3. løp
description: The Samnanger Winter Series is a social and inclusive running series organised by Samnanger IL Athletics. The races take place at Nesodden, with the start and finish in the same place. Participants can choose between 2 km and 5 km distances. The Winter Series is suitable for all levels, whether you want to compete, set a new personal best, maintain your fitness, or simply enjoy a pleasant run with others. Races are held approximately every other Friday throughout the winter, and participants are encouraged to wear reflective gear because of the dark season.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Nesodden
Choice of 2 km and 5 km distances
The 5 km course is officially measured by the Norwegian Athletics Federation (NFIF)
additional: Races are held approximately every other Friday throughout the winter. The running group is beginner-friendly, free, and open to all levels. Wearing a reflective vest is recommended because of the dark season. Samnanger IL Running Group also offers group training every Monday at 18:10 at Hagabotnane. The schedule lists the start time as 18:30. The Winter Series is free; remember your reflective vest.

name: Vinterkarusellen 5. løp
description: The 5th race in Vinterkarusellen was held at Fana Stadium, where it was crowded, and a total of 515 participants completed the 5 km, while 247 took part in the double distance. Participation has increased sharply since the winter race 3 weeks ago, and the running conditions were good despite brisk winds in exposed areas. Markus Galleberg and Eli Anne Dvergsdal were fastest in the 5 km, while Andre Lenningsvik and Renate Galleberg won the 10 km.

name: Polar Night Marathon
description: The Polar Night Marathon is a spectacular race during the blue hour north of the Arctic Circle. Choose from several distances, from 5 km to a full marathon (42.195 km), and experience the magic of the magnificent Arctic landscape. The race takes place in early January, during the polar night, when the sun does not rise above the horizon.

name: Magni Maraton 106
description: Magni Marathon is a popular marathon that attracts participants from various places. The course is known for its beautiful scenery and varied terrain, offering runners a unique experience. Participants can enjoy both challenging hills and flat stretches, making the race exciting for beginners and experienced runners alike.

name: Eikanger Vintarkarusell 4
description: The second race in the 2025–26 winter series takes place on Saturday 15 November at Eikanger. There will be seven races in total this season, with three before Christmas and four after New Year. The course follows the usual route around Eikangervågen, and registration opens from 14:20.

name: Askløpet
description: Askløpet is a long-standing race organized by Ask Friidrett in beautiful surroundings on Askøy in Vestland. The race brings together both local and visiting runners for a friendly and inclusive competition. It is a great opportunity for both recreational runners and competitive athletes to test their fitness early in the year. The event has a long history, and past results are available for those who want to follow previous performances.

name: Nidaros Vinterkarusell: Løp 2
description: Nidaros Winter Running Series is a winter running series organized by Strindheim IL Friidrett at Ranheimshallen. The races take place indoors and include distances such as 3,000 meters for everyone and 1,000 meters for children. The event is open to both young people and adults. Timing is provided by EQTiming, but times are not accepted for records or annual statistics. The series is part of Strindheim’s tradition of offering inclusive athletics events that bring the community together in Trondheim.
course_highlights: Indoor races at Ranheimshallen
3,000 meters for all participants
1,000 meters for children
additional: Timing is provided by EQTiming, but times are not accepted for records or annual statistics. Registration on the day of the event incurs a fee. The event is part of a series with several races in the winter running series.

Vinterkarusellen 3. løp
description: The 3rd Vinterkarusellen race offers two distances, 5 and 10 km, on accurately measured courses through Brusdalen. The course turns around after 2.5 km and 5 km, then returns to the start/finish. The 5 km distance has a recreational class without timing. There is usually little car traffic on Gamle Brusdals veg on Sundays, but be aware that cars may be in the area.

name: Snøkuten Nordhagarunden
description: Snøkuten Nordhagarunden takes place on October 17, 2023, and covers a distance of 9.5 km. The race is part of the Snøkuten series and gives participants the opportunity to challenge themselves in beautiful surroundings. The course is quite demanding, but takes you through beautiful scenery, and is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. This is a popular event on Veldre Friidrett’s calendar.

name: Åsane løpskarusell 2027
description: Åsane Running Series is a recreational running series with weekly 5 km races that start and finish at IKEA in Åsane. The courses are nationally measured and suitable for all levels, led by experienced coaches. The series has a sociable and inclusive atmosphere, and also offers training sessions for those who want to join the running group. Race bibs are collected in the IKEA garage before the races, and family and individual registration are available.
course_highlights: 5 km course measured and certified by NFIF
Start and finish inside IKEA, at the back facing south
The races are held in the evening, with a 19:00 start
additional: Race bibs are collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45. Race bibs must be worn visibly, and the tags must not be folded or damaged. A new race bib costs 100 kr. The races are held in the evening on selected Thursdays throughout the year. Race bibs are collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45.

name: Vinterkarusellen 6.løp
description: The 6th race of the season in the NECON Winter Series took place on January 20, with 721 participants finishing despite torrential rain. A total of 382 runners completed the 5 km, while 169 finished the double distance. Hector Breivik from Ask was the fastest over 5 km with a time of 18:13, while Miriam Emilie Stensland Donovan from Lerøy won the women’s race in 21:31. The 10 km winners were Magne Knudsen (35:48) and Vanja Flatberg (40:26).

name: 5 Km Sport Glexe
description: Sport 1 Glexe is organizing a 10 km race on October 12 at 11:00! The race starts at MSG car wash, heading toward Gvarv from Bø. The course has been officially measured and is a fast route on new walking and cycling paths. It is easy to run, with an unattended drink station after approximately 3.4 km, 6.6 km, and at the finish. Toilets are available at Circle K, but there are no shower facilities.

name: Bislett Spring 5k
description: Bislett Spring 5K takes place at Bislett Stadium and offers a great opportunity to set a personal best over 5 km. The starting groups are divided by target finish time, and each group has a pacer to help you reach your goal. But remember, you still have to do the running!

description: Hagemanns Hill Mile 2027 is a unique last-man-standing race in Drammen where participants run laps of one English mile (1609 metres) in under 20 minutes. The race starts at 10:00 on 16 January and continues with new starts every 20 minutes. Each lap has approximately 80 metres of elevation gain, and medals are awarded to everyone who completes at least one lap. The start and finish are at Svelvik Sports Association’s clubhouse/football pitch at Solbakken, with the option to rest indoors in the changing rooms between laps.
course_highlights: Run 1609-metre laps with approximately 80 metres of elevation gain per lap
Last-man-standing format with a start every 20 minutes
Start and finish at Svelvik Sports Association’s clubhouse/football pitch at Solbakken
additional: A reflective vest is required when it is dark, but the street is lit, so a headlamp is not mandatory. There is an opportunity to heat food and drinks, and blackcurrant cordial will be available. Buying and selling race bibs is also permitted. A minimum of 50 registrations is required by 16 November 2026 for the race to go ahead. Registration is referred to via the event page.

name: Bergen 3000 Indoor
description: Gneist 3000 Indoor is an indoor 3 km race held at Gneist Arena in Bergen. The race consists of 15 laps on a soft, smooth blue athletics track, and participants may wear running shoes or spikes with blunt pins no longer than 6 mm. To ensure evenly matched heats and a smooth event, start times are assigned based on estimated finishing times, and pacers are planned for several heats. The event also includes a separate children’s race, Gneist 400 Kids, for children aged 6 to 12, covering 400 metres. A café with grandstand seating will be open during the event, and race bibs must be collected no later than one hour before the start.
course_highlights: Indoor 3 km race on a blue athletics track
15 laps on a soft surface at Gneist Arena
Choose between running shoes and spikes with blunt pins (maximum 6 mm)
additional: Race bibs must be collected at Gneist Arena no later than one hour before the start. Athletes must report to the Call Room 10–15 minutes before each heat, where their shoes will be checked. Runners will be allowed onto the track when it is ready for the next heat. Warm-ups must take place outdoors, as there is no space to warm up inside the hall. A café with grandstand seating will be open during the event. Access to the competition area is not permitted without a race bib. Warm-ups take place outdoors. Participants should report to the Call Room 10–15 minutes before their heat. A café and grandstand seating are available. Information for the 2027 date has not been confirmed on the organiser’s website.

name: HOKA Solastranden Halvmaraton
description: HOKA Solastranden Half Marathon offers a unique running experience, with distances of 5 km, 10 km, and 21 km. Half-marathon runners should note that course marshals go home after a target time of 2:40, but timing remains open for up to 3 hours. Pacers are also available for all distances, and aid stations serve both water and sports drinks. The race takes place in a scenic area, with alternative parking options nearby.

name: Gneist 3000 Indoor
description: Gneist 3000 Indoor is an indoor 3 km track race held at Gneist Arena. The race consists of 15 laps on a soft, smooth blue track surface. Participants can choose to run in running shoes or spikes with blunt pins no longer than 6 mm. The race uses eq-timing’s timing system with lap times, and heats are organized according to estimated finish times to ensure evenly matched groups. There is also a separate children’s race, Gneist 400 Kids, for children aged 6 to 12, over 400 metres. The first start is scheduled for 17:00, and a café and seating in the stands will be available during the event.
course_highlights: 3 km indoor track race on a blue athletics track surface
15 laps, timed with lap times via eq-timing
Choice of running shoes or spikes with blunt pins (maximum 6 mm)
additional: Race numbers must be collected at Gneist Arena no later than 1 hour before the start. Callroom check-in is 10–15 minutes before each heat, with shoes checked. Runners are let into the hall when it is ready for the next heat. Warm-ups must take place outdoors, as there is no space to warm up inside the hall. Each heat has approximately 15–20 participants, and pacemakers are planned for as many heats as possible. Warm-ups must take place outdoors, and race numbers must be collected at Gneist Arena no later than one hour before the start. Registration requires an estimated finish time. Gneist 400 Kids, a 400-metre race for children aged 6–12, will also be held.

name: Sørlandstesten 5
description: Sørlandstesten is an accessible fun run for everyone looking for a positive running experience, whatever their level of ambition. Whether you’re training for a bigger goal, want to experience the excitement of competition, or simply want a social and active day, this is the race for you! There’s room for both beginners and experienced runners. The start and finish are on the opposite side of the road from Gumpens Auto, along Setesdalsveien in Kristiansand. Participants follow a flat, fast route up Setesdalsveien to Strai, then turn around and run back.

name: Vinterkarusellen Løp 4
description: Vinterkarusellen is an annual running series featuring several distances, with courses officially measured and certified. This means that times achieved in the races will be recognized in statistics for both 5 km and 10 km. Participants have the opportunity to set personal records that will be recognized forever. The series has a rich history dating back to the mid-1980s, and since winter 2023, Ålesundløpene has once again been the organizer.

name: Hamarkarusellen Vinter Løp 4
description: Hamarkarusellen Winter is the winter edition of the new Hamarkarusellen. All races follow the same 5-kilometer course along illuminated walking and cycling paths in the Prestrud area of Hamar. Everyone is welcome, whatever their ambitions—whether you walk or run, with or without a time. There is no registration at the start, and the race offers an excellent opportunity to test your fitness, with 6 races during the winter.

name: Sandsjöbacka Trail 180
description: Sandsjöbacka Trail is one of western Sweden’s most exciting and challenging winter trail races, offering distances of 30k, 60k, 90k and 180k. The races feature varied terrain, from easy-to-run trails to technical trail running in a magical setting. Whether you’re an ultrarunner or a recreational runner, there’s a challenge to suit you. Welcome to experience the community, challenge and joy of Sandsjöbacka!
course_highlights: Terrain ranging from easy-to-run trails to technical trail running
Elevation gain from approx. 1,000 m (30k) up to approx. 5,000 m (180k)
Magical winter scenery in the Gothenburg area
additional: The 180k race is an out-and-back race starting in Skatås and turning around at Tjolöholm. The Friday start time can be chosen freely between 11:00 and 20:00, but all 90k and 180k runners must start together at 06:00 on Saturday morning. Drop bags and a place to rest are available in Tjolöholm. Self-support applies on the Skatås–Tjolöholm section, according to Fastest Known Time rules. A headlamp is recommended for dark sections. There are time limits and several aid stations with closing times along the courses. The event is known for its scenic course and challenging terrain, making it a popular choice for trail runners in the region.

name: Becksvart
description: Becksvart is a unique night race held in total darkness, with headlamps and reflectors as the only guides. Choose between two challenging and varied courses of 6 km or 12 km, taking you over logs and rocks, along narrow trails and across rocky outcrops around Gunnebo Castle, Kallebäck and Lackarebäcksfjället. The races are a perfect Friday activity focused on adventure and experience, with an AfterRun featuring food, drinks and music waiting in the finish area. There is also a secret contest within the race for anyone looking for an extra challenge.
course_highlights: Run in the dark, with headlamps and reflectors as the only guides
The course follows unique trails around Norra Långevattnet, Lackarebäcksfjället and Kallebäck
Gothenburg’s most legendary hill—Hobo Hill, with 80 metres of elevation gain over approximately 200 metres (12 km course)
additional: Start and finish at Gunnebo Castle & Gardens. The courses are marked with reflectors attached to clothespins and trail markers. Bibs and timing chips can be collected at Nordic Wellness Krokslätt the day before and on race day. Unsupervised bag drop is available. There is one water station halfway around the course, and refreshments are provided after the finish. Medical staff will be on site. Bus 754 goes to Gunnebo Park. Parking is available below the castle, but not at the start/finish. AfterRun with food, drinks and music takes place in the finish area. Trail shoes with a substantial sole are recommended; a headlamp is mandatory. A headlamp is strongly recommended and described as mandatory on the race information page; trail shoes are recommended. There is a water station approximately halfway around the course. AfterRun with music, food and drinks awaits after the finish.

name: Vinterkarusellen Sørlandet
description: Vinterkarusellen Sørlandet is an exciting running race held in Kristiansand. The race covers a distance of 10 kilometres and gives participants the opportunity to experience the beautiful winter landscape of Sørlandet. It is perfect for both recreational and experienced runners who want to challenge themselves in a wintry setting.

name: Bergen Vintermaraton
description: Bergen Winter Marathon will be held for the 5th time on Saturday, January 18, 2025. The start and finish area will be at Fana Stadium. The course is an out-and-back route on paved roads that are either completely free of cars or have very little traffic, and a large part of the route follows a disused railway line through idyllic rural surroundings. Each loop is exactly one half marathon, and the same loop is run twice for the full marathon. The half marathon is one loop, while the marathon is two loops.

The race features a certified 5 km course that starts north of Londalskrysset, runs to Gamle Haukeland station and returns along the same route, with the finish inside the sports ground. The event is part of a race series with several dates throughout the winter and early spring. It is a popular recreational race with a friendly atmosphere and enthusiastic participants of all ages.

Finish inside Espeland sports ground

Results are published at www.eqtiming.no. The race takes place at Espeland sports ground in Arna. Registration is stated to be via EQ Timing.

name: Søknad Frikarusellen løp nr.4 2027
description: The Frikarusellen is a winter running series organized by Idrettslaget Fri in Arna, with six races throughout the winter and spring. The course is certified as 5 km and runs mainly along a pedestrian and cycle path between Espeland and Gamle Haukeland station, with the start and finish at Espeland sports grounds. The race is suitable for both young people and adults, with separate prices for members and age groups. It is a social and inclusive running series that encourages people to enjoy running together through the winter months.

The course runs mostly along a pedestrian and cycle path or a lightly trafficked road
Start and finish at Espeland sports grounds
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Espelandshallen on race day between 18:00 and 18:55. Registration is open until 18:55 on race day. A license fee is added for participants over 13 years old who do not have an annual license. A fee of 50 kr applies if participants who registered for all the races forget their race number. Results are published at www.eqtiming.no.

description: Winterrun Oslo 2027 is the big winter running festival, taking place on Saturday, 30 January at Rådhusplassen in Oslo. The race offers a unique atmosphere, with fire baskets, torches and music along the course, as thousands of participants gather for a magical running experience through Oslo’s streets. All participants receive a medal and Vitamin Well at the finish, and great prizes are drawn after the race. This is a feel-good race for anyone who wants to test their fitness or simply have fun in the winter cold.

Start and finish at the beautiful Rådhusplassen
A unique atmosphere with music and marshals providing an extra boost
additional: Race bibs are distributed a few days before the race in the city, but can also be collected in the start area on race day. Bag storage is outdoors and requires a luggage tag. There is a dedicated women’s tent for warming up and changing. Public transport to the start area is recommended due to limited parking. Race bibs can be transferred for a fee of NOK 150 via My Page. The race takes place on winter surfaces. Costumes are encouraged, and prizes are awarded for eye-catching outfits. All participants receive a medal and Vitamin Well at the finish.

name: Götas ungdomsspel
location: Eva Lisa Holtz Arena, Karlstad, Sweden
price_range: 110–120 kr per gren; efteranmälan i mån av plats mot dubbel avgift
description: Götas Youth Indoor Games is an athletics competition for young people, held at the modern Eva Lisa Holtz Arena in Karlstad. The event provides a welcoming and supportive environment for young athletes to compete and develop in various athletics disciplines. The arena is a multifunctional indoor facility with seating for 1,700 spectators, creating a great atmosphere for both participants and spectators. The event is organised by IF Göta Karlstad, one of Sweden’s most successful athletics clubs, and offers a safe and inspiring competition environment.
course_highlights: The competition is held indoors at Eva Lisa Holtz Arena, a modern venue with seating for 1,700 spectators
Multifunctional facility for both competitions and training
Organised by IF Göta Karlstad, a club with a long tradition and a strong record in athletics
additional: The competition takes place at Eva Lisa Holtz Arena, which opened in 2022 and is a modern indoor venue for athletics and physical training. The multifunctional arena is also used for meetings and training courses. IF Göta Karlstad covers the entry fees for a maximum of three events per competition for its members. Entries for children and young people under 14 should be sent to the relevant group email address, or to tavlingsanmalan@ifgota.se if no group email address is available. Enter by 24 January via EasyRecord or gus@ifgota.se. Participants compete in their age category or the senior category.

name: EcoTrail Stockholm Winter
location: Stora Skuggan, Norra Djurgården, Stockholm, Sweden
description: EcoTrail Stockholm Winter is a winter adventure for runners who love nature even when the temperature drops. The race takes place in beautiful Norra Djurgården, starting and finishing at Stora Skuggan. Choose from three distances on snowy trails and enjoy a unique winter medal at the finish. After the race, warm up at the after-run with a hot drink and refreshments alongside other runners.
course_highlights: Rolling snowy trails in Norra Djurgården
Aid stations at 4 km on the 6 km and 12 km courses
Start and finish at Stora Skuggan, easily accessible by metro and bus
additional: Everyone who finishes receives a unique winter medal. Aid stations are located at 4 km on the 6 km and 12 km courses. The start and finish are at Stora Skuggan, close to the metro and bus. After the race, a warming after-run with a hot drink and refreshments is available. Registration is through the partner EQ Timing and is binding, with no refunds. Refund protection can be purchased as an add-on through Startklar. Start and finish at Stora Skuggan. Registration is open until 29 January 2027.

description: Winter Run Stockholm is an atmospheric winter race taking place at Skansen and Djurgården on January 31, 2027. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km on a course that combines historic surroundings with beautiful winter scenery, illuminated by fire performers, torches and flares. The race also includes a children’s race for ages 7–11, making it an experience for the whole family. The event is organized by Marathongruppen together with the athletics clubs Hässelby SK and Spårvägens FK, and any surplus goes back to sport.
course_highlights: 5 km course with 57% paved surface and 43% gravel
Just over 1 km through Skansen’s historic surroundings, with the rest around Djurgården
The course is illuminated by flares, fire baskets and a fire show
additional: Children’s race: 1.3 km for ages 7–11. Minimum age: 13 for 5 km (11 when accompanied by a parent or guardian) and 15 for 10 km (13 when accompanied by a parent or guardian). Skansen is a dog-free zone. The course is sanctioned by the Swedish Athletics Association and officially measured by an approved course measurer. There is a risk of ice on the course, so shoes suitable for winter conditions are recommended. Skansen opens to runners at 14:30. Start times: children’s race 16:30, 5 km 17:00, 10 km 18:00. There is also a children’s race for ages 7–11. Any surplus goes back to sport.

name: Necon Vinterkarusellen Bergen - løp 5
description: The Necon Winter Series in Bergen is a winter running series with eight races, where participants can choose between 5 or 10 km. The races start and finish at Fana Stadium, with a start time of 18:45. The series runs on several Mondays from October to April and offers discounts for members of IL Gneist. Registration is individual via EQ-timing, and members of the athletics groups who pay a training fee may participate for free.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km races
Start and finish at Fana Stadium
Evening races starting at 18:45
additional: Discounts are available for IL Gneist members, with different codes for free or reduced entry fees. An annual licence is required for participants over 13 and can be selected during registration. Registration is individual via EQ-timing. Participants are responsible for using the correct discount code and paying the correct fee. The series takes place on several Mondays during the winter half of the year. A licence fee of 50 kr may be added if you do not have an annual licence.

name: Necon Vinterkarusell 26-27 løp 5 (1. jan)
description: Necon Vinterkarusell is a winter race series consisting of 8 races held on Mondays throughout the winter, with the start and finish at Fana Stadion in Bergen. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km distances. The races start at 18:45, and discounts are available for IL Gneist members. Registration is individual through EQ-timing, with options for both annual-license holders and those without a license.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Fana Stadion
Choice of 5 km and 10 km distances
Evening races starting at 18:45
additional: Discounts for IL Gneist members: free for athletics members who pay the main club membership fee and training fee (code Gneist00), 50% off for Gneist trim members (code Gneist50), and 25% off for other Gneist members (code Gneist25). The annual license must be selected during registration, and a license fee of 50 kr applies to those without a license. Registration is individual through EQ-timing. Registration is individual through EQ Timing. The annual license costs 50 kr if it has not already been paid.

name: Bjørgene løpskarusell - 5. løp
description: Bjørgene Running Series is a long-standing series of races organized by the Athletics Group of Torvastad Sports Club. The 2026/2027 season will be the 19th in the series, with races held on the first Tuesday of each month from October to March. The races take place in the scenic surroundings of Bjørgene, Karmøy, and attract many local runners of all ages. The start is usually at 19:00, and the atmosphere is social and inclusive, with biscuits, squash and fruit served after the race.
course_highlights: Races in the scenic surroundings of Bjørgene, Karmøy
Held on the first Tuesday of each month from October to March
Race numbers can be collected from 18:00, with the start at 19:00
additional: Race numbers can be collected from 18:00. Biscuits, squash and fruit are served to participants after the race. The running series relies on voluntary efforts by coaches, team leaders and parents to take place.

name: Samnanger Vinterkarusell - 4. løp
description: Samnanger Winter Series is an inclusive running series organized by Samnanger IL Running Group, held approximately every other Friday at Nesodden. Participants can choose between 2 km and 5 km courses, with the 5 km course officially measured by NFIF. The races are suitable for all levels, from beginners to experienced runners, and focus on competition, training, and socializing. The event takes place in the evening during the winter darkness, and participants are encouraged to wear reflective vests for safety. Samnanger IL Running Group also offers group training sessions and other running events throughout the year.
course_highlights: Run at Nesodden, with the start and finish in the same place
Choose between 2 km and 5 km courses; the 5 km course is officially measured by NFIF
Races are held approximately every other Friday in the evening during the winter darkness
additional: The running group is informal, free, and open to all levels. Group training sessions are held every Monday at 18:10 in Hagabotnane. Participants are encouraged to wear reflective vests because of the darkness. The races are social and inclusive, with a focus on the joy of running and community. Reflective vests are recommended.

description: Grimstadvatnet Rundt is a 7.8 km road race that is part of the Hareid Winter Series, which consists of four races held on the first Saturday in November, December, January and February. The course is mostly on asphalt and relatively flat, making the race accessible to many runners. The first race in the series was held in 1981, and prizes are awarded after the final race in February to participants who have taken part in at least three of the four races. The event is a cherished tradition and brings together runners of all ages at the Hareid clubhouse.
course_highlights: 7.8 km road race
The course is mostly on asphalt
Relatively flat course
additional: Registration takes place at the Hareid clubhouse from 13:00 on race day. Changing facilities are available at the clubhouse. A one-time licence from the Norwegian Athletics Federation is required for races outside a track if you do not have an annual licence. Prizes are awarded after the four-race series, using a points system based on the three best races, with bonus points for participating in all four. The race starts at 14:00, with registration from 13:00 at the Hareid clubhouse. Changing rooms are available at the clubhouse. Overall prizes are awarded after the fourth race; participants must complete at least three of the four races to qualify for a prize.

description: Winterrun Bergen is Bergen city centre’s big winter running festival, taking place on Saturday, 6 February 2027. The race offers a unique atmosphere with fire baskets, torches and music along the course, and participants can choose between the 5 km and 10 km distances. All participants receive a medal and a drink at the finish, and the race is known for its great atmosphere and excellent prizes. Race numbers can be collected in advance at Løplabbet Bergen or in the start area on race day.
course_highlights: Run through Bergen city centre in an atmospheric winter setting
Fire baskets, torches and music along the course
Everyone receives a medal and Vitamin Well at the finish
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Løplabbet Bergen, Strandkaien 6, from 4 to 6 February, 10:00–19:00, or in the start area from 2 hours before the start. There will be approximately 45 seconds between each start group, with pacers from 4:00 to 6:30 min/km. Outdoor baggage storage is available; bring your own baggage tag. There are no shower or changing facilities in the start and finish area. Public transport is recommended due to limited parking. Start time: 18:00. Race numbers can be collected at Løplabbet Bergen at Strandkaien 6 or in the start area. Participants are encouraged to wear luminous costumes.

name: DGI Nordjysk Trail Cup 2026/2027 - Hammer Bakker Trail
BTR Winter 12 km
location: Öströö Fårfarm, Varberg Municipality, Halland County, Sweden
description: Bocksten TrailRun Winter is a winter trail race offering runners a unique opportunity to experience the Åkulla beech forests in their winter dress. With distances of 5, 12 and 24 km, the race features magical trails and a wonderful atmosphere in beautiful natural surroundings. The start and finish are at Öströö Fårfarm, and the event is characterised by community, commitment and respect for nature. Only 600 exclusive starting places are available, making this an intimate and special experience for trail enthusiasts.
course_highlights: Winter trail in the Åkulla beech forests
Start and finish at Öströö Fårfarm
A magical winter landscape experience
additional: A total of 600 starting places are available: 5 km (150 places), 12 km (300 places) and 24 km (150 places). You must help other runners if needed. The start list is available online. Startklar and Startklar Plus insurance are offered for refunds in case of illness or injury. Traffic rules apply at road crossings. Littering will result in disqualification. For urgent assistance, call 076-8159678 or 112. The race starts at 10:00 from Öströö Fårfarm. There is one refreshment station with energy supplies along the course. The final registration date is 2 February 2027.

name: Vintermossa (Mossaloppet)
description: Vintermossa is a winter edition of Mossarun, a trail race featuring a challenging, technical 21 km loop with over 600 metres of elevation gain. The race is self-supported and unstaffed, so participants navigate using a GPX file, with no trail markings. A large fire is kept burning throughout the event to warm up cold runners, and participants can grill their own food. Skis are allowed if there is enough snow, making it possible to combine running and skiing on the loop.
course_highlights: 21 km loop with 600+ metres of elevation gain
Technical, hilly terrain with high-quality trails
Unstaffed race with self-navigation using a GPX file
additional: The race is unsupported, with no timing or checkpoints. There is no cut-off time. Mandatory equipment includes an emergency blanket and a headlamp. A large fire is kept burning throughout the event for participants to warm themselves between laps. Participants can choose to run one or more laps. Skis are allowed when there is snow. Participants are encouraged to Swish any amount they wish to War Child or another organisation of their choice. An external race calendar lists the distance as 241.4 km; this information is not confirmed on Mossarun’s results page.

name: Sormlands Winter Trail
location: Nävekvarns IP, Nävekvarn, Nyköping Municipality, Sweden
description: Sörmlands Winter Trail is a winter race offering three distances: 43 km, 22 km and 10 km, all starting and finishing at Nävekvarns IP in Nävekvarn. The routes pass through varied terrain, including forest trails, hilly landscapes and scenic coastal sections, providing a challenging and picturesque experience. The race uses electronic timing and has several aid stations with food and drinks along the course. After the finish, all participants are served a hot meal and non-alcoholic recovery beer. Safety is a priority, with mandatory equipment and access to showers and changing rooms at the start.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with forest trails, hilly slopes and coastal paths
Several aid stations with food, hot drinks and Umara Energy
Electronic chip timing and clear cut-off times for each distance
additional: Start times: 43 km at 09:00, 22 km at 10:00, 10 km at 11:00. Maximum cut-off times: 8 hours for 43 km, 5 hours for 22 km, 2 hours for 10 km. Mandatory equipment includes, among other things, a mobile phone, windproof jacket, thermal base layer, hat, gloves, water bottle (at least 500 ml), whistle, emergency blanket and headlamp when running in the dark. Showers, changing rooms and toilets are available at Nävekvarns IP. Parking is available for a fee at the start/finish area. After the race, runners are served a hot meal and non-alcoholic Mineral Brewing Recovery Lager. The distances are 10, 22 and 43 km. Race numbers can be collected at the start area at Nävekvarns IP. Aid stations offer food and hot drinks, and a hot meal is served at the finish. Mandatory equipment includes, among other things, a charged phone, wind jacket, water and trail shoes with good grip. Parking is available for a small fee.

name: Snøkuten - Glestadrunden
description: Snøkuten is a traditional series of running races held in Veldre, starting from Kirkekretsen School in Byflaten. The races cover varying distances, including the 9.5 km Nordhagarunden. The event is social and includes both competitive classes and the option to participate without timing. Prizes are awarded to everyone who completes at least four of the six races in the season.
course_highlights: Start from Kirkekretsen School in Byflaten
Nordhagarunden, one of the race routes, is 9.5 km
Both timed and untimed participation options
additional: Untimed start at 17:00; competitive class start at 18:30. A prize is awarded to everyone who completes 4 of the 6 races in the season.

name: Åsane løpskarusell 2027 | Løp 2
description: Åsane Running Series is a recreational running series with weekly 5 km races that start and finish on the south side of the IKEA Åsane building. The course is nationally measured and suitable for all levels, with an inclusive atmosphere and qualified coaches. The series is organized by I.L. Norna-Salhus and has a long tradition of focusing on community and the joy of running. Race bibs are collected in the IKEA garage before the race, and participants can take part in individual races or the entire series.
course_highlights: 5 km course measured and certified by NFIF
Start and finish on the south side of IKEA Åsane
The course is nationally measured, with certification valid until 31.12.2026
additional: Race bibs are collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45. Race bibs must be worn visibly and must not be folded or damaged. A replacement race bib costs 100 kr. The race is organized by I.L. Norna-Salhus. Participants can take part in individual races or the entire series. Training sessions and races are suitable for all levels and led by qualified coaches. Race bibs are collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45.

name: Åsane Løpskarusell 2027 Løp 2
description: Åsane Running Series is a recreational running series featuring weekly 5 km races in Åsane, starting and finishing at IKEA. The course is nationally certified and suitable for all levels, led by experienced coaches. The series has a friendly and inclusive atmosphere and also offers training sessions for those who would like to join the running group. Race numbers are collected at the venue before the race, and participants can enter individual races or the entire series.
course_highlights: 5 km nationally certified, officially measured course
Start and finish inside IKEA, at the rear facing south
The course was measured by a certified course measurer on 19.11.2022
additional: Race numbers are collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45. Race numbers must be worn visibly and must not be folded or damaged. A replacement race number costs 100 kr. The race is organized by I.L. Norna-Salhus. Participants can enter individual races or the entire series. The race takes place on Thursday evenings. Race numbers are collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45.

name: Bislett Indoor Marathon 12 - 14 februar 2027
distance_verbose: 50 km, Maraton, Halvmaraton, 10 km, 5 km, 3000 meter
description: Bislett Indoor Marathon 2027 takes place from 12–14 February on the heated indoor track beneath the stands at Bislett Stadium in Oslo. The event offers distances from 3 km to 50 km, all on an AIMS-certified course measuring 546.5 metres per lap. Held indoors, the event provides stable conditions without wind, ice or rain. It takes place at a historic venue that has been in use since 1922 and hosted the 1952 Olympic Games. This is a unique opportunity to run long distances during winter in a comfortable environment.
course_highlights: Heated indoor running track measuring 546.5 metres per lap
The course is AIMS-certified, with the finish at the entrance to the track
Historic venue in use since 1922 and an Olympic venue in 1952
additional: All distances are run on the same indoor lap. Time limits vary by distance; for example, 5 hours for the marathon and 50 km. The marathon and 50 km start together. The number of available places is updated daily. The event takes place at Bislett Stadium, known for the Bislett Games and as a historic Olympic venue. All finishers receive a medal. Enter via the Training Entrance at Sofies gate 38. An NFIF one-time licence must be purchased if required.

name: AKVA Robust-løpet 2027
organizer: Robust Trening og Fysioterapi og Undheim IL
description: AKVA Robust-løpet 2027 is a city-centre race in Bryne offering several distances, including 5 km, 10 km in two waves, a half marathon, a relay, a children’s race and a wheelchair race. The event takes place on 13 February, with most distances starting and finishing at Bryne torg. The children’s race is an informal, untimed 800-metre run for children up to 12 years old. Facilities include toilets, changing rooms and bag drop, and good parking and transport options are available in the area.
course_highlights: City-centre race starting and finishing at Bryne torg
10 km race split into two waves based on expected finish time
Relay with 4 legs of 2.5 km each
additional: Race numbers can be collected on race day, no later than 30 minutes before the start. Parking is recommended at Bryne Torg, Time rådhus and Kiwi. Facilities include toilets, changing rooms and bag drop. Children must register for the children’s race, but there is no timing. Den Robuste is a separate registration option that includes the 5 km, 10 km and half marathon. The wheelchair race is approximately 200 metres, but the distance is somewhat uncertain. The children’s race is for children aged 0–12 and is untimed. The 10 km starts in Storgata and finishes at Bryne torg. Registration is through the organiser.
