description: Modine Söderköping City Race is a festive fun run taking place on June 22, 2027, with the start and finish in Brunnsparken in Söderköping. Participants can walk, jog, or run 5 kilometers through the town’s beautiful surroundings along the Storån River and Göta Canal. The race features music, performances, and plenty of encouragement along the course, creating a wonderful atmosphere for runners and spectators alike. After crossing the finish line, all participants are treated to a hearty summer plate by ICA Supermarket. This annual running celebration is organized by Norrköpings Löparklubb and attracts many participants and spectators.
course_highlights: 5 kilometers through Söderköping, starting and finishing in Brunnsparken
The course consists of three laps: the first along the Storån River and Göta Canal, the second through central Söderköping, and the third around Brunnsparken and the residential neighborhood
Music and performances along the entire course create a festive atmosphere
additional: Race bibs can be collected at ICA Supermarket Söderköping on Monday, June 21, from 12:00 to 18:00, or on race day in Brunnsparken from 15:00 to 18:30. The top flap of the race bib is the timing chip. After crossing the finish line, all participants are treated to a hearty summer plate by ICA Supermarket, served on the grass. On-site late registration is available at ICA Supermarket on June 21 from 12:00 to 18:00 and on race day from 15:00 to 18:30. Only Swish is accepted for on-site late registration. The 2027 race takes place on Tuesday, June 22, with a 19:00 start. All participants receive a medal. Race bibs can be collected at ICA Supermarket Söderköping or on race day in Brunnsparken. Late registration costs an additional 50 kronor.

name: Karlstad Stadslopp

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Ordinarie pris fram till sista anmälningsdag

description: Karlstad Stadslopp is a community celebration and recreational race featuring a fast, scenic 10 km course through the most central parts of Karlstad. The race is marked by a sense of community and the joy of running, with many spectator spots along the course. In addition to the main race, there is also the Minilopp for children aged 7–12 and the Miniminilopp for the youngest children. Karlstad Stadslopp is a traditional summer event that brings together over 3,000 runners and is part of SM-veckan.
course_highlights: Certified 10 km course through central Karlstad
Start on Tingvallabron at 18:35
Many spectator spots where runners pass several times
additional: Seeding for start corrals is based on the estimated running time provided at registration. Team competition for the 10 km, with 5–6 people per team; the five fastest times count. Bib pickup and late registration take place in Museiparken on race day. Concert with Dotter at Sandgrund after the finish. Gift cards are available to purchase as gifts. There is also the Karlstad Minilopp for children aged 7–12 and the Miniminilopp for children aged 0–6.

name: St Olavsloppet
organizer: St Olavsgruppens Ideella förening i Sverige och St Olavsloppet A/S i Norge
description: St Olavsloppet is a unique three-day relay race stretching from Trondheim in Norway to Östersund in Sweden. The race offers two main distance options, StOlav 340 and StOlav 210, with teams running timed daily stages and using GPS tracking. It is a social and challenging competition for teams in various categories, including open teams, corporate teams and club teams. There are drink stations and timed changeovers along the route, and the event is characterised by a great atmosphere and teamwork among participants.
course_highlights: Three-day relay from Trondheim to Östersund
Drink stations approximately every four kilometres and at changeovers
GPS tracking with a relay baton for each team
additional: Start groups are based on the team’s running speed, with seeding by the race management. Race bibs must be worn clearly visible on the chest and back, without being folded; otherwise, a time penalty will be added. Changeovers are permitted only at regular and extra changeover points, with timing at regular changeover points. GPS transmitters are attached to the relay baton, which is handed over at changeovers. Teams may hand out their own drinks, but not from moving vehicles. Discounts are available when multiple teams from the same association or company register. Teams can take part in one, two or three daily stages. Categories include, among others, open class, corporate teams, women’s teams and club teams.

name: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt 5. løp
description: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt is an annual recreational race organized by Osterøy IL/Athletics, with a 4.4 km course through the scenic surroundings of Valestrandsmarka. The race has a long tradition and is part of a race series with several events throughout the year. The start is at Furubakken sports ground, with two start times: one for walkers and one for the main field. Participants can look forward to a friendly and inclusive atmosphere, with prizes, cordial and sveler served after the race. Course records earn a cash prize from HTB.
course_highlights: 4.4 km course around Valestrandsmarka
Start and finish at Furubakken sports ground
Scenic surroundings and varied terrain
additional: There are two start times: 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field. Times in the walking group are recorded only if they are 30 minutes or more. After the race, sveler from Toro and cordial from Saftsuse are served. Course records earn a prize of NOK 3,000 from HTB. The race is part of a series with several races throughout the year, including a Christmas race and a New Year's race. Start for walkers at 18:45 and the main field at 19:00. No race licence required. Course records in regular races are awarded NOK 3,000 from HTB.

name: Preikestolen Backyard Ultra 2027
description: Preikestolen Backyard Ultra 2027 is held at Jørpelands Brug in Jørpelandsvågen. Participants run a fixed 6.7 km loop at the start of every hour, with a maximum of 12 loops, corresponding to approximately 80 km in total. The course offers varied terrain, including asphalt, a pier, gravel road and easy-running trail, and is suitable for ultrarunners looking for a challenging, tactical competition. The event includes a practical briefing before the start, and food and drinks are available in the rest area. The start and finish are at Jørpelands Brug, with good parking and public transport options nearby.
course_highlights: The 6.7 km loop includes asphalt, a pier, gravel road and easy-running trail
Maximum of 12 loops, approximately 80 km in total
Start and finish at Jørpelands Brug, Jørpeland
additional: Bib numbers are collected at the specified location and time. Parking is available by the municipal building on Oldeidevegen in Jørpeland. Bus route 100 stops at the start area. The rest area offers water, squash, cola, sandwiches, fruit, crisps and hot food later on. Toilets and changing facilities are available. A loop starts at the beginning of every hour from 09:00 to 20:00, with the prize-giving at 21:15. The start and finish are at Jørpelands Brug, Sagholmen 4. Parking is available by the municipal building on Oldeidevegen, and bus route 100 stops at Jørpeland Brug. The rest area offers drinks, sandwiches, fruit and crisps, among other things, with hot food later on.

name: Trosa Stadslopp
description: Trosa Stadslopp is a traditional community celebration and running race held every year on the Friday after Midsummer in the beautiful summer town of Trosa. The race offers categories for all ages and ability levels, from young children to elite runners, on a varied course through the town centre and close to the water. Chip timing and several start groups create a welcoming, race-friendly atmosphere for both recreational and competitive runners. Trosa Stadslopp is known for its positive atmosphere, enthusiastic spectators and compact course, creating a unique running experience.
course_highlights: The course runs through summery Trosa, close to the water
Chip timing with two intermediate timing points in the 8.9 km race
Competitive and recreational categories for all ages and ability levels
additional: Race bibs with disposable chips are handed out from 10:00 on race day at Team Sportia Trosa. The cutoff time to reach the lap point in the 8.9 km race is 40 minutes. Start groups are available for elite runners, and runners in categories 1 and 2 can choose their start group. The jogging and Nordic walking events start shortly before the competitive categories. Parking is available, with a voluntary fee supporting youth activities. All runners receive 50 cl of Vitamin Well at the finish of the 8.9 km and 4 km races. Registration is available via the race’s registration portal; late and on-site registration have specific dates and fees.

name: Kristiansund Havmaraton
price_range: 50 kr for barneløpet; 300–500 kr for 6, 12 og 23 km
description: Kristiansund Sea Marathon offers a unique coastal running experience with beautiful sea views. The courses follow coastal trails, quays, rocky shoreline and coastal heath, with waves and sea spray close by. Choose from several distances for the whole family, from a children’s race to 23 km around Kirklandet and Gomalandet. The event combines spectacular scenery with technically challenging courses and good facilities at the start and finish.
course_highlights: Course along coastal trails, quays and rocky shoreline, with sea spray
23 km route around Kirklandet and Gomalandet with great views
Varied terrain including asphalt, gravel and coastal trails
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Norodd’s premises at Atlanten stadium (3rd floor). Changing rooms with showers and toilets are available. Luggage storage is at your own risk. Water and sports drinks are available at aid stations along the course. Free parking is available at several locations near the start/finish. Medical staff will be present. The event has an environmental focus, with rubbish bins at aid stations. GPX files are available for the courses. Start times: children’s race at 10:00, 23 km at 10:30, 12 km at 11:00 and 6 km at 11:30. Age limits: 23 km from age 15, 12 km from age 13 and 6 km from age 11. Changing rooms, showers, toilets and aid stations are available.

name: Ottaløpet
description: Ottaløpet is a local recreational race held in the centre of Otta in Gudbrandsdalen. The event offers 10 km, 5 km, an untimed 5 km recreational run, and a 10 km relay, with the start and finish in the park in central Otta. The event has a friendly atmosphere, with prizes for the top three finishers in the 5 km and 10 km, as well as class winners in the 10 km, and a challenge trophy for the male and female 10 km winners. There is also a children’s race for children aged 1 to 12, as well as a company competition to find the fittest company in Nord-Gudbrandsdalen. Ottaløpet has a long history: it began in 1993 and was revived in 2021 with great local enthusiasm.
course_highlights: The course runs mainly on asphalt and gravel
Start and finish in the park in central Otta
The 10 km runners complete two laps of a 5 km course that includes a tartan running track and a riverside promenade
additional: There is a group warm-up in the park led by instructors from Spenst Otta. The relay can be divided into up to five legs. The children’s race is free, and every child receives a prize. The company competition awards a challenge trophy to the company with the most participants finishing. The course is clearly marked, and marshals ensure safety during the race. The 5 km course is one lap, while the 10 km is run over two laps. The relay can be divided into up to five legs of distances chosen by the team. The children’s race is free, and a group warm-up is offered in the park.

name: Ecotrail Bergen
description: EcoTrail Bergen is an environmentally conscious trail race offering four distances through beautiful scenery with spectacular views of the fjord and city. The courses range from 27 km to 91 km and feature challenging terrain, including trails, boggy sections, mountains and cultural landscapes. The race is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners looking to enjoy a sense of achievement and community in scenic surroundings. The event emphasizes the environment and sustainability, and participants receive, among other things, merino wool race shirts from Devold.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with trails, boggy sections and bare rock
Spectacular views of the fjord, city and cultural landscapes
Cultural heritage sites and historic areas along the course
additional: Aid stations provide water, sports drinks, salty and sweet snacks, but no hot food. Mandatory equipment includes a cup or soft flask, an emergency blanket, a mobile phone and a bank card/ID. There are cut-off times along the way on the longer distances. Bib pickup takes place before the race, including at Intersport at Thon Senter Bergen. The organizer states that the courses have drink and food stations. For the 27 km, a cup or soft flask, mobile phone and bank card or ID card are listed as mandatory equipment.

name: Fjällmaraton Gastronomi
location: Ottsjö and Trillevallen, Åre Municipality, Jämtland County, Sweden
description: Fjällmaraton Gastronomi is a relaxed mountain marathon offering an experience-filled day in the Åre Mountains, with good food and drink served along the classic mountain marathon trails. Participants can choose between two distances, 22 km and 43 km, both following well-marked trails, with starts in Ottsjö and Trillevallen respectively and the finish in Ottsjö. With an open start time, runners and walkers can complete the course without time pressure, making the race an enjoyable experience in a mountain setting. Accommodation near the start and finish is recommended for the best transfer options.
course_highlights: Local food served at aid stations along the course
Well-marked mountain trails with scenic views
Two distances: 22 km and 43 km, starting in Ottsjö and Trillevallen respectively, and finishing in Ottsjö
additional: Entries can be transferred for a fee of 250 kr. Food and drink stations serve local food, and a kåsa (drinking cup) is provided for use at cup-free stations. Bus transfers to the start are available from Ottsjö, Trillevallen and Undersåker, with return transfers after the finish. Electronic chip timing. A safety team is in place to respond quickly to accidents. The number of start places is limited (400 participants). The open start time allows participants to complete the course without time pressure. Those who want to take it easy are advised to start early. The entry fee includes, among other things, food and drink stations and bus transfers.

name: Kustmaran (Kristianopel)
location: Kristianopel, Karlskrona Municipality, Blekinge County, Sweden
description: Kustmaran and Kristianopel Runt is a running festival for the whole family, with distances from 0.9 km to the marathon (42.2 km). The race takes place amid the idyllic summer scenery of Kristianopel and offers opportunities to enjoy running and set personal records. Team Blekinge provides enthusiastic support and cheerful encouragement along the course. Make a day of it with some relaxing time in the picturesque town, which has swimming spots, restaurants and cafés. In 2027, the race will also host the Swedish Veteran Championships in the marathon.
course_highlights: Distances from 0.9 km to 42.2 km, including the marathon and half marathon
Courses through idyllic summer scenery around Kristianopel
Children’s races and Sommarlunken, a 4 km untimed event
additional: Late registration is available on race day from 08:00, on a first-come, first-served basis. Standard registration can be paid for by card or Swish; late registration can be paid for by Swish or cash. Distances have assigned bib number series and colour codes, but late registrants may receive a different colour code. Sommarlunken is an untimed 4 km course with no medal; prizes are awarded by draw. Kristianopel offers swimming spots, restaurants, cafés and accommodation for participants and their companions. The Swedish Veteran Championships in the marathon will be held in conjunction with the race in 2027. Registration opens in January 2027; late registration on race day is available from 08:00, subject to availability. Electronic timing is provided by Racetimer.

name: Kalmar Malkars 21 km
description: Kalmar Malkars 21 km is a half marathon offering a fast, single-lap course through many of Kalmar’s beautiful surroundings. Runners pass, among other places, the Tegelviken allotment area, Stensö fishing harbour, Kalmarsund Park with Kalmar Castle in the foreground, and areas around Ängöleden and Skälby. The race is open to both men and women and is known for many runners setting personal records here. There is also a 5 km fun run, Malkars Femman, open to everyone, whether they walk, run or roll. All finishers receive a medal.
course_highlights: Single-lap course through Kalmar’s beautiful surroundings
Passes Kalmarsund Park with Kalmar Castle in the foreground
Refreshment stations at 5 km, 10 km, 15 km, 18 km and the finish
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Kalmar Malkars Västra, Torsåsgatan, on Friday, June 26, from 15:00 to 17:00 and Saturday, June 27, from 12:00 to 15:00. Late registration is possible until June 25 and then at race-bib collection. Everyone who registers for the 21.1 km race by June 20 receives a shirt with the Kalmar Malkars logo at race-bib collection. ICA MAXI provides a drink, fruit and a piece of chocolate after the race. Timing and prize-giving are provided for the men’s and women’s categories. All finishers receive a medal. For 2026, the start is listed as 15:00. Refreshment stations are located after 5, 10, 15 and 18 km, and at the finish. A shirt is included for half-marathon runners who register by the final ordinary registration date. Prices and practical details for 2027 have not been confirmed.

name: Jordgubbslunken
description: Jordgubbslunken is a popular fun run held every year on the first Saturday after Midsummer in Rudskoga. Participants can choose between 6 km and 10 km on winding village roads through a beautiful historic rural landscape, with gravel and grass surfaces. Children can take part in Minilunken, a 500-metre race. The event welcomes everyone from competitive recreational runners to families looking to enjoy a pleasant walk. All participants receive a litre of strawberries at the finish and have a chance to win great prizes.
course_highlights: 6 km loop on gravel roads
10 km loop on gravel roads and well-mown grass
Beautiful winding village roads through the historic rural landscape
additional: Start and finish at Grunnebacka School. Categories for men, women and children. All participants receive a litre of strawberries at the finish. A generous prize table is offered, and a top prize is drawn using the race number. Start and finish at Grunnebacka School. All finishers receive strawberries and a medal; the top prize is drawn using the race number. Prices shown are from previous events and may change for 2027.

name: Silverleden Ultra 100 Miles
location: Silvergruvan, Hällefors Municipality, Örebro County, Sweden
description: Silverleden Ultra is a challenging ultramarathon in Bergslagen, with several distances ranging from 9 km to 100 miles. The races follow the well-marked Silverleden, a hiking trail with hilly terrain and beautiful views. Silverleden Ultra 100M is known as one of Sweden’s toughest 100-mile races, with a high DNF rate, while the shorter distances offer tough but accessible challenges for different runners. The event includes transport to the start for some distances and nearby accommodation options. The race is marked by a love of running and a strong sense of community in a scenic setting.
course_highlights: Hilly, trail-filled terrain with steep climbs
Fantastic views from the hilltops along the trail
Well-marked hiking trail with bridges over marshes and waterways
additional: Bus transport is included in the entry fee for the 33 km and 100-mile races, departing at 13:00 on Friday for 100M and 11:30 on Saturday for 33K. Children and young people can take part in the 9 km race for free when accompanied by a registered adult. A limited number of caravan and motorhome pitches are available at the start and finish; book by email. To have a name and club/town printed on the race bib, register by 31 May. Silverleden Ultra’s program includes distances of 9 km, 33 km, 64 km and 100 miles. The official website lists the race weekend as 2–3 July 2027, which does not match the stated date of 26 June.

name: Kristianopel Runt 10 km
location: Kristianopel, Karlskrona Municipality, Blekinge County, Sweden
description: Kristianopel Runt is part of the running festival in Kristianopel, organised by Team Blekinge LF. The event offers several distances, from a children’s race to a marathon, with 10 km being a popular distance. The courses pass through idyllic summer scenery, with enthusiastic support and cheers from the race marshals. Participants can combine running with relaxing in picturesque Kristianopel, which offers swimming, restaurants and cafés. This year’s event also includes the Swedish Veterans’ Marathon Championships, adding to the competitive excitement.
course_highlights: Running through idyllic summer scenery on the east coast
Several distances from 0.9 km to 42.2 km, including the 10 km Kristianopel Runt
Courses with colour-coded number series and family-friendly races
additional: Late registration is available on race day from 08:00, on a first-come, first-served basis. Payment for regular registration can be made by card or Swish; late registration can be paid for by Swish or cash. Number series and colour codes are used for the different distances. Kristianopel offers swimming, restaurants, cafés and accommodation for participants and their companions. The organiser’s website lists the 10 km start time as 11:00 and says that electronic timing is provided by Racetimer. It also states that the 2027 race will take place on 3 July, which differs from the date in the race metadata.

name: TrailÖvik
location: Själevad, Örnsköldsvik Municipality, Västernorrland County, Sweden
description: TrailÖvik is a trail race in Själevad with four different courses to suit all levels. Participants can enjoy a challenging running experience in magnificent natural surroundings, with fantastic trails and fairytale views of the World Heritage Site of the High Coast. The course has been praised by both recreational and elite runners for its fun trails, challenging climbs and beautiful views, with no gravel roads or asphalt. The event has a welcoming, family atmosphere while still being professional, and is well worth travelling to experience.
course_highlights: Fantastic trails in magnificent natural surroundings
Fairytale views of the World Heritage Site of the High Coast
Challenging climbs and no asphalt sections
additional: Race bibs must be collected at the arena no later than 30 minutes before the start. On-site registration opens at the arena and closes 30 minutes before each start. The courses are marked with signs and tape, but runners are encouraged to study the map carefully before starting. Printed maps are available at the beginning of Älgstråket, and digital maps can be downloaded to the Avenza Maps app. Spiked shoes are recommended in wet weather due to slippery rock slabs. Safety staff are available at checkpoints and the finish to help with minor injuries and discomfort. Results are posted immediately after finishing at the arena and on the website. It is possible to test-run the courses.

name: Böda Beach Run
location: Böda Sand Beach Resort, Löttorp, Öland, Sweden
description: Böda Beach Run is a challenging and fun race for the whole family, with distances ranging from 500 metres to 10 kilometres. The race takes place on the beautiful, long sandy beach at Böda Sand Beach Resort on Öland, offering a unique and scenic running experience. Everyone who finishes receives a medal as a keepsake. The event is held annually and is part of Böda Sand’s wide range of summer activities and events.
course_highlights: Run on one of Öland’s most beautiful beaches, with almost two miles of white sand
Courses ranging from 500 metres to 10 kilometres
Family-friendly race with a medal for everyone who finishes
additional: The race is part of Böda Sand’s summer programme, with activities for the whole family. There are several distances to choose from, making it accessible to both children and adults. Böda Sand also offers many other sports and leisure activities alongside the event. Everyone who finishes receives a medal. An accommodation offer at Böda Sand has previously been mentioned in the race information.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://www.bodasand.se/evenemang/): 2027-06-30 — "Böda Beach Run — 30 juni 2027" (was estimated 2027-06-23)

name: Jotunheimen Trail Run
description: Jotunheimen Trail Run offers an unforgettable trail running experience in Norway’s stunning high-alpine landscapes. Participants can choose from several distances, including 12K, 16K, 21K, Marathon, and an epic 73K Ultra that loops around Lake Bygdin. The race features challenging elevation gains, flowing mountain trails, and breathtaking panoramic views, all in a friendly and welcoming atmosphere suitable for runners of all levels. The event includes well-organized check-in, aid stations, and post-race activities such as sauna and swimming at Bygdin.
course_highlights: Ultra: 73 km loop around Lake Bygdin with demanding elevation and runnable high-mountain plateau sections
Marathon: 40 km trail with a scenic detour via Skjetning and a final sprint to the finish line in Bygdin
Half Marathon: 17 km trail with a major climb to panoramic ridge views and a fast downhill finish in Beitostølen
additional: Check-in and bib collection at Beito Resort Hotel and Bygdin Høyfjellshotell. Pre-race pasta dinner at Lodge 900 (booking required). Post-race sauna and swimming available at Bygdin. Shuttle buses provided for Ultra and Marathon runners. Award ceremony for top finishers at Bygdin Høyfjellshotell. Social shake-out run and shoe testing with La Sportiva before race day. The race is part of the Norway Trail Series. The program also includes race briefings, meals, shuttle buses, and award ceremonies; some dinners and bus tickets must be booked in advance.

name: Lofoten Skyrace
description: HOKA Lofoten Skyrace is a spectacular trail race held in Svolvær, with three distances: 15 km, 32 km and 42 km. The courses offer varied, technical terrain, panoramic views, challenging ridges and experiences in nature whatever the weather. The race takes place over two days, with the marathon distance on 2 July and the shorter distances on 3 July 2027. A dedicated SkyCrew helps ensure a great race experience and safety along the way. Participants must be self-sufficient with drinks and nutrition, and must carry the mandatory equipment.
course_highlights: 42 km with approximately 2,000 metres of elevation gain over Matmora, Isvatnryggen and Tjeldbergtinden
Technical, varied terrain with panoramic views and challenging ridges
Natural and staffed drink stations along the way on all distances
additional: Registration opens on 15 September 2026 at 12:00, with a queue system to ensure fair allocation. Bib collection takes place at Sport1 in Svolvær in the days before the race. A HOKA shake-out run and Kids race are also held beforehand. Bus transport to the marathon start is available. Runners must bring a fully charged mobile phone, drinks and nutrition, and mandatory equipment may be checked before the start. Registration for 2027 opens on 15 September 2026 at 12:00. Participants in the 42 km race must be at least 18 years old and must provide their own drinks and nutrition. Bus transport to the start can be selected during registration, and the courses may be changed at short notice due to weather or other unforeseen circumstances.

name: Byrundan
location: Unos park, Gamleby, Västervik Municipality, Sweden
description: Byrundan is a running race held in Gamleby, starting and finishing in Unos Park. The race offers distances for all ages, from children to adults, on a beautiful summer course through Gamleby. There are several categories and distances, including children’s and youth races, as well as a joint start for the 4 km and 8 km races. All participants receive a medal after finishing, and prizes are awarded to the top finishers in each category, along with sprint prizes in the 4 km and 8 km races. Byrundan is part of TOUR DE RUN and is organised by Gamleby OK.
course_highlights: The course runs through beautiful summer scenery in Gamleby
Start and finish in Unos Park
Water stations at the start/finish and at 4 km
additional: Race numbers can be collected in Unos Park from 15:00 until one hour before the start. Children are offered hamburgers/sausages after the race, sponsored by ICA Supermarket. Medals are sponsored by Metallfabriken Norden AB. Professional timing by Racetimer. The prize ceremony takes place at approximately 19:25 for children and 20:45 for everyone else. A sprint prize at 450 m for the 4 km and 8 km races is a gift card worth 3000 kr. The 8 km course record comes with a 1000 kr prize.

name: Jølster Maraton
description: Jølster Marathon is a popular race that brings runners from all over the country to beautiful Jølster. The race starts and finishes at Jølstrahallen in Vassenden and offers four distances: marathon, half marathon, 10 km and 5 km. The route follows scenic stretches in the area, and places are limited, so early registration is recommended. The event also includes extra activities for the whole family and a music and marathon quiz the evening after the race.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Jølstrahallen in Vassenden
The route follows beautiful stretches in Jølster
Refreshment stations with water, squash, cola, sports drink and bananas
additional: Maximum 1,300 participants. Prize-giving at 13:00 for all distances. 5% of the proceeds go to a good cause. A pink T-shirt can be purchased, partially sponsored by Enivest. Cars are not allowed to drive to the event office on race day. Race numbers should be collected on Friday or well before the start. Extra activities, including a cycling event and a mini race for children, are held. Great prizes from sponsors are drawn among all participants. The top three in each category and distance receive prizes.

name: Bitihorn Opp
price_range: 150 kr under 17 år; 300 kr fra 17 år
description: Bitihorn Opp is an informal, laid-back uphill race up majestic Bitihorn in Øystre Slidre. The race is suitable for everyone, whether you walk or run, fast or slow, and focuses on an enjoyable outing in spectacular nature. The course follows stone steps and trails on the “front side” of Bitihorn, offering a unique nature experience with 450 metres of elevation gain over 2 kilometres. The event supports local sport, and all participants receive a prize, with extra prizes for the fastest man and woman.
course_highlights: The course follows majestic stone steps and trails on the front side of Bitihorn
450 metres of elevation gain over 2 kilometres
A spectacular nature experience in mountain terrain
additional: Bib distribution from 11:30 at the start of the stairs. Parking at Båtskaret, with signs on race day. The proceeds go to Øystre Slidre IL. All participants receive a prize, with extra prizes for the fastest man and woman, as well as fun draw prizes. Registration via EQ Timing. All participants receive a prize, with extra prizes for the fastest woman and man. Parking is listed at Båtskaret or Båtskardstølen.

name: Hornindal Rundt
location: Hornindal, Volda, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: Bocksten Trailrun
location: Öströö Fårfarm, Åkulla Bokskogar, Varberg Municipality, Halland County, Sweden
distance_verbose: Marathon, 24 km, Halvmarathon, 12 km, 6.7 km, 5 km
description: Bocksten TrailRun is a nature-focused trail race with its event centre at Öströö sheep farm and courses in the Åkulla beech forests. The event offers four distances (5 km, 12 km, 22 km and Ultra 44 km) through beech and spruce forests, with lake views and varied trails. The races are spectator-friendly, have limited start places, and offer participants a special medal. Welcome to experience the joy of running and a sense of community in a magical forest setting.
course_highlights: Running in the Åkulla beech forests and enchanting spruce forests
Varied terrain: technical trails, off-trail sections and gravel roads with lake views
Plenty of elevation and scenic views; also a 6.7 km loop course for the Vineyard Backyard Ultra
additional: Distances: 5 km (start 10:15, 200 places), 12 km (start 10:00, 400 places), 22 km (start 10:30, 300 places) and Ultra 44 km (start 08:00, 100 places). The total number of start places is limited (only 1000 places). GPS coordinates for the event centre: 57.06881078975495, 12.506526026672418. Only tap water is served during the event (no plastic bottles); Tailwind and squash are available as alternatives. For the Vineyard Backyard Ultra, bringing your own cup is mandatory; a headlamp and personal medication are mandatory, and the headlamp must be worn between 20:00 and 07:00. Bib collection and registration take place in the start area (see the invitation for the specified times); if you need assistance, contact race management on 076-8159678. It is possible to take out Startklar cancellation and accident insurance (see the invitation for prices). The summer edition takes place on 27 June 2026, with distances of 5/12/22/Ultra 44 km; the winter edition is at Öströö Gård, with 5/12/24 km and 500 places. Accommodation can be booked through Åkulla Resort with a discount (code bockstentrailrun). The Backyard Ultra race at Ästad Vingård has a 6.7 km course and starts every full hour.

name: Strömstadmilen
description: Strömstadmilen is a welcoming running event organized by Strömstad Running Club, featuring a runner-friendly 5-kilometer loop through central Strömstad. Participants can choose to run one or two laps, covering 5 km or 10 km, respectively. The event also includes races for children and young people, as well as a walking class along the Strömstad waterfront. The start and finish are at Strömsvallen, and the event has a lovely summer atmosphere, with plenty of spectators and activities creating a real town festival.
course_highlights: Runner-friendly 5 km loop through central Strömstad
Start and finish at Strömsvallen
Clearly marked course with plenty of directional signs
additional: Start times: 11:00 4 km walk, 12:10 Girls 7 years, 12:30 Boys 7 years, 12:50 Girls 9 years and Boys 9 years, 13:20 Girls 11 years and Boys 11 years, 14:00 5 km, 15:00 10 km. Bib pickup and race-day registration are available from 09:30 on race day and also the evening before. All participants who finish receive a specially designed medal. A technical T-shirt featuring a Strömstadmilen design can be purchased when registering. Timekeeping ends at 16:45. Parking at Strömsvallen is limited; parking at Strömstad Upper Secondary School is recommended. Start and finish at Strömsvallen. The information found relates to the 2026 edition and does not confirm details for 2027.

name: Kolmårdsrundan / Kolmården Ultra Trail
description: Kolmården Ultra Trail is a challenging and scenic running experience in the deep forests of Kolmården, with distances of 45 km and 60 km. The course offers varied terrain, with forest trails, mountain ridges featuring spectacular views, sections along the shores of Bråviken, and technical running in nature reserves. The race is suitable for both elite runners and recreational runners seeking a memorable trail experience. At the finish, participants receive a medal and a light meal, included in the entry fee.
course_highlights: Start in Kolmården Forest, with trails through varied terrain
Views from the mountain ridge at Kvarseboklint and running along the shores of Bråviken
Technical and challenging running through Bråviksbranten Nature Reserve
additional: Mandatory equipment: mobile phone, running vest/backpack/belt with at least 0.5 L of fluids, a pressure bandage/blood stopper, and a map with the emergency number (provided at bib collection). Aid stations: the 45K has 4 stations, and the 60K has 5 stations offering sports drink, energy products, and water. The cutoff time for the 45K is 13:30 at 44 km (pace 9:00 min/km). Participants are served a light meal at the finish. Start and finish at Klintvallen in Kvarsebo. Medical services are available on site. After finishing, participants receive a medal and are offered hot vegetarian soup. Mandatory equipment rules apply; aid stations are located along the course.

name: Mörksuggejakten TrailRun

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Startavgift före 1/7 Barn och ungdom upp till 16 år 150 kr

description: Mörksuggejakten is one of Sweden’s most popular events in the long-distance race cup, offering a top-class competition since 1997. The cycling race in Rättvik features a beautiful and varied course covering 74 km, with a shorter 46 km option. The route passes through Rättvik, climbs to heights with breathtaking views over Lake Siljan, follows gravel roads and trails, and passes distinctive locations such as Dalhalla and Springkällan. Younger participants can take part in Lilla Mörksuggejakten, with several spectator-friendly courses in the Jarl area. Mörksuggejakten TrailRun also offers 10 km and 20.8 km runs starting from IK Jarl Rättvik.
course_highlights: The course offers beautiful views over Lake Siljan from the heights around Vidablick and the Hedsåsen summer pastures
The route follows gravel roads and trails, and crosses narrow suspension bridges over the Enån valley
Passes distinctive locations such as Dalhalla, Springkällan and Kungshol
additional: Mass start for all classes at 09:30. Maximum time: 5 hours. Race bibs can be collected on race day from 08:00 at IK Jarl. The courses are marked with red-and-white tape and signs. The course is 95% trail and 5% gravel road. It is permitted to switch to a shorter distance during the race. Parking is available at Rättvik Arena; camping in the parking area is prohibited.

name: Oslo Løpsfestival, Maridalsvannet rundt

description: Maridalsvannet Rundt is one of eight races in the Oslo Running Festival, which follows the capital’s beautiful trails and roads. The race has a mass start on Sunday, July 4 at 11:00, with the start and finish at Frysja, a lovely area with good facilities and opportunities for swimming, barbecuing, and relaxing after the race. The course is 13.5 km long and offers scenic surroundings around Lake Maridalsvannet. The Oslo Running Festival gives you the flexibility to run alone or with others, and you can take part in several races with a festival pass or day tickets.
course_highlights: The 13.5 km course goes around Lake Maridalsvannet
Start and finish at Frysja, with good facilities such as a café and grocery store
Lovely start and finish area with opportunities for swimming and barbecuing
additional: Race bibs can be picked up at Löplabbet Oslo city centre from April 7. The same race bib is used throughout the series. The course is marked only for the mass start. Timing is recorded by a chip attached to the race bib, which must be visible on your chest. There are good public transport connections and several parking spaces near the start area. The race can be completed at a time that suits you during the period June 25–July 4, 2027. An early-bird price is listed; prices vary by ticket type.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, halvmaraton
description: Perseløpet is a simple, fast race event at Ås school in Eidsvoll, featuring a flat, measured 2,633-metre loop. The race offers seven distances from 3 km to 100 km, including 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon, and is suitable for anyone looking to chase a personal best. Participants can set out their own bottles and gels on their personal nutrition table, which they pass each lap, giving them good control over their nutrition during the race. The event has good facilities, with changing rooms, toilets and free parking at the venue.
course_highlights: Flat, measured 2,633-metre loop
Each participant’s own nutrition table at every lap
Good facilities, with changing rooms and toilets inside Ås school
additional: Race numbers are collected at the school using self-service, approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. The race has a lap-time calculator for planning lap times. At selected races, 9th grade students from Feiring school staff an official drink station and raise money for their school trip. Participants who set a personal best can ring the bell near the finish area. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Race numbers are collected at the school using self-service from approximately two hours before the start.

name: Perseløpet ¤5- 2027
description: Perseløpet is a simple, fast race event at Ås School in Eidsvoll, featuring a flat, accurately measured 2,633-meter loop. The race offers seven distances from 3 km to 100 km, giving runners the opportunity to set personal records in a well-equipped setting with a dedicated nutrition table. Bibs are collected via self-service at the venue, which has free parking, changing rooms, and toilets. The race is organized by Feiring IL and has a tradition of many personal records, with a friendly atmosphere where runners can celebrate their personal records by ringing the bell at the finish.
course_highlights: Flat, accurately measured 2,633-meter loop
Dedicated nutrition table passed on every lap
Flat road races with the opportunity to achieve fast times
additional: Bibs are collected via self-service about two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms, and toilets are available at the venue. Runners can place their own bottles and gels on the nutrition table before the start. At selected races, 9th-grade students from Feiring School staff an official refreshment station to raise money for their school trip. A lap-time calculator is available to help plan split times. The weather forecast is updated four times daily based on satellite data for the area. Registration via RaceDays. Free parking, changing rooms, and toilets are available at the venue. Bibs are collected via self-service at the school, and runners can place their own drinks and nutrition at the nutrition table.

name: Feriespretten 2027
description: Feriespretten is the most beautiful and fun summer trail race, organized by Hope IL in Risør, Agder. The race offers two distances over varied, hilly terrain, with the start and finish in the same place. The long course of approximately 9 km is suited to those looking for a proper workout in beautiful natural surroundings, while the short course of approximately 5 km is perfect for beginners, children and families, or as an untimed fun run. Feriespretten is a family-friendly event that brings experienced runners and beginners together for an enjoyable race experience.
course_highlights: Two distances over varied, hilly terrain
Start and finish in the same place
The course runs through beautiful natural surroundings on the Sandnes Peninsula
additional: The race takes place on Tuesday, 7 July 2026 at 18:00. The short course can be run untimed as a fun run. The organizer is Hope IL. Results and statistics from previous years are available on the website. Untimed recreational classes are offered for the 5 km and 9 km distances. The time is provided in the organizer’s channels.

name: Hestane Skyrace
organizer: Lars Øvrebø og Torstein Bolstad Blikra, med Gaular IL
description: Hestane Skyrace is a demanding skyrace over the spectacular peaks of Storehesten and Lisjehesten in Bygstad. The race features technical climbing, an exposed ridge and magnificent panoramic views in dramatic natural surroundings. There are two distances: 32 km with 1,900 metres of elevation gain and 26 km with 1,400 metres of elevation gain, both across challenging mountain terrain. The event is a celebration for the whole village, with activities for participants and spectators alike.
course_highlights: Technical climbing and an exposed ridge over Storehesten and Lisjehesten
Magnificent panoramic views and challenging mountain terrain
Two distances: 32 km (~1,900 m elevation gain) and 26 km (~1,400 m elevation gain)
additional: Mandatory equipment: mobile phone, 1 L of water, emergency ration and wind jacket. Cutoff at Skaraly at 15:30; final finish at 19:00. Parking at Langeland Ski Centre costs 50 kr. Race bibs can be collected on Friday 9 July and on race day from 07:00. There are staffed stations with water and first aid along the route. After-run gathering at Tønna in Bygstad from 20:00, with food and socialising. Start and finish at Langeland Ski Centre. Start at 09:00. Registration via Racedays.

name: Black Lake Race
description: Black Lake Race is a challenging mountain trail race held in Vågstranda, Norway, featuring stunning views over Norwegian fjords. The main 29 km course combines runnable terrain, steep climbs, and exposed ridge running, including a demanding ascent to Trollstolen and a high mountain ridge section. There is also a faster and more accessible 20 km course that mixes gravel roads, forest trails, alpine terrain, and technical descents. The race offers a unique experience in spectacular natural surroundings with aid stations and mandatory GPX navigation for the longer course.
course_highlights: Steep climbs, including more than 850 vertical meters of ascent to Trollstolen
Exposed mountain ridge running with panoramic fjord views
Technical descents and alpine terrain
additional: The 29 km race requires mandatory GPX navigation loaded onto GPS watches. Aid stations with food and drinks are available along the course. A 5-hour cut-off applies at Checkpoint 3 on the 29 km course, with an alternative route for late participants. Running poles are permitted. Free camping is offered for participants at Hjelvik Idrettsplass, with assistance available for campervan/caravan parking upon request.

name: Melbuløpet
location: Melbu torg, Melbu, Hadsel, Nordland, Norway
description: Melbuløpet takes place at Melbu Square and offers three officially measured distances: 2.5 km, 5 km and 10 km on a very flat, fast course, offering good opportunities to achieve fast times. A children’s race of approximately 600 metres is also held for the youngest participants. The race is part of Sommer-Melbu, a long-running summer festival held since 1986 and characterised by broad local involvement and a strong volunteer spirit.
course_highlights: Very flat and fast course
Three officially measured distances: 2.5 km, 5 km and 10 km
Children’s race of approximately 600 metres
additional: The children’s race starts at 15:30 and the competitive race categories start at 16:00. Children’s race participants register on site. The race is held as part of the Sommer-Melbu festival, which lasts ten days and is run by volunteers. The listed start location is Melbu Square. Registration for the competitive race categories is via EQ Timing, while children’s race participants register on site.

name: Hornindal Rundt
description: Hornindal Rundt is a demanding mountain ultramarathon through the spectacular scenery of Hornindal, surrounded by some of the finest mountains in the Nordic region. The race covers 75 kilometres with 5,600 metres of elevation gain and includes 20 mountain checkpoints. Participants experience a tough and varied course with views of Jostedalsbreen, the Sunnmøre Alps and the sea, and are challenged both physically and mentally in one of Norway’s most demanding trail races.
course_highlights: 75 km ultramarathon with 5,600 metres of elevation gain
20 mountain checkpoints along the route
Views of Jostedalsbreen, the Sunnmøre Alps and the sea
additional: The 75 km ultramarathon starts at 07:00 from Honndalshallen. There are cut-off times along the course to ensure safety, with the first at Horndøla Bru and the second at Holskarsætra (checkpoint 13). Participants in the 75 km race must carry mandatory equipment, including a headlamp, clothing and a mobile phone. For the 75 km race, the start is at Honndalshallen at 07:00, and mandatory equipment includes a headlamp, clothing and a mobile phone. The 38 km race starts at Horndøla Bru at 11:00 and finishes at Honndalshallen. The race information on the website applies to 2026; the date and details for 2027 have not been confirmed in the available sources.

name: Böda Sandsloppet
location: Böda Sand SportCamp, Böda, Öland, Sweden
description: Böda Sandsloppet is a family-friendly running race held at Böda Sand SportCamp on Öland. The race offers several distances for both children and adults, with routes through lovely forest terrain. Adults can choose between 6.5 km and 4 km, while shorter distances are available for children and young people. All participants who finish the race receive a medal as a keepsake. The event has a welcoming atmosphere and is open to runners of all ages and abilities.
course_highlights: Route through lovely forest terrain
Start and finish at Böda Sand SportCamp
Distances available for both children and adults
additional: Late registration is available through 8 July, followed by race-number collection on race day from 15:00. Payment can be made in cash, by card or via Swish. Children and young people under 11 are not timed and there is no prize ceremony for them. Start and finish at Böda Sand SportCamp. Register by 3 July 2027; late registration is available for a higher fee. Children aged 11 and under are not timed and there is no prize ceremony.

name: Musköloppet
description: Musköloppet is a popular running race held in the spectacular archipelago setting of Muskö. The race has a long tradition and celebrated its 30th anniversary in 2022, after being paused during the pandemic. There are several different courses and categories, including children’s races, and the event offers a wonderful nature experience, with the start and finish at Muskö Hembygdsgård. Late registration is available on site up to one hour before the start.
course_highlights: The race takes place in the beautiful archipelago setting of Muskö
Start and finish at Muskö Hembygdsgård
Children’s races over 1.5 km and 2.5 km for different age groups
additional: Late registration is available on site at the start and finish area up to one hour before the race begins. There are water stations along the course, and runners may arrange their own drinks. Race management may decide to restart the race if needed. Pacing assistance from non-competitors is not permitted. The children’s races start at 10:00 for 1.5 km (ages 7–10) and at 10:30 for 2.5 km (ages 11–14). The countdown on the official website indicates 10 July 2027. However, the published times and distances on the website are for 2026. The relay costs 150 kr per team, and the children’s race for ages 4–6 is free, according to the published information.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://www.muskoloppet.se/): 2027-07-10 — "Nedräkning till Musköloppet 10 juli 2027" (was estimated 2027-07-10)

name: H2 Trail
distance_verbose: 50 miles, 50 km, 28 km, 18 km, 10 km, 5 km
description: Umara H2 Trail 2027 is organized by OK Skogsvargarna and takes place on July 10 at Bergagården, Hunneberg. The event offers several distances from 6 km up to 50 km, including a kids’ trail for the youngest participants. The courses cross varied terrain on Hunneberg, with a mix of trails, gravel roads and asphalt, and feature beautiful viewpoints, crofts and swimming spots. All participants in the 11 km to 50 km distances receive their own Umara cup to reduce the use of disposable cups at the aid stations. The club also offers showers, a sauna and changing rooms in its clubhouse at Bergagården.
course_highlights: The 50 km distance crosses Hunneberg and passes attractions such as viewpoints, crofts and swimming spots
The course is marked with arrows and flags, and consists of 23% gravel roads, 73% trails and 4% asphalt
Kids’ trail and mini trail for children, with a medal for every participant
additional: All participants in the 11 km to 50 km distances receive their own Umara cup to use at the aid stations to reduce the use of disposable cups. Aid stations are located along the course, and participants are encouraged to carry their own fluids. Support is available at a designated spot on the course at the lap point at Bergagården (25 km). The kids’ trail and mini trail are untimed, and every participant receives a medal. The clubhouse at Bergagården offers showers, a sauna and changing rooms. Parking is available about 300 metres from the event centre and is signposted. A mobile phone and power bank are recommended for emergencies. Previous editions have had aid stations along the course; participants have needed to bring their own fluids.

name: Gotland Run 511k (2026)
description: Gotland Run 511k is a unique running adventure and a journey to explore your inner landscape. It is not a traditional race, but a self-supported run around the beautiful island of Gotland, including a loop around Fårö, starting and finishing in Visby. Participants have 10 days to complete the approximately 511 km course, with support from four Angel Stations along the way. The organizer provides basic support, while runners are responsible for their own food and accommodation.
course_highlights: Start and finish in Visby, Gotland’s medieval capital
Clockwise loop around the island, including Fårö
Mixed terrain with asphalt, gravel roads, and shorter trails
additional: Participants must check in twice daily using an online tool. Accommodation on the first night is at Visby Fängelse Hostel in shared rooms. A pre-race dinner and briefing are held the evening before the start. Angel Stations offer support, water, rest, and sometimes shower facilities. The ferry to Fårö runs every 30 minutes, but requires a call between 22:00 and 05:30. The run must be completed on foot within 10 days, averaging approximately 51 km per day. Luggage storage is available at the hostel. Parking is available near the ferry terminal, with cheaper options at Visby Airport. This is a self-supported event: participants are responsible for most of their food and logistics. The entire distance must be completed on foot within ten days, with regular position reports.

name: Branäsutmaningen
description: Branäsutmaningen is a summer adventure in Branäs featuring a challenging 6-kilometre course. Branäs is known for its beautiful natural surroundings and family-friendly outdoor activities all year round. In summer, activities include mountain biking, padel and water activities by the Klarälven River. Branäs is investing in family-friendly cycling trails and scenic hiking trails, making it a perfect place for an active and fun summer experience.
course_highlights: A challenging 6-kilometre course
Family-friendly downhill trails and wide cross-country trails
A scenic location by the Klarälven River, with hiking trails and fishing
additional: Branäs offers family-friendly lift-accessed cycling, with the six-seat express lift Sjöexpressen at the heart of its cycling programme. There are barbecue and rest areas with views, miles of gravel and paved roads for training, and cycling tracks for children at Soltorget. Food and drinks are available at Ladan restaurant in the centre. The summer map includes a pump track, zipline, trampoline with a big airbag, and trails in Logläntan. Start at 14:00 at Soltorget. Family Day also includes Björnbuseloppet for children, an after-run and an evening of live music. The first prize in the race is a family ski holiday.

name: Semesterhalvmaran
location: Torps herrgård, Kumla Municipality, Örebro County, Sweden
description: Semesterhalvmaran is a recurring running event organized by the running club LK Gränslöst, inviting runners to experience the beautiful open landscapes of the Närke Plain. The race starts and finishes at Torps herrgård outside Kumla and offers a lovely running experience on gravel roads among rolling grain fields. After a two-year break, the race returns on July 11, 2027, welcoming runners of all levels to take part in a community filled with the joy of running. LK Gränslöst is an inclusive club that aims to bring runners from across the country together and build a strong community around running.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Torps herrgård outside Kumla
Run on gravel roads among rolling grain fields on the Närke Plain
Beautiful, nature-rich surroundings on the Närke Plain
additional: Registration is planned to open in January. The race is organized by the running club LK Gränslöst, which also organizes other races and group training every Wednesday at 18:00 in Örebro. The club focuses on community and the joy of running for all levels.

pipeline_log.evidence_quote: Söndagen den 11 juli 2027 är det åter dags för löpning på Närkeslätten när den är som bäst!

name: Västervik City Run
description: Västervik City Run is a city race of approximately 6.3 km that takes place in and around central Västervik, starting and finishing at Grönsaks- och Fiskartorget. The race offers a scenic course along the cycle path beside Gamlebyviken, passing landmarks including the Stegeholm Castle ruins and Myntbryggan. After finishing, participants receive a medal as proof of their participation. The race is a popular summer tradition that welcomes runners of all ages.
course_highlights: A city race of approximately 6.3 km in central Västervik
The course follows the cycle path beside Gamlebyviken and passes the Stegeholm Castle ruins
Start and finish at Grönsaks- och Fiskartorget
additional: A children’s race (Sparbanksloppet) of 800 m for children up to 10 years old, with a group start from Fiskaretorget at 18:30. Participants receive medals after finishing. A separate Sparbanksloppet of approximately 700 metres is offered for children up to 10 years old. Registration for the 2027 race opens on 1 May.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://www.vikhockey.se/boka-bord-2/city-run/): 2027-07-12 — "Måndag den 12 juli är det dags för 2027 års löpartävling i Västerviks centrum!" (was estimated 2027-07-05)
pipeline_log.evidence_quote: Måndag den 12 juli är det dags för 2027 års löpartävling i Västerviks centrum!

name: Sommerkarusell Ålesund - 2. løp
description: The Summer Series in Ålesund is a long-running race series held in scenic surroundings along Vasstranda by Lillevatnet and Brusdalsvatnet. The courses are relatively flat and run on asphalt with little traffic, offering good conditions for both the 5 km and 10 km distances. The races start from the car park by the walking trail at the western end of Lillevatnet in Spjelkavik. The atmosphere is friendly, with prizes and medals for participants who take part in multiple races. The Summer Series has a long history in Ålesund and is now back under the organisation of Ålesundløpene.
course_highlights: The courses run along Vasstranda on the south side of Lillevatnet and Brusdalsvatnet
Relatively flat asphalt courses with little traffic
Start and finish at the car park by the walking trail at the western end of Lillevatnet in Spjelkavik
additional: The 10 km starts at 18:00 and the 5 km at 18:05. The courses have been officially measured by Kondis. Gift prizes are awarded after each race. Medals go to participants who take part in 2 or 3 races in the series. Course records for both the 5 km and 10 km distances are listed. The participation record is 132 finishers. Registration is through EQ Timing. Participants who finish at least two races in the series receive a medal at the final race of the season.

name: Victorialoppet
description: Victorialoppet is a traditional running festival held every year in Borgholm on Öland. The event offers several distances for all ages and abilities, including a 9 km main race, the 4 km Victoriajoggen, the 2 km Lilla Victorialoppet, and Mini, a 1.5 km race for the youngest participants. The course is fast and easy to run, with beautiful views along the shore and an enthusiastic crowd creating a wonderful atmosphere. The event is a popular celebration, with music along the course and a strong commitment to the Crown Princess Victoria’s Fund.
course_highlights: Fast, easy-to-run 9 km course with views along the shore
Music at several locations along the course
Courses adapted for all ages and abilities
additional: Bib pickup takes place on race day from 10:00 to 18:00 at Borgholms Sporthall. Changing rooms and showers are available for men and boys at Borgholms Sporthall, and for women and girls at Viktoriaskolan’s gymnasium. Water is provided along the 9 km course, and there is music at several locations. Prizes are awarded in different categories, and participants receive medals, commemorative plaques, ice cream, and drinks, depending on the race. Timing uses disposable chips for most races; timing is optional for Victoriajoggen and the parasport categories. There are also parasport and youth categories. Water is available along the 9 km course, and changing rooms and showers are provided at Borgholms Sporthall and Viktoriaskolan’s gymnasium. Fees vary depending on the race and registration date; an administration fee applies.

name: Kraftprovet
organizer: Trollhättans IF Friidrott och Trollhättans SOK
description: Kraftprovet is a classic city race in Trollhättan, offering a unique running experience along the canal area, with leafy paths, hilly terrain and beautiful views of the Göta älv, the locks and historic power stations. The race is a festival for everyone, with both elite runners and recreational runners taking part, while cheers from the crowd and music along the course add to the atmosphere. With more than 40 years of tradition, Kraftprovet brings the city, nature and people together during Fallens Dagar. There are several races to choose from, ranging from 800 metres to 11.6 kilometres, including a fun costume competition and an untimed Fun Run category.
course_highlights: The course follows the canal area, with varied and hilly terrain
Beautiful views of the Göta älv, the locks and historic power stations
Crowd support, music and a festive atmosphere along the entire course
additional: Start and finish at Hansenplatsen in Trollhättan. A race bib with your first name is available if you register by 30 June. A T-shirt can be ordered when registering by 15 May; it is included in some races and costs extra in others. Runners who finish in under 50 minutes (men) or 55 minutes (women) receive a silver medal. Pacers are available for finish times of 50, 55, 60 and 65 minutes. Costume competition with prizes before the start. Showers and changing facilities are available about 1 km from the finish at Arena Älvhögsborg. Water stations with Umara sports drink and water are available along the course.

name: Yttersia Skyrace Senja
description: Yttersia Skyrace Senja is a rugged and accessible skyrace held on the spectacular outer side of Senja, starting and finishing at Yttersia Base in Skaland. The course takes participants through dramatic coastal mountain terrain with long ridgelines, steep cliffs and fantastic views of Bergsøyene, Steinfjorden and Okshornan. The race features a continuous, runnable climb to Husfjellet, followed by narrow, exposed ridges and challenging technical terrain. It finishes with a social atmosphere, music and an after-run gathering at the finish area. This race is for those who want to experience authentic Senja terrain and a day filled with community and good spirits.
course_highlights: Dramatic coastal mountain terrain with long ridgelines and steep cliffs
Continuous, runnable climb to Husfjellet (632 m above sea level) with spectacular views
Technical, untouched terrain at Nonshaugen, home to a historic graphite mine
additional: The race starts with a short stretch of gravel road before continuing onto trail and uphill terrain. There is one drinking station at Litjebrusen. The finish area at Yttersia Base offers music, an announcer, awards, food, drinks and an after-run gathering with a social atmosphere into the afternoon and evening. For 2026, the course is listed as running over gravel road, trail and technical mountain terrain, with one drinking station. These details are not confirmed for 2027.

name: Lidingöloppet Funäsfjällen
description: Lidingöloppet Funäsfjällen is a challenging trail race in a mountain setting, with steep climbs, sloping trails and flat meadows offering fantastic views of the mountains. The race combines adrenaline-filled running with scenic experiences and is held at Bruksvallarna ski stadium in Bruksvallarna. This is the fourth edition of the race, welcoming runners to a unique and beautiful challenge in the Swedish mountains.
course_highlights: Steep climbs and sloping trails
Flat meadows with incredible mountain views
A downhill stretch towards Bruksvallarna village after a tough climb
additional: Bib pick-up takes place at the venue in Bruksvallarna. A late-entry fee of SEK 100 applies to registrations on race day. During the week before the race, running clinics, shoe testing, try-out mountain running sessions and other activities are held in Bruksvallarna. Water stations and food and drink stations are available along the course.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://www.lidingoloppet.se/lidingoloppet-funasfjallen): 2027-07-17 — "Date 17 juli" (was estimated 2027-07-10)

name: Gårvikloppet
description: Gårvikloppet is a popular running race in Gårvik that began in 2016 and quickly became a success, with over 100 participants of all ages. The race offers several classes and courses, from challenging tough courses to walking classes, making it possible for everyone to take part regardless of ability. The event is run by Badortsföreningen in collaboration with Dreambody gym and is known for its friendly, inclusive atmosphere.
course_highlights: Several courses and classes for different ability levels
Trail running in scenic Gårvik
Course records for 4 km and 8 km for both women and men
additional: The race has classes ranging from walking to elite level and welcomes participants of all ages. Course records are listed for 4 km and 8 km for both women and men. Previous results include 4 km and 8 km classes. Information about registration and the 2027 format is not available in the sources.

name: Blefjells Beste
description: Blefjells Beste is a trail race on Blefjell that passes several of the most beautiful places on Store-Ble. The race offers distances of 92, 53, 24, 10 and 5 km, and is a social, informal event for everyone who enjoys being outdoors in the forest and mountains. The start and finish are at Bestebu, a private cabin at Klengstøl. The courses are mainly on trails and mountain terrain, with the final kilometres on gravel roads. Participants must carry all their own food, drink and equipment, as there are no food or drink stations along the way.
course_highlights: Trail race with distances of 92, 53, 24, 10 and 5 km
The courses are mainly on trails and mountain terrain, with 150 to 3,150 metres of elevation gain
Start and finish at the Bestebu cabin at Klengstøl, along Store-Bleveien
additional: The Storetroll course (92 km) consists of completing the other distances—53+24+10+5 km—in sequence. For the 92 km race, there are time limits for passing through the event area: after 1 lap (53 km) by Saturday at 12:00, and after 2 laps (53 + 24 km) by Saturday at 18:00. The 53 km and 24 km courses are not marked by the organiser, while the 5 km and 10 km courses are well marked. Name changes cost 150 kr for the 92, 53 and 24 km distances, and are free for the 10 and 5 km distances. The race requires participants to respect wild reindeer and leave no litter. There are no food or drink stations along the way, but clean water is normally easy to find in the mountains. Participants must carry their own food, drink and equipment; there are no food or drink stations. The event is listed for 23–24 July 2027, with registration opening on 1 December 2026.

name: Kaldoaivi Ultra Trail
description: Kaldoaivi Ultra Trail is the world’s northernmost ultra-running event, held in Utsjoki, in the Lapland wilderness. The route climbs to the summits of Kaldoaivi’s highest fells and offers spectacular, challenging scenery. The race tests runners’ endurance and skills in demanding natural terrain, but rewards them with an experience that brings many back year after year. The event also includes mountain bike races and offers a range of options for participants of different levels.
course_highlights: The route climbs to the summits of Kaldoaivi’s highest fells
Spectacular, rugged Lapland wilderness scenery
A demanding and instructive trail route
additional: Registering for two days gives a 30% discount on the price of the lower-priced category. The entry fee includes drinks and energy supplies at aid stations, washing facilities, transport of a gear bag to the finish, a race number, timing, a Kaldoaivi Ultra Trail lightweight backpack, a KUT product and a Finisher pendant. Category changes and transfers are free of charge until 7.7.2027. The event centres and start locations are in Nuorgam and Utsjoki. The race schedule includes several start times for different distances on 23.7. and 24.7.2027. Participant limits vary by distance; for example, MTB & E-MTB 57 km: 100 participants, Trailrun 168 km: 100 participants. The event offers several distances, including trail running, mountain biking and road cycling, with no amenities along the route. Participation includes a race number, timing chip, lightweight backpack and Finisher pendant. The event takes place in July 2027; detailed schedules and registration information are available on the website.

name: Rondane Backyard Ultra
description: Rondane Backyard Ultra is a unique ultrarun in the beautiful natural surroundings of Rondane, held at Stormoegga Ski Arena in Folldal. The race follows a scenic and varied loop through the Kroktjønna area, with pine forest, trails, gravel roads and idyllic ponds, and the Rondane mountains as a spectacular backdrop. The competition is a “Last Man Standing” race, with a new loop starting every hour, and continues until only one runner remains. In 2027, a separate night course will be introduced, offering participants a different experience in the dark. The arena’s service building offers facilities such as showers, changing rooms and a lounge for runners and supporters.
course_highlights: A varied route on forest trails, gravel paths and tractor roads in scenic surroundings
The course passes the Kroktjønna swimming area twice per lap
Night course on gravel road and asphalt between midnight and 06:00
additional: The race starts on 24 July 2027 at 09:00 and continues as long as runners complete the lap in under one hour. The service building at Stormoegga Ski Arena offers toilets, changing rooms, showers and a lounge. Participants may pitch their own tents and park caravans/campervans on site. A reflective vest is mandatory between 23:00 and 04:00, and a headlamp is recommended between 00:00 and 03:00. The race takes place on private gravel roads with some vehicle traffic, and runners must run on the left-hand side. First aid is available, and the race director can be contacted by phone on 909 56 674. Race bibs and timing chips are used. All places are sold out, but there is a waiting list to take over resold race entries. The start and finish are at Stormoegga Ski Arena, which has a lounge, kitchen, toilets, changing rooms and showers. Camping or parking a campervan/caravan at the arena is permitted.

name: Bleik Backyard Ultra - Last Man Standing
Kyststien Trail Ultra

description: Kyststien Trail Ultra is an unforgettable 50 km ultramarathon along the Coastal Trail from Helgeroa to Gon Camping. The race offers varied terrain, including idyllic sandy beaches, technical trails along cliffs and coves, and spectacular panoramic views of the sea and lush countryside. It is a challenge that requires good preparation, with demanding climbs and descents, but also offers the joy of running and a wonderful sense of community among participants. The race celebrates nature and a passion for running, and encourages respect for the surroundings.
course_highlights: 50 km along the Coastal Trail over varied terrain: sand, grass, mountains, stairs, rocks, roots and gravel
Spectacular panoramic views of the sea, cliffs and lush countryside
Technical coastal trails with demanding climbs and descents
additional: Race bibs can be collected the evening before or on race day. The finish at Gonhytta offers water, drinks, snacks and hot soup. Prizes for the top 3 women and men, plus a race-bib raffle. All finishers receive a locally made birch medal. There is an opportunity to take a free hot shower and a cold sea swim. The race has 5 staffed aid stations with first aid, toilets, drinks and snacks. The course is marked with blue blazes and additional signs; a GPX file is recommended for navigation. Maximum 180 participants; a waiting list will be available if the race fills up. The start is at Blokkebukta camping, with the finish at Gonhytta at Gon Camping. Participants are provided with refreshments and a free hot shower, and all finishers receive a medal made from local birch.

name: Mefjellet Opp 2027
description: Mefjellet Opp is a traditional uphill race organized by Valldal Idrettslag in Fjørå, Valldal. The race features a challenging climb up Mefjellet and attracts both local and visiting runners looking for a demanding and scenic experience. The event is a great opportunity to test your fitness in beautiful surroundings and experience the welcoming atmosphere of Valldal IL.
course_highlights: Steep uphill climb up Mefjellet
Scenic surroundings in Fjørå, Valldal
A traditional race with strong local roots
additional: The event is organized by Valldal Idrettslag. No specific information about the start time, price, or registration was found. Contact person for the event: leiar@valldalil.no. A village brunch is also held at the clubhouse in November, and the clubhouse is available for private use in June, but these are not directly related to the race. Previous editions have had a recreational start from Fjørå town center or Hauge, and a mass start for the competition classes. There have been two water stations along the course.

name: Helags Fjällmara
description: Helags Fjällmara is a classic mountain marathon held in the Ljungdalsfjällen since 1985. The race offers several distances to suit all levels, from the challenging 42 km full marathon to the 800-metre children’s race. It offers a unique mountain experience amid beautiful scenery and varied terrain, and is family-friendly, with races for both adults and children. The start and finish are on the meadow in the centre of Ljungdalen, and the event includes energy and drink stations, a personal cup, a medal for everyone who finishes, and showers and a sauna after the race.
course_highlights: Trail race amid the beautiful mountain scenery of the Ljungdalsfjällen
Distances ranging from an 800 m children’s race to a 42 km full marathon
Start and finish on the meadow in the centre of Ljungdalen
additional: Mass start for all distances. Race bibs are distributed at the gymnasium by the event area, with a chip for electronic timing. Energy and drink stations along the course and after the finish. A medal for everyone who finishes. Showers and a sauna are available after the race. Participant caps apply to each distance; for example, 100 participants for the 42 km race. Children under a certain age must run with an adult.

name: Hornsjön Runt
description: Hornsjön Runt is a traditional running race around Öland’s only inland lake, through beautiful and varied Öland countryside. The race offers several distances for both young people and adults, including a walking class. Along the course, participants pass gravel roads with limestone surfaces, grass, cow pastures, deciduous and coniferous forest, and sand dunes. Everyone who finishes receives a medal, and prizes are awarded to the top three in each class.
course_highlights: The race goes around Öland’s only inland lake
Varied terrain including gravel roads, grass, cow pastures, deciduous and coniferous forest, and sand dunes
Three water stations along the course, as well as at the start/finish
additional: A walking class is available for 5.5 km and 11 km, with start times between 13:00 and 16:00 and no timing. Showers and changing facilities are available at Högby Idrottsplats. Prizes are awarded to the top three in all classes. The start and finish are at Pensionat Hornsjön. Youth classes have different start times between 15:30 and 16:00, depending on age and distance. There are distances for children and young people, as well as an untimed walking class. Everyone who finishes receives a medal.
