name: Blodslitet
description: Blodslitet is an international ultra-long-distance orienteering race and a long-standing season finale in Norway, organized annually by Fredrikstad Ski Club. The race offers challenging and varied courses in beautiful terrain, with mass starts in all classes, including the Norwegian Ultra-Long-Distance Championships. The terrain at Gillingsrød consists of open spruce and pine forest, marshland, and demanding hilly sections, and is suitable for elite athletes, recreational runners, and young participants alike. Blodslitet is known for its lively arena atmosphere and exciting battles on the course.
course_highlights: Ultra-long-distance race with mass starts in all classes
Varied terrain featuring spruce and pine forest, marshland, and hilly sections
New orienteering map at a scale of 1:15000, 1:10000, or 1:7500
additional: Parking is available in fields 200–700 meters from the arena, with a parking fee of 75 NOK payable via Vipps. Race office with collection of bib numbers and maps. EmiTag is used for timing; rental of an EmiTag costs 50 NOK. Kiosk serving food and drinks, as well as sports equipment for sale at the arena. Childcare and a Småtroll program are available. Poor mobile coverage, but a guest network from NOF is available. First aid at the arena. Start and finish at the arena, with mass starts in all classes.

name: Sørdalskarusellen - Tverrløpet
location: Kleivbakken above Håkons Hall, Lillehammer, Norway
description: Sørdalskarusellen - Tverrløpet is the season finale of Sørdalskarusellen, a series of ten recreational races held from April to September. The race is suitable for everyone, regardless of fitness, age or ambitions, and focuses on the joy of running, community and personal achievement. The event offers an enjoyable race experience with a mass start and the option to run virtually. The start is at Kleivbakken above Håkons Hall in Lillehammer, and the distance is approximately 3.9 km.
course_highlights: Approximately 3.9 km course
Start at Kleivbakken above Håkons Hall in Lillehammer
Season finale of Sørdalskarusellen, with a mass start
additional: You can participate virtually from 5 to 8 September. The race is part of a series of ten recreational races suitable for all levels and ages. The organisers are Innlandet Corporate Sports Association and Tele BIL. The event emphasises the joy of running, community and personal achievement. Tverrløpet can also be completed virtually. The listed 2027 event is dated 8 September, but the date and time of the mass start should be confirmed with the organisers’ latest information.

name: Skärblackaloppet 2026
location: Folkets Hus, Skärblacka, Norrköping Municipality, Östergötland County, Sweden

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Early Bird, 250 kr, fram till och med 30 april 23:59.

description: Skärblackaloppet is an annual town race through beautiful Skärblacka in Östergötland. The event offers a festival atmosphere where everyone can take part, whether they choose to run 6 km, walk 4 km or cheer from the sidelines. The course runs on asphalt, cycle paths, gravel and partly on trails, with the start and finish at Folkets Hus. There are great prizes and exciting features such as the Mericon sprint and prize ceremonies for both runners and walkers.
course_highlights: 6 km run through Skärblacka on asphalt, cycle paths, gravel and trails
4 km walking class without timekeeping, starting and finishing at Folkets Hus
Mericon sprint over the final 300 metres, with a chance to win a gift card
additional: Race numbers can be collected at ICA Supermarket in Skärblacka on the Tuesday before the race between 11:00 and 18:00, or at Folkets Hus no later than one hour before the start. Late registration is available at race-number collection and on race day for an additional fee. Prizes are awarded to the fastest runners, gift cards are available for the Mericon sprint, and there are also prizes for picking up trimmers and tyres along the course. The walking class is not timed, and dogs are not allowed. A first-aid volunteer will be on site. There is also a 4 km walking class.

name: Sormlands 100 Trail Run
description: Sörmlands 100 Trail Run is a running event offering a unique experience through one of Sweden’s most biologically diverse regions. The races range from 8 km to 100 miles and cover a mix of forest trails, technical coastal paths, and fast sections. The event welcomes runners of all ages and abilities and offers a memorable weekend in Nävekvarn, surrounded by beautiful nature and challenging terrain.
course_highlights: A mix of forest trails, technical coastal paths, and fast sections
Distances ranging from 8 km to 100 miles
Beautiful, biologically diverse region along the Sörmlandsleden trail
additional: All distances are cupless, so participants must bring their own cup for drinks. After the race, a sauna and Nävekvarn Folkets Park are available. Well-stocked aid stations offer, among other things, Coca-Cola, Umara, coffee, and locally produced food. GPS tracking and live results are available. Mandatory equipment requirements vary by distance and include a mobile phone, navigation tools, a first-aid kit, and a headlamp for longer distances. Transport from the finish is available for the 50 km distance, with a bus to Nyköping Central Station. Race weekend runs from 10–12 September 2027. Registration opens on 1 December.

name: Sörmlands 100 Trail Run
location: Mariefred, Strängnäs Municipality, Södermanland County, Sweden
description: Sörmlands 100 Trail Run is an ultramarathon offering a unique experience through one of Sweden’s most species-rich regions. The race offers several distances from 8 km up to 100 miles, across varied terrain including forest trails, technical coastal paths, and fast sections. The event welcomes runners of all ages and levels and promises a memorable day in beautiful and challenging natural surroundings. After the race, sauna and locally produced food and drinks are available at Nävekvarn Folkets Park.
course_highlights: A mix of forest trails, technical coastal paths, and fast sections
Beautiful and challenging trail sections on the Sörmlandsleden trail
Well-stocked aid stations with a variety of energy options and drinks
additional: All distances are cupless, so participants must bring their own cup for drinks. Mandatory equipment includes a GPS tracker, a mobile phone with important numbers, a first-aid kit, a rain jacket, and a headlamp with extra batteries. Well-stocked aid stations along the course offer Coca-Cola, Umara, coffee, fruit, chips, and local specialties, among other items. After the race, sauna, locally produced food, and non-alcoholic beer are available. Shuttle buses from the finish of the 50 km race to Nyköping Central Station are available.

name: Kongskleiva Opp
description: Kongskleiva is Bekkjarvik’s most popular hike, a refreshing and scenic walk that rewards you with 360-degree views from the top of Kongsfjellet. The route passes through beautiful scenery via a fine Sherpa trail and includes a stop at Taushaugen, with views over Bekkjarvik. It is ideal for both exercise and enjoying nature, and offers the chance to spot wildlife from western Norway, such as white-tailed eagles and feral sheep. The official record time is an impressive 05:31.
course_highlights: A fine Sherpa trail through beautiful scenery
360-degree views from the top of Kongsfjellet
A chance to spot white-tailed eagles and feral sheep
additional: Parking is limited at the start of Kongskleivo; parking at Selbjørn Primary School, Bekkjarvik Torg or Leirvikjo is recommended. The hike can start from Bekkjarvik Torg or Leirvikjo and includes steps up to the summit. It suits all levels if you adjust your pace. Kongskleiva Opp is listed as 5 km. A results overview for 2026 lists the race as cancelled; information about the 2027 edition is not available in the sources.

name: Grimstad Maraton
price_range: Gratis barneløp; 250–600 kr for individuelle distanser; maratontrippel 950 kr; stafett 300 kr per deltaker

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Avgift: 250,- Passer for deg som vil løpe eller gå uten tidtaking.

description: Grimstad Marathon is an inclusive running festival taking place on 11 September 2027 in beautiful Grimstad. The event is suitable for all levels, from beginners to experienced runners, and offers distances from a 3 km fun run to a full half marathon, including a relay and a triple challenge. The start and finish are at Grimstad Library in Byhaven, and the course offers scenic surroundings, with sections through the town centre and cheering spectators. All participants receive medals, and there is also a free children’s race, Sparrisløpet.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Grimstad Library – Byhaven
The course passes through beautiful Groos and charming town-centre streets
Pacers are available for the 10 km and half marathon at various finish times
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the Library in Byhaven on Friday from 16:00 to 18:00 and on Saturday from 08:00. Changing facilities and lockers are available; bring your own padlock. EQ Timing handles registration, payment, timing and results. Pacers are available for the 10 km and half marathon at various finish times. The 3 km fun run is suitable for running or walking and is untimed. The 3 km distance is untimed and can be run or walked. All participants receive medals.

name: Nærsnes Backyard
description: Nærsnes Backyard is a social, accessible race held in Nærsnes, Asker. It is suitable for all levels, from beginners to experienced runners, and has both a children’s course and a longer adults’ course. The event focuses on participation and inclusion, and aims to be climate-neutral. It is a pleasant day with activities for the whole family, including a market, bouncy castle and face painting.
course_highlights: The course starts at the sports field and follows footpaths, trails and gravel roads in the area around Nærsnes.
Includes a steep hill of approximately 500 metres leading up to a farm.
Finishes with a lap of the football field and a finish beneath the finish arch.
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Sport1 (Rortunet) in the days before the race. The children’s race starts at 12:15, with a medal and ice cream from Joker Nærsnes. Activities include a market, bouncy castle, face painting and Wipe out for children and adults. The evening ends with lit fire pans from 19:00 to 23:00. Registration for 2027 is mentioned on the organiser’s website.

name: TFS FrontYard Festningen
description: TFS FrontYard Festningen is a unique race held at the historic Kristiansten Fortress in Trondheim. The race consists of a challenging 3 km loop course, with each lap needing to be run faster than the previous one, creating an exciting and tactical competition. The event offers a lively atmosphere, with the option to set up your own camp, and food and drinks available for both participants and spectators. This race is for anyone looking for a fun and challenging experience in the city's most iconic surroundings.
course_highlights: 3 km loop course at Kristiansten Fortress
Start and finish inside the fortress
Challenging race with the pace increasing each lap
additional: On race day, participants are advised to arrive well before the start. You can set up your own camp on Friday evening. Food and drinks are sold on site, but you must bring your own race nutrition or buy it at race bib collection. There is no parking at the fortress, and participants are encouraged to use public transport, cycle or walk. Spectators can follow the race live via RaceTracker. Camps can be set up from Friday evening. Parking is not available at the Fortress; the organizer encourages people to walk, cycle or use public transport. Registration via RaceTracker.

name: Jentebølgen - Steinkjer
description: Jentebølgen in Steinkjer is an inclusive race for girls and women of all ages, held as part of the Vi bryr oss run. The event brings participants together for an energising experience focused on achievement, community and mental health. Held at Steinkjer Torg, it offers a welcoming setting for taking part with friends, family and colleagues. Participation also supports Mental Helse Ungdom through a contribution for each race entry sold.
course_highlights: The race takes place at Steinkjer Torg
Focus on community, achievement and mental health
Open to girls and women of all ages
additional: The race entry includes access to the race, insurance and a ticket fee. The event supports Mental Helse Ungdom with NOK 10 for each race entry sold. The event is a meeting place focused on safety, inclusion, entertainment and activities. An earlier local Vi bryr oss race listing stated that 50% of ticket revenue goes to Mental Helse Ungdom. Prices and details for 2027 have not been confirmed.

name: Skjervøy 20:1000
description: Skjervøy 20:1000 is a challenging mountain race combining a 20 km distance with 1,000 metres of elevation gain in scenic surroundings on Skjervøy, at the edge of the open sea at 70 degrees north. The race features steep, technically demanding trails, cart tracks and boardwalks across marshland, with spectacular views and varied terrain around Skjervøy centre. It is suitable both for the fittest runners and for those looking for a manageable challenge, with recreational and competitive classes. A shorter 10 km course with 500 metres of elevation gain is also held, as well as a 1 km children’s race. The event has a social focus and aims to inspire more people to experience the island’s wonderful routes.
course_highlights: Steep, technically demanding trails with narrow sections
Cart tracks in hilly terrain and boardwalks across marshland
Wonderful views at 70 degrees north and a varied course around Skjervøy centre
additional: The 1 km children’s race is free, with registration on race day. Race bibs can be collected at Sporten Skjervøy on Thursday, Friday and Saturday before the race. Aid stations with water and cordial are located at 8 km and 12 km on the 20:1000 course, and at 3 km on the 10:500 course; runners must bring their own bottle or cup. Poles are allowed, but runners are responsible for their own safety. Headphones are not allowed. The time limit is 7 hours for the recreational class and 5 hours for the competitive class on the 20:1000. Prizes include cash prizes for the three fastest runners in the competitive class, a prize for a new course record, and draw prizes for all finishers. There is also a sprint prize (Seppalaspurten) on the final 160 metres. The programme lists separate starts for the recreational and competitive classes in the 20:1000 and 10:500. The children’s race is 1 km.

name: Valdresløpet
description: Valdresløpet is a challenging trail race that truly puts your running fitness and trail skills to the test. The half-marathon course offers varied terrain and a wonderful experience in the traditional mountain-farm region. There are also shorter distances, including a quarter marathon, and several mini-races for children in different age groups, so the whole family can take part and enjoy a sense of achievement.
course_highlights: Half marathon of 21.1 km with 570 m of elevation gain on varied terrain
Quarter marathon of 10.3 km, starting at the same place as the half marathon, but following its own route up Knippesetvegen
Several mini-races for children from 450 m to 3.9 km, adapted to different age groups
additional: The race bib must be attached visibly to the front of the chest, with two timing chips on the back. Race headquarters opens at 10:00 on race day. The Red Cross will be on standby with an ATV patrol and a treatment tent. Awards are given in 10-year age groups, with medals and Valdres Ost for the top three in each group. Refreshment and food stations on the half-marathon course are at 7.3 km, 12.9 km and 17.7 km. The quarter marathon has a refreshment station after 6.7 km. Start location: Vasetgrende 1, 2960 Røn. The event also includes three distances for children.

name: Kyststien Rundt 2027
location: Bud, Hustadvika, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Preliminärt pris for løpet 2027 er 500 kr pluss eventuelt 100 kr for transport.

description: Kyststien Trail Ultra is an unforgettable 50 km ultrarun along the Coastal Trail, from Blokkebukta Camping to Gon Camping. The race offers varied terrain, including sandy beaches, technical trails along cliffs and coves, and spectacular panoramic views of the sea and lush landscape. It is a challenge for adventurous runners looking to test their physical and mental limits while experiencing the beauty of nature. The race celebrates community and a shared passion for nature and running, with locally made medals for everyone who finishes.
course_highlights: 50 km of varied terrain with sand, grass, mountains, stairs, rocks, and roots
The course follows the blue-marked Coastal Trail, with extra signage and a GPX file available
Spectacular views of the sea, cliffs, and lush landscape
additional: Race bibs can be picked up the evening before or on race day. The finish is at Gonhytta, where water, snacks, and hot soup will be served. Prizes for the top 3 women and men, plus a race-bib draw. All finishers receive a locally made birch medal. Free hot showers and the option of a cold sea swim after finishing. Five staffed aid stations along the course with first aid, toilets, drinks, and snacks. The sports drink is homemade and contains sugar, salt, honey, and lime juice.

name: Urke Challenge Saksaløpet 2027
location: Urke, Ørsta, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: Ålesund Trail 2027
description: Ålesund Trail 2027 is a trail race offering challenges in some of Norway’s most beautiful surroundings, with Borgundfjorden and the Sunnmøre Alps as a backdrop. The event offers three distances: a 15 km main race that starts in the city and climbs into the mountains to around 450 metres above sea level, a demanding 2.75 km uphill race with 313 metres of elevation gain, and a short 500-metre children’s race. The event is suitable for all levels, from recreational runners to competitive athletes, and emphasizes a friendly atmosphere, safety, and sustainability. Mandatory equipment is required for the 15 km race, and staffed aid stations are available along the route and at the finish.
course_highlights: 15 km trail race with a highest point of around 450 metres above sea level
Demanding 2.75 km uphill race with 313 metres of elevation gain and a 20% gradient
Panoramic views of the Sunnmøre Alps and Borgundfjorden
additional: Start times: Uphill race 10:00, children’s race 11:00, 15 km main race 12:00. Mandatory equipment for the 15 km race: a fully charged mobile phone, at least 500 ml of drink, trail shoes, and clothing suitable for the conditions; food/energy is recommended. A staffed aid station is located halfway through the 15 km race, and another is at the finish of the uphill race. Equipment checks may take place at the start and along the route. Medical personnel are present at the start, finish, and aid stations. The organizer may stop the race in the event of safety threats. Participants are required to help injured runners. The event emphasizes leaving no trace and sustainability. The uphill race starts at 10:00 and the children’s race at 11:00. Participants in the 15 km race must bring a mobile phone, at least 500 ml of drink, trail shoes, and clothing suitable for the conditions. Course maps, elevation profiles, and GPX tracks are available, and registration is via the website.

name: Torvikbukt 6 topper 2027
location: Torvikbukt, Gjemnes, Møre og Romsdal, Norway
description: Torvikbukt 6 Topper is a challenging mountain race held in Torvikbukt, with several distances tailored to different age groups. The race offers spectacular scenery and six peaks that together involve considerable elevation gain. It is suitable for youth, junior and senior runners. The event has a long tradition and attracts both recreational and competitive runners looking for a challenging experience in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: The course includes six mountain peaks with up to 2,000 metres of elevation gain in total
Scenic surroundings in Torvikbukt with varied terrain
Several distances for youth, junior and senior runners, with varying lengths and elevation gain
additional: Start times vary by category: Tour class at 08:00, recreational at 10:00, senior at 11:00, junior and recreational at 11:30, and youth at 11:40. Registration is through EQTiming or on site for the tour class. Elevation profiles and maps of the course are available on the Instagram page. The listed distances and course information are from previous editions and may differ from 2027. Previous start and finish locations have been at Gjemneshallen.

name: MOSSARUN
description: Mossarun is a small, welcoming charity race in southern Sweden, focused on technical singletrack and community rather than prize money. The main format is a 17 km loop used for the 24-hour ultra; there are also 51 km and a children’s race. The course is technical and hilly, with many short, steep climbs and mostly singletrack. The organizers emphasize simplicity and sustainability, and a large portion of the entry fee goes to charity.
course_highlights: 17 km loop — used for the 24-hour ultra (51 km = 3 laps)
Approximately 500 m of elevation gain per lap (according to barometric watches)
90% singletrack, 10% gravel; technical terrain with many short hills
additional: Accommodation: you can sleep in the barn (20–30 places) or camp on site; social activities before and after the race include a campfire and BBQ/pizza. Wood-fired pizza is sold (100–120 kr, 13:00–15:00). 24-hour runners pass the base camp every lap; there are special features for the 24-hour race ("chainsaw segment") — see the race rules. The cut-off for the 24-hour ultra is stated as Sunday 6.09.2026. The event provides separate toilets/changing rooms and access to menstrual products; support is available to help find a night-running buddy for dark laps. Swish donations to WAR Child: 900 55 47 (write "mossarun"); alternatively, donate via the respective NGO’s website. Registration requires proof of a donation to War Child or another NGO; the event offers several distances and a child-friendly course.

name: Bysjöloppet
description: Bysjöloppet is a highly regarded race organized by Åtvidabergs IF since 1983. The race offers a varied course combining asphalt, gravel roads and forest trails through scenic, gently rolling terrain around Lake Bysjön in Åtvidaberg. The start and finish are at Edbergavallen, and the event offers several distances for both children and adults, with timing for most races. It is a family-friendly and inclusive competition, with medals for everyone who finishes and special commemorative medals for loyal participants.
course_highlights: A varied mix of surfaces: asphalt, gravel roads and forest trails
Scenic terrain around Lake Bysjön with moderate elevation changes
The 10 km course includes challenging trail sections and floodlit trails
additional: Start times: 700 m at 11:30, 1.3 km at 11:40, and 5 km and 10 km at 13:00. Race bibs can be collected from 10:00 on race day at Edbergavallen. Changing facilities, showers and toilets are available at Kanonvallen. A kiosk serving hot dogs, drinks and sweets is located at the event venue. Teams consist of 4–6 participants in any categories and receive a picnic bag from ICA Supermarket to share after finishing. Late registration is available on site from 10:00, with payment by Swish or cash; discount codes cannot be used for on-site late registration. The race has traditionally been held on the second Saturday in September and offers distances for children and adults.

name: Hagenloppet
description: Hagenloppet is a traditional running race held at Billingen in Skövde. The race offers several distances, including 8.8 km, 4.4 km, 2.5 km, and a children’s race for the youngest participants. The spectator-friendly course consists of two loops, with the start and finish at the ski stadium. The event is marked by a wonderful spirit of running and has a long history, attracting many participants from different age groups.
course_highlights: The course is 4.4 km long and consists of two loops
Start and finish at the ski stadium on Billingen
Spectator-friendly course with clear markings and course marshals
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the ski stadium from 10:00 and no later than 30 minutes before the start. Timing is done with a chip attached to the race number. Water is available at the lap point and finish. All finishers receive a medal. Prizes are awarded to the fastest runners in different categories. Late registration is available on race day from 10:00 until 45 minutes before the start. Refreshments are available near the finish. Parking is at the main car park in the Billingen Recreation Area.

name: Gränna StadsTrail
description: Gränna StadsTrail is a fun run offering a unique experience in nature and a challenge, with three distances: 5, 10 and 21 km. The race features varied terrain, from asphalt to winding trails through beech forest and up to the summit of Grännaberget. The start and finish are centrally located at Gränna Square, where participants can enjoy beautiful views over Lake Vättern and a mass start. All participants receive a unique medal, and times are recorded for all distances. The race is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners looking to combine performance with an experience in nature.
course_highlights: 21 km course combining asphalt, trails and gravel roads
Route through beech forest and up to the summit of Grännaberget
Start and finish at Gränna Square, with views over Lake Vättern
additional: The mass start is from Gränna Square, going through the town to the harbor, where timing begins. Timing and a unique medal for all participants. The race venue is in the heart of Gränna, close to shops, cafés and accommodation. The courses may change depending on conditions and permits. Timing and a medal at the finish.

name: Bocksten Vineyard Backyard Ultra
location: Ästad Vingård, Tvååker, Varberg Municipality, Halland County, Sweden
description: Bocksten Vineyard Backyard Ultra is a unique trail race held at Ästad Vingård. The race follows a 6.7 km loop through beautiful surroundings, with a start every hour on the hour. Participants run lap after lap until only one runner remains, creating an exciting and challenging race format. The event offers a wonderful atmosphere and the opportunity to enjoy Ästad Vingård’s scenic surroundings over an entire weekend.
course_highlights: A 6.7 km loop through the beautiful surroundings of Ästad Vingård
A start every hour on the hour, with runners completing laps until only one remains
Scenic views of beech forests, spruce forests and bogs
additional: The race starts every hour on the hour from 09:00. Anyone who does not complete the course before the next start is out of the race. The race continues until only one participant remains, and that runner completes a final solo lap. The loop course increases safety, makes the race spectator-friendly and allows runners to change equipment at the end of each lap. The event encourages community and respect for nature. The first start is at 09:00. The race continues until one participant remains, and that runner completes a final lap.

name: USWE Paradiset STHLM
description: USWE Paradiset STHLM is a trail race in the beautiful and rugged Paradiset nature reserve in southern Stockholm. The race offers challenging trail running along winding paths, across bogs and boardwalks, where runners experience forest, mountains and sea. The distances are 26 km, 13 km and 6 km, and the 26 km distance is a leg of the Outnorth Trailtour. The race is known for its strong sense of community and festive atmosphere after the finish.
course_highlights: Beautiful wild terrain with rocky outcrops and open pine forest
Small winding trails, bogs and boardwalks
The 26 km distance is a leg of the Outnorth Trailtour
additional: The race offers three distances: 26 km, 13 km and 6 km. There is a strong sense of community and a festive atmosphere after the finish. The terrain is challenging and gives runners a strong sense of achievement. 26 km. The race is part of the Outnorth Trailtour.

name: Duvnäsloppet
description: Duvnäsloppet is a family-friendly competitive and recreational race that has been held in Saltsjö-Duvnäs since 2007. The race is primarily intended for residents of Nacka, Värmdö and Saltsjöbaden, but welcomes other participants too. The start and finish are in Ringparken, and the race has strong local roots, with a focus on preserving its character as a family event for all ages. In 2027, the race celebrates 20 years with new start categories and continued community spirit among neighbours and runners.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Ringparken in Saltsjö-Duvnäs
Courses of 1.7 km, 5 km and 10 km (the 10 km course is two laps of the 5 km course)
The course features varied terrain with hills, a waterfront promenade and views around Duvnäs Udde
additional: Timing chips are now integrated into the race bib. Race administration opens the day before and on race day. Participant numbers are limited to preserve the family atmosphere. The children’s race has its own short course around Ringparken.

name: Innovationsstafetten
organizer: IFK Lund Friidrott, Ideon Science Park och Medicon Village
description: Innovationsstafetten is a relay race for teams of 2–4 people, held in Nobelparken in Brunnshög, Lund. The course is approximately 5.4 km long and winds through areas including ESS and Kunskapsparken, on a mix of asphalt and gravel. The relay is part of Innovationsloppet & stafetten, where participants kick off autumn together with an energy boost in a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere. The races celebrate Lund as a city of innovation and are organised in partnership by IFK Lund Friidrott and Ideon Science Park.
course_highlights: The course is approximately 5.4 km and runs from Nobelparken via ESS and Kunskapsparken
A mix of asphalt and gravel, with a flat course and approximately 10 metres of elevation difference
Views of northwestern Lund from a hill in Kunskapsparken
additional: Relay teams can be women's, men's or mixed teams of 2–4 people, and runners may run more than one leg. The start and finish are in Nobelparken in Brunnshög. The relay starts 15 minutes before the individual race. After finishing, participants can choose between a medal or a sausage. The competition area is easily accessible by tram and bus. Teams compete in women's, men's or mixed categories. Each runner runs approximately 5 km.

name: Enköpingsloppet
description: Enköpingsloppet is an annual running festival in Enköping that brings together hundreds of runners from across Sweden. The event offers several distances for runners of all levels, from a children’s race to longer 10 km races, and is a celebration for the whole city. The courses are scenic and flat, with beautiful views of Enköping’s parks and waterfront areas. There is a group warm-up, music and cheering along the course, as well as post-race refreshments with recovery drinks and snacks.
course_highlights: A scenic two-lap course around Drömparken (5.5 km)
A flat, scenic 10 km course through Enköping, officially measured by the Swedish Athletics Association
A water station halfway along the 10 km course, with music and cheering along the way
additional: Group warm-up approximately 15 minutes before each race starts. Post-race refreshments with recovery drinks and snacks for all runners. Results and finish times are available online immediately after finishing. The event area at ENA-vallen’s IP opens at 10:00. Start times: 11:00 Ajabaja Cancer Race (children’s race), 12:30 APC Race (5.5 km), 14:00 ICA Maxi Mile (10 km). Prize ceremonies take place after each race. The event area is located at ENA-vallen’s IP. The official website lists a different race date for 2027 than the stated date of 11 September.

name: Hogialoppet 2026

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Deltagaravgiften är 100 kronor per vuxen vid anmälan till klasserna DAM och HERR

description: Hogialoppet is a fun run in Stenungsund that focuses on the joy of movement and community. Participants can choose to run, jog or walk one of two distances, approximately 3.1 km or 6.5 km. Everyone is welcome, including children, dogs, and participants with strollers or walking poles. The event area offers activities and entertainment for the whole family on race day.
course_highlights: The course is approximately 6.5 km long and runs from Hogia, over Hallerna to Kyrkenorum, and back along Ucklumsvägen
A water station is available after approximately 3 km
The finish is in the event area, where participants are offered water and fruit
additional: The starting field is arranged so that participants with walking poles, dogs or strollers line up farther back to avoid congestion. Race bibs can be collected from 09:00. The event area is open 09:30–13:30 and offers a quiz walk with questions for both adults and children. Participants may bring a stroller, dog or walking poles. For the 2026 race, the adult entry fee is stated to go entirely to BRIS. Dogs, strollers and walking poles are allowed. The race has also included a shorter children's race.

name: Innovationsloppet
organizer: IFK Lund Friidrott och Ideon Science Park
description: Innovationsloppet & the relay is a running event held in Nobelparken in Brunnshög, Lund. The event offers an individual 11 km distance or a relay with 4 legs of 5.5 km each. The course winds through areas such as ESS and Kunskapsparken, offering flat, varied terrain with asphalt and gravel. The event celebrates Lund as a city of innovation and is open to women’s, men’s and mixed relay teams, as well as individual runners. The start and finish are centrally located in Nobelparken, with good public transport connections by tram and bus.
course_highlights: The course is approximately 5.4 km per lap, with two laps for individual runners
The terrain is flat, with approximately 10 metres of elevation difference, and consists of asphalt and gravel
Views over northwestern Lund from a hill in Kunskapsparken
additional: Relay teams consist of 2–4 people and can be women’s, men’s or mixed teams. Teams with fewer than 4 members must have runners complete more than one leg. The relay starts 15 minutes before the individual race. After finishing, participants can choose between a medal and a sausage. The entry fee includes a place in the event, a bib with timing, and a medal or sausage after the finish. Participants choose a medal or sausage when registering.

name: Jentebølgen - Hitra
description: Jentebølgen Hitra 2027 is an inclusive race for girls and women of all ages, taking place on 12 September 2027. The event focuses on achievement, community and a great atmosphere, and aims to create a meeting place filled with energy and the joy of running. The race is held every other year on Hitra and Frøya, and invites participants to a morning of activities and entertainment. The race bib provides entry to the race, including insurance and the ticket fee.
additional: The race bib includes insurance and the ticket fee. The event supports Mental Helse Ungdom with NOK 10 per race bib sold. There is also registration for businesses and sports clubs, with separate prices and terms. NOK 10 from each race bib sold goes to Mental Helse Ungdom. The event venue has not yet been decided.

name: Neskollen løpsfestival 2027
description: Neskollen Running Festival 2027 is Hvam Runners’ signature race, offering a trail run with fantastic views of Romerike. The race is suitable for all levels and includes distances of 4.5 km, 0.5 km, and 1 km for children. The event takes place on September 12, 2027, and offers a great opportunity to enjoy running in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: Trail run on varied terrain
Fantastic views of Romerike
Races for all levels, including children’s races
additional: The race includes distances of 4.5 km, 0.5 km, and 1 km children’s races. The organizer is Hvam IL Friidrett. The starting point is Neskollen. The race is Hvam Runners’ signature event, with a focus on community and the joy of running. Registration is stated to open on June 1, 2027.

name: Mälarömilen
description: Mälarömilen is a recurring running race on Ekerö that welcomes runners of all levels and the whole family. The event offers four different distances, from a children’s race for the youngest runners to the classic 10-kilometre main race. The courses pass through scenic surroundings on paved footpaths and park trails, with the start and finish at Träkvista sports ground. Mälarömilen is organised by Mälarö SOK, and all proceeds go back to the club’s sporting activities.
course_highlights: Pleasant, runner-friendly courses on paved footpaths and park trails
Signs at every kilometre marker
Start and finish at Träkvista sports ground, in scenic surroundings
additional: Late registration is available on race day, subject to availability. There is a drinks station shortly after the start/lap point. Toilets, showers and changing rooms are available in the KOM building at Träkvista sports ground. A first-aid tent is staffed throughout the event. All races start and finish at Träkvista sports ground. Group registration is available for teams and companies.

name: Rådalunken
description: Rådalunken is an annual running and recreational race organized by Lidköpings VSK since the late 1960s. The race takes place in Råda and offers classes and distances of up to 18 km. It is usually held on the second Saturday in September and is a welcome event for runners of all ages. The Paprikaloppet for children is often held on the same day in partnership with Ica Hjertbergs.
course_highlights: Run in scenic Råda
Classes and distances of up to 18 km
Traditionally held on the second Saturday in September
additional: Rådalunken is held together with the Paprikaloppet for children on the same day. The race offers classes and distances of up to 18 km. The event is part of Lidköpings VSK’s annual competition program. Previous editions have offered the Papricaloppet for younger children. Timing has been handled by C-time, and Umara sports drink has been served.

name: Brotorp Trailrun
location: Skogsluffarnas klubbstuga Brotorp, Bagarmossen, Stockholm, Sweden
description: Brotorp Trailrun is a challenging and enjoyable trail race on a technical 7 km loop through the finest parts of Nacka Nature Reserve. The race offers several distances, including a children’s course, 7 km, 14 km and 21 km, with the start and finish at Skogsluffarna’s Brotorp clubhouse in Bagarmossen. The courses offer varied terrain, with trails near lakes and hills, marked with orange ribbons and signs. There are aid stations with water, sports drinks and bananas during the race, and hamburgers are served after the finish to runners in the longer distances. Timing is provided by Sportident, and prizes are awarded to the top three in each category.
course_highlights: Technical 7 km loop marked with orange ribbons and signs
The course passes through the finest parts of Nacka Nature Reserve, with lakes and hills
Aid stations every 3.5 km with water, sports drinks and bananas
additional: Start and finish at the Brotorp clubhouse. Bib pickup takes place on race day at least one hour before the start. Food and refreshments are available at the clubhouse. Timing by Sportident. The time limit for the longest distance is 4 hours; everyone must finish before 14:00. Showers are available, but runners are advised to shower at home. The prize-giving ceremony is planned for approximately 12:30. A discount code is available for children running 7 km (50% discount). Start and finish at Skogsluffarna’s Brotorp clubhouse. According to the organizer, children who register for 7 km get a 50 percent discount with the code “barnrabatt”.

name: Vildmarksmilen
description: Vildmarksmilen is a fun trail race through the beautiful natural surroundings of Hemlingby Outdoor Recreation Area in Gävle. The varied course features changing terrain affected by the weather, making the race challenging but accessible to runners accustomed to narrow trails and off-trail terrain. The start and finish are at Spårcentralen, and the race ends with a substantial climb up the Hemlingbyberget ski slope. For those looking for a bigger challenge, Vildmark15 is recommended, but this race is not held in 2026 due to construction work.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with trails, roots, rocks and marshland
Water station at 5 km and at the finish
Final climb up the Hemlingbyberget ski slope before the finish
additional: Late registration is available on-site until 15 minutes before the start. Bib collection, late registration, the start and the finish are at Hemlingby Spårcentral. Hemlingbystugan is currently closed, and no food or refreshments are served there. Everyone who completes the race receives a medal, and there are performance prizes and raffle prizes. Information about the 2027 edition and course route is not available in the sources. In 2026, an alternative course route was used due to construction work in Hemlingby Outdoor Recreation Area, and Vildmark 15 was not held.

name: Terrengløp i Smidalen
organizer: Nidelv IL Friidrett og Nidelv IL Ski
description: Terrengløp i Smidalen is an accessible cross-country race for children and young people in grades 1–7, organized by Nidelv IL Friidrett og Ski in collaboration with Kjeldsberg Eiendom AS. The race takes place on a circuit of approximately 1,000 meters, with distances adapted to the participants’ grades. Everyone starts together, and the event encourages varied training and competition in an inclusive environment. It is an important offering for children at Nidelv IL and part of the club’s sponsorship agreement. The race is held several times during the year, with the season’s final race on 15 September.
course_highlights: A cross-country circuit of approximately 1,000 meters
Race distance adapted by grade: grades 1–3 (1 lap), grades 4–5 (2 laps), grades 6–7 (3 laps)
All participants start together
additional: The races are held several times a year, with a focus on children and young people at Nidelv IL. Coaches and team leaders are encouraged to prioritize participation over their own training. The event is part of a sponsorship agreement with Kjeldsberg Eiendom AS. Previous race formats had one lap for grades 1–3, two laps for grades 4–5, and three laps for grades 6–7.

name: LöpRallarn
description: LöpRallarn is a running race organized by Bottnaryds IF at Bottnaryds IP. The race offers distances of 7.5 km and 15 km, on a course that includes loops through varied terrain. The event attracts both young people and adult runners and has a wonderful late-summer atmosphere, with energetic participants. The race has a tradition of bringing together a strong field and offers an enjoyable challenge for both competitive and recreational runners.
course_highlights: 7.5 km and 15 km course options with two loops
Varied terrain and surfaces
Start and finish at Bottnaryds IP
additional: The race has two distances: 7.5 km and 15 km. In previous years, the race has had start groups and attracted over 100 participants. Results and contact details are available via christian.wigren@rallarloppet.se. Shorter distances of 1 and 2 km are also available. Bottnaryds IF’s pages list different dates for the 2027 race.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://www.bottnarydsif.se/bottnarydsif-rallarloppen-loprallarn): 2027-09-16 — "RallarLoppen 2027 16 sep" (was estimated 2027-09-05)

name: TronFjellet Ultra 2027
description: TronFjellet Ultra is a challenging, self-navigated mountain ultramarathon of approximately 50 km with 3,000 meters of elevation gain in Østkjolen, Alvdal. The race offers a rugged and technically demanding route with long sections off-trail, steep descents, and exposed high-mountain terrain. Participants must navigate using a GPS track with no course markings, be self-sufficient throughout, and face challenges such as rapidly changing weather and demanding terrain. With a maximum of 25 participants and a 24-hour time limit, this is a race for strong, experienced ultrarunners seeking an iconic mountain challenge in Østerdalen.
course_highlights: Approximately 50 km with 3,000 meters of elevation gain
Self-navigated on unmarked trails, using GPS
Technically demanding mountain terrain with steep descents and exposed sections
additional: Maximum 25 participants. 24-hour time limit. No course markings; the race requires GPS navigation using a GPX track. 100% self-sufficient throughout, with no aid stations or drop bags. Pacers and pets are not allowed. Live tracking for safety. The race is 100% self-sufficient, with no food stations or drop bags, and has a 24-hour time limit. Live tracking; maximum 25 participants. No pacers or pets.

name: BMW Oslo Maraton inkl. NM maraton

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Pris for deltagelse på 10 for Grete er 800 kroner. Administrasjonsgebyr på 6,75% + 3 kr er inkludert i prisen. Engangslisens (50 kr) vil komme i tillegg.

description: DNB Oslo Marathon is one of Norway’s largest road races, with over 29,000 participants, and offers distances for all ages and levels, including the marathon, half marathon, 10 km, and the children’s event Extra Oslo Mini Marathon. The race takes place in central Oslo on a varied course with beautiful city and fjord views. It is an inclusive event with dedicated para categories and a wheelchair race, and places great emphasis on a positive participant experience, with aid stations, pacers, and a wide range of services. The race takes place on September 18, 2027, and has a new registration system for 2027.
course_highlights: The marathon course has approximately 350 metres of elevation gain and consists of two laps of the half-marathon course
The half-marathon course has approximately 175 metres of elevation gain and runs through central Oslo
The 10 km course has approximately 50 metres of elevation gain and is suitable for all levels
additional: There are aid stations approximately every 5 kilometres, with Maxim energy drink and water included in the registration fee. Pacers carrying flags guide runners toward various finish times and provide motivation. Group registration is available, with discounts for groups of at least 10 participants and consolidated invoicing. Cancellation insurance is also available when registering. GPX files for the courses are available to download. Previous editions have also offered the half marathon, 10 km, and Oslotrippelen.

name: BERGAN BYGG Brakvatnet halvmaraton + stafett
description: Bergan Bygg Brakvatnet Half Marathon is a traditional half-marathon organized by Osterøy IL Friidrett. The race takes place around Brakvatnet on Osterøy, on a course of eight laps of 2,595 metres plus 337.5 metres, with the start and finish by the bathing area. The event also includes a relay and a children’s race, and provides changing and toilet facilities as well as food in the finish area. It attracts both recreational runners and competitive athletes, offering beautiful scenery and a challenging course in picturesque surroundings.
course_highlights: The course consists of 8 laps around Brakvatnet plus 337.5 metres to the start/finish
Start and finish by the bathing area at Brakvatnet
Course records: Espen Borge Joensen 1.18,02 (2024) and Hilde Aasheim 1.24,29 (2013)
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:00. Changing tents and toilets for women and men are available in the finish area. Food is served in the finish area, with Vipps as the preferred payment method. Parking is limited; parking at Valestrand school or Valestrandsvatnet is recommended. Cars cannot be driven from the start area. The course is 2,595 metres per lap around Brakvatnet. Previous editions have had the half-marathon and relay start at 12:00. Changing tents, toilets and a dining room are listed in the finish area. Parking is recommended at Valestrand school or the car park at Valestrandsvatnet; it is not possible to drive all the way to Brakvatnet.

name: Bryneløpet
description: Bryneløpet is an annual race organized by Bryne Friidrett for primary school children in grades 1 to 7. It has been held since 2013 and takes place during the Potetfestivalen in Bryne. The race starts between M44 and Brynesenteret and follows a route around the lower part of Fritz Røed Park, covering approximately 400 meters. Participants are divided into groups by age and gender for a safe and enjoyable running experience.
course_highlights: The route starts between M44 and Brynesenteret
Around the lower part of Fritz Røed Park
Approximately 400 meters, with the start and finish in the same place
additional: Participants start in groups by grade and gender: girls and boys in grades 1–2, girls and boys in grades 3–4, and girls and boys in grades 5–7. Race numbers are handed out in the play area at the start/finish. The race is held in connection with the Potetfestivalen. For the 2026 edition, race numbers could be collected outside Jordbærpikene in M44; corresponding practical information for 2027 has not been provided.

name: Sandnes Halvmaraton
description: Sandnes Half Marathon takes place on 18 September 2027, starting and finishing at Bogafjellhallen. The courses are officially measured and offer beautiful scenery around Stokkalandsvatnet, Sandvedparken and Bogafjell, with varied terrain including a steep hill up to Bogafjell Church. The event offers distances for everyone, from a children’s race to a half marathon, with drink stations along the way. It is a great opportunity for both recreational and experienced runners to enjoy the scenic surroundings of Sandnes.
course_highlights: Officially measured 21.1 km course with two laps around Stokkalandsvatnet and Sandvedparken
Steep hill up to Bogafjell Church on the 5 km and children’s race courses
Drink stations after approximately 3 km (for the 5 km and 10 km/half marathon) along the course
additional: You can travel to the start by public transport by taking the train to Ganddal station and walking 30 minutes to Bogafjell, or by taking the bus to Bogafjell. The children’s race starts at 12:00 and can also serve as a warm-up for adults who want to run with the children. The half marathon starts at 13:00. The start location may be adjusted due to work at the venue. Ganddal station and the bus to Bogafjell are the stated public transport options.

name: Fýri Trail by Salomon
description: Fýri Trail by Salomon invites you to a unique trail-running experience in the Norwegian mountains at Fýri Resort in Hemsedal. This race is the final event in the Salomon Golden Trail Nordic Series and offers three distances: 29 km, 18 km, and a 56 km ultra. The race combines demanding technical trails with spectacular scenery, including the challenging “Queen of the Hill” climb and the fast “Max Effort” descent. After the race, participants can celebrate at the “Mud & Champagne” party, creating a social and inclusive atmosphere for all runners.
course_highlights: Queen of the Hill: 3 km technical climb with 550 m of elevation gain
Max Effort: 4 km descent with 600 m of elevation loss
Start just outside Fýri Resort on varied surfaces including asphalt, gravel, and wide trails
additional: The race has two start groups based on expected finish time, with an Elite group for the top 50 men and women starting in a separate wave. Shuttle buses run from Fýri Resort before the start. After the race, the “Mud & Champagne” party features live music and a Superhero Celebration Hour to honour the final runners. Fýri Resort is the festival’s meeting point. The programme may include test runs, talks, an awards ceremony, and the Fýri Trail Party.

name: Ulvøyløpet
organizer: Ulvøy Challenge (Melbu Idrettslag, Stokmarknes Idrettslag og Lekang Ski- og Bygdelag)
description: Ulvøyløpet is a beautiful trail race through Hadseløya’s stunning landscape in the heart of Lofoten and Vesterålen. The race offers two distances, 13 km and 26 km, with varied terrain featuring technical trails, forest roads and open mountain trails. Whether you’re looking for a challenge or a wonderful experience in nature, Ulvøyløpet offers spectacular views and flowing trails that let you pick up the pace. The event has a long tradition and is organised by volunteers in support of local sports clubs and children and young people.
course_highlights: 13 km course with 450 metres of elevation gain, featuring technical and steep trails, forest roads and open mountain trails
26 km course with 1,000 metres of elevation gain and varied terrain, including forest roads, technical trails and mountain landscape
Flowing trails between Moan and Barheia are a highlight of the long course
additional: The recreational class starts between 09:00 and 11:00. Race numbers can be collected at Corner Sport in Stokmarknes or at Stokmarknes Stadium on race day from 08:30. Drop-bag transport from the start to the finish and return transport from Melbu to Stokmarknes after the race are available. There is ample parking at the start and finish, and toilets are available. The café in the finish area is open from 11:00 to 16:30. The prize-giving ceremony takes place at approximately 14:30 at Havfisk Arena, Melbu. The courses are marked with flags and signs, and downloading the GPX file for navigation is recommended. Aid stations offer bananas, cordial, sports drink and water (bring your own cup). Littering along the course is prohibited. A recreational walk along the 13 km course is also available. Walking participants register at Stokmarknes Stadium and may start between 09:00 and 11:00.

name: Bergan Bygg Brakvatnet Halvmaraton
description: Bergan Bygg Brakvatnet Half Marathon is a traditional half-marathon held at Brakvatnet on Osterøy. The course consists of eight laps around Brakvatnet plus an extra 337.5-meter section, with the start and finish at the bathing area. The event also includes a children’s race and a relay. Changing and toilet facilities are available in the finish area, and food is for sale. The race attracts both local and visiting runners and offers a scenic, varied route around the lake.
course_highlights: The course consists of 8 laps around Brakvatnet plus 337.5 meters
Start and finish at the bathing area by Brakvatnet
Scenic course approximately 2 km from Valestrandsfossen on Osterøy
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:00, and the half marathon and relay start at 12:00. There are changing tents and toilets for both women and men in the finish area. Food is for sale in the finish area; Vipps or cash is preferred. Parking is limited, and participants are encouraged to park at Valestrand School or by Valestrandsvatnet. Cars are not driven from the start area. The finish area has changing tents, toilets, and a dining room. Parking is at Valestrand School or the parking lot by Valestrandsvatnet.

name: Løb Mellem Husene i Aalborg SØ 2026
Kung Björn Loppet

price_tiers.distance: Mini Kung Björn (barn upp till 7 år)
Lilla Kung Björn (barn upp till 12 år)
10 km, 6 km och Trail ca 5 km

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Anmälan sista veckan 345 kr för samtliga klasser

description: Kung Björn Loppet is a trail race in Uppsala that welcomes elite runners, recreational runners and children of all ages, with families at its heart. The race is held at OK Linné’s clubhouse and offers several distances, including a children’s race, 6 km, 10 km and a trail race of approximately 5 km. The courses consist of gravel roads, forest trails and asphalt, with water stations along the longer distances. After the race, there is an awards ceremony and a prize draw for participants.
course_highlights: Trail race on gravel roads, forest trails and asphalt
Courses of approximately 10 km and 6 km, plus a trail race of approximately 5 km
Two water stations on the 10 km course and one on the 6 km course
additional: Race bibs with electronic chips can be collected from Löplabbet the day before race day or on race day from 09:00. Changing rooms with showers and toilets are available at the event site, but space is limited. A kiosk sells drinks, hot dogs and baked goods. Start groups are available for the 10 km, with a choice of faster and slower groups. Paid parking is available, but public transport and cycling are recommended. The event includes race-bib collection with electronic chips and an awards ceremony.

name: Kistaloppet
location: Jan Stenbecks torg, Kista, Stockholm, Sweden

tiers.label: tier_1

description: Kistaloppet is a popular running event in Kista, Stockholm, offering races for the whole family, with distances ranging from 400 metres for the youngest participants to 5 km for adults. The race passes through Kista’s distinctive surroundings, including the high-rise buildings of the Million Programme, the green spaces of Järvafältet and the IT cluster that has made Kista known as the Silicon Valley of Northern Europe. The event has a festive atmosphere, with music and entertainment along the course, and an inclusive spirit in which all participants receive a medal. Kistaloppet is organised by Löparakademin, a non-profit organisation that works to promote health and physical activity in suburban communities.
course_highlights: A 5 km measured course through Kista’s Million Programme neighbourhood and green spaces
Start and finish at Jan Stenbecks torg, in central Kista
Entertainment and music stations along the course to keep participants motivated
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the event centre in Kista Galleria, in the premises opposite McDonald’s, on Friday 12:00–18:00 and Saturday 09:15–13:00. Late registration is available on site, subject to availability. There is a water station at the finish. Medical staff will be on site. All participants receive a specially designed medal. Music and DJs along the course create a festive atmosphere. The published information applies to the 2026 edition and does not confirm the date or registration terms for 2027. The 2026 information also lists a 1.6 km untimed Fun Run and children’s races of approximately 1.6 km and 500 metres.

name: Black River Run, 100 miles
location: Västerås SOK clubhouse Orientalen, Västerås, Sweden
description: Black River Run is an ultramarathon in Västerås with several distances: 100 miles (161 km), 50 miles (80.5 km), Instegsultra (48 km), 20 miles (32.2 km) and 10 miles. The start, lap point and finish are at Västerås SOK’s clubhouse, Orientalen, which has changing rooms, showers and a sauna. The course consists of a 10-mile loop with varied surfaces, including technical trails, exercise trails, gravel roads, hiking trails and asphalt. Runners who complete 100 miles within 24 hours receive a belt buckle; other finishers receive a medal.
course_highlights: Varied surfaces: technical trails, exercise trails, gravel roads, hiking trails and asphalt
One loop is 10 miles (16.1 km)
The start, lap point and finish are at Västerås SOK’s clubhouse, Orientalen, which has showers and a sauna
additional: Changing rooms, showers and a sauna are available at the clubhouse. Runners can choose to forgo their medal in favour of Médecins Sans Frontières, with 20 kr donated for each medal declined. The race is organised by Västerås Löparklubb. The easiest way to get in touch is via Black River Run’s Messenger. Orientalen has changing rooms, showers and a sauna. Finishers receive a medal; those who complete 100 miles within 24 hours also receive a belt buckle.

name: Lergöksloppet
description: Lergöksloppet is a running race on trails and forest roads in the beautiful Kronoskogen in Ängelholm, offering a nature-rich and inspiring setting for runners of all ages. After the finish, participants in Class 1 are offered fruit and cordial, while runners in the other classes can enjoy coffee or tea. The race welcomes runners young and old and is marked by a wonderful sense of community in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: The courses follow trails and forest roads
The race takes place in Kronoskogen in Ängelholm
A nature-rich and inspiring setting
additional: After the finish, participants in Class 1 are offered fruit and cordial. Runners in the other classes can enjoy coffee or tea. After the finish, fruit and cordial are served to participants in Class 1; the other classes are offered coffee or tea.

name: Klarälvsloppet Run 21k
description: Klarälvsloppet Run 21K is a fast and scenic half marathon on a gently descending, paved trail from Forshaga Learning Center to Karlstad. The course is completely traffic-free and has no steep climbs, providing ideal conditions for setting personal records. The race follows Klarälvsbanan through the Värmland countryside and offers a unique running experience on 90 kilometers of paved nature trail. There are three official refreshment stations along the course with water and sports drinks, and fruit and refreshments await at the finish. The race starts on Saturday at 10:30, with a group warm-up in the start area.
course_highlights: Gently descending paved trail from Forshaga to Karlstad
Completely traffic-free course with no steep climbs
Three official refreshment stations with water and sports drinks
additional: The start and race-bib distribution take place at Forshaga Learning Center from 09:00 to 10:00 on race day. Participants must finish within the time limit of 2:45. A minibus follows the field and picks up participants who do not meet the time limit. Buses run from Karlstad City Library to the start for those who have purchased bus transport. Fruit and refreshments are available at the finish. On-site payments are accepted only by card or Swish. Medical assistance is available at the start, finish, and refreshment stations. The organizer describes the race as a possible “Scandinavia’s fastest half marathon?”.

description: Lina Roindt is a traditional race organized by Rindal IL, bringing competitive runners, recreational runners, and walkers together for a major family day at Torshall in Bolme, Rindal. The 10.8 km route is on asphalt and forms a loop around Rindal town centre, with a 6.7 km option for the recreational class. The event includes competitive classes for different age groups, an untimed recreational class, and a school cup for grades 5–10. There is an awards ceremony, sprint prizes, prizes for course records, and raffle prizes in the recreational class. Lina Roindt attracts high participation and is known for its great atmosphere and efficient organization.
course_highlights: 10.8 km asphalt route around Rindal town centre
Recreational class with a 6.7 km option via Sunnabrua and Elvepromenaden
Course records are rewarded with NOK 1,000
additional: Start and finish at Torshall in Bolme. Race office at the start. Changing facilities at Rinnvollen Football Stadium. Awards ceremony for competitive classes at 15:00 at Torshall. The recreational class starts between 11:00 and 12:30. The «Bjergpris» sprint prize of NOK 300 is awarded after 2.7 km. One-third of participants receive prizes in each class, including cash prizes for the top three overall, regardless of class. The school cup is for grades 5–10, with a prize for the class with the highest participation. An untimed recreational class and a school cup for pupils in grades 5–10 are offered. The stated distances and practical details apply to previous editions and may change for 2027.

name: Gjesdalmilå
description: Gjesdalmilå is an annual race organized by Gjesdal Idrettslag and held in Ålgård. The event offers distances for children, 5 km and 10 km, as well as a double distance for those who want to run both the 5 km and 10 km. The courses pass through scenic surroundings, with the start and finish at Sentralidrettsanlegget, and feature varied terrain with both easy-running sections and some hills. The event is a natural choice for both recreational and elite athletes in the region and promotes the joy of sport for all ages.
course_highlights: The 5 km course is easy to run, with fewer hills, and consists of several loops around Solås skole and Åfaret.
The 10 km course crosses the E39 through the underpass and follows Edlandsvatnet over varied terrain.
The finish is on the athletics track at the finish line at Sentralidrettsanlegget.
additional: Schedule: The children's race starts at 12:00, the 5 km starts at 12:30, and the 10 km starts at 13:30. The double distance involves running both the 5 km and 10 km. The children's race is 650 metres and takes place in the area around Ålgård Stadion. For 2027, the schedule is: children's race at 12:00, 5 km at 12:30, and 10 km at 13:30.

location: Godøy, Giske, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: Juutuanvaaran kymppi – polkujuoksu Inarissa 2026
location: Juutunvaaran vanha metsä, Inari, Lapland, Finland
description: Juutuanvaaran kymppi on uusi polkujuoksutapahtuma Inarissa, joka tarjoaa elämyksellisiä polkuja eri mittaisina kaikille juoksijoille. Reitti kulkee Juutunvaaran vanhassa metsässä, jossa on vaihtelevaa maastoa mäntykankaista tunturikoivikkoon ja upea näkymä Inarijärvelle. Kilpailu alkaa 20.9.2026 klo 12:00, ja osallistujille on tarjolla kunniapalkintoja sekä muistomitalit. Tapahtuma sopii niin kuntoilijoille kuin kilpaileville juoksijoille, ja osallistujat saavat kisamakkaran ja juoman.

name: Trollhättan City Trail
description: Trollhättan City Trail is a trail race through central Trollhättan that began in 2016. Starting at Folkets Park, the race takes runners through varied terrain, including urban surroundings, hilly trails, stairs and scenic areas such as Kopparklinten, Gamle dal, several locks, Olidan and Kungsgrottan. There are several distances to choose from, from a short, child-friendly Mini Trail to longer, challenging courses of up to 22.5 km. The race also offers start classes for running with a dog on certain distances, making it an inclusive event with a strong sense of community.
course_highlights: A trail race featuring hilly paths and pulse-raising stairways
Passes several locks, Kopparklinten, Gamle dal, Olidan and Kungsgrottan
A mix of urban surroundings and nature experiences
additional: Bib distribution opens at 11:30. Start times: 13:00 for Mini Trail 0.8 km; 14:00 for City Trail 8.5, 14 and 22.5 km; and 14:15 for City Trail 8.5 and 14 km with dogs on a leash. The awards ceremony takes place about 30 minutes after the first finisher crosses the line. The race offers dedicated start groups for running with a dog on a leash in the 8.5 km and 14 km races. Mini Trail is a children’s race for ages 0–12, with no timing or competition. Start and finish at Folkets Park. Previous editions have offered 8.5 km, 14 km and 22.5 km, as well as Trollhättan Mini Trail at approximately 0.8 km. The distances and practical details for 2027 have not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Billingehusloppet
description: Billingehusloppet is a traditional cross-country race dating back to 1966, organized by IFK Skövde Skidor. The race has historically featured varying distances, but since 1993 both men and women have competed over 10.5 km. There are also categories for younger participants, such as Knatteloppet and Lilla Billingehusloppet, as well as a Nordic walking category for recreational participants. Over the years, the race has attracted many well-known Swedish runners and is a popular event in Skövde.
course_highlights: A cross-country race with a rich tradition dating back to 1966
A 10.5 km race for both men and women since 1993
Categories for younger runners and Nordic walking
additional: New categories for younger participants are available, including Knatteloppet and Lilla Billingehusloppet. There is also a Nordic walking category for those who prefer it. Course records are documented for men and women over 10.5 km, as well as for older distances. There is also a Nordic walking category for recreational participants.

name: Coop Linköping Runt
description: Coop Linköping Runt is a popular fun run held in Linköping, starting and finishing at Trädgårdsföreningen. The race offers a pleasant course through the central parts of the city and a great running experience for both recreational and competitive runners. The event is known for its friendly atmosphere and good amenities, including changing rooms, showers and bag drop. It is a traditional autumn race that attracts runners of different ages and abilities.
course_highlights: The course passes through central Linköping, with lovely views
Start and finish at Trädgårdsföreningen
Paved surface with gentle undulations
additional: Changing rooms and showers are available. A bag drop is offered. Food and drink, as well as medical assistance, are available on site. Bib numbers and race confirmations are handled according to the terms and conditions. It is possible to transfer an entry and change category. The race also seeks volunteers.

name: Sicklaloppet
description: Sicklaloppet is Nacka’s big autumn running festival, with races for all ages and ability levels. The main event is a 10 km fun run along the beautiful lakeshores of Sickla and Hammarby Sjöstad, starting and finishing at Sickla Köpkvarter. There is also a 5 km Energiloppet, Lilla Sicklaloppet for children up to 12 years old, and Mini Sickla for the youngest participants. The races offer a scenic, fast course, a great atmosphere and plenty of crowd support. Sicklaloppet is organised by Järla IF Orientering and is a public health event for Nacka and Stockholm.
course_highlights: The course runs along the lakeshores of Sickla and Hammarby Sjöstad
The surface consists of asphalt, gravel and a wooden boardwalk
Start and finish at Sickla Köpkvarter, with spectators and musical entertainment
additional: The event venue opens at 08:00 at Marcusplatsen in Sickla Köpkvarter, with race bib collection and on-site registration. Food trucks and partners will be on site. Lilla Sicklaloppet has start times from 09:15 to 10:15 for different age groups. The Sicklaloppet 5 km starts at 11:45 and the 10 km starts at 13:00. The time limit for the 10 km is 1 hour and 15 minutes, with a cut-off at Kyrkviken after approximately 7.5 km. The course has been officially measured by the Swedish Athletics Association. All races start and finish at Sickla Köpkvarter. The race website describes the 2026 edition; details about the 2027 event format and registration have not been confirmed.

name: Voss Løpskarusell 2027, løp 5
description: Voss Running Series 2027 is an inclusive running series for everyone aged 9 and up, with five races throughout the year. The races are held on Mondays, starting at 19:00, except for the fifth race on 20 September, which starts at 18:30. The course is 5 km long, starting and finishing at Voss Sports Ground, and passes through Prestegardsmoen and along the waterfront promenade. This is a friendly recreational race that welcomes both casual runners and competitive runners.
course_highlights: 5 km course starting and finishing at Voss Sports Ground
Route through Prestegardsmoen
Run along the waterfront promenade
additional: A discount is available when registering for all six races before the second race. Registration for all six races opens on 15 November 2026 and closes on 3 May 2027. Registration for individual races is available via eqtiming.no. The races take place on Mondays. Start time: 18:30. Registration takes place online via EQ Timing. You can register for an individual race or get a discount by registering for all six races before the second race.

name: TCS Lidingöloppet (Lidingöloppshelgen)
distance_verbose: 30 km, 15 km, 10 km, 5 km, 5 km, 1.7 km
description: TCS Lidingöloppet is the world’s largest cross-country race and a much-loved running challenge held annually on Lidingö since 1965. More than 30,000 runners gather during race weekend to run scenic, hilly courses, from short children’s races to the classic 30 km race, a true test of endurance. The race is a world-class celebration of running and a showcase for the joy of movement and public health, with nature always at its heart. Participants can also enjoy a sports expo featuring partners and exhibitors offering inspiration ahead of the race.
course_highlights: A hilly cross-country course featuring flat meadows, gravel roads and steep climbs
The 30 km race has 522 metres of elevation gain and is open for training around the clock before race day
Aid stations along the course offering sports drink, water, pickled cucumber, buns and bananas
additional: The sports expo at Lidingövallen takes place during race weekend, where participants collect their race bibs and can browse offers and expert advice. Free buses run between Ropsten and Lidingövallen during race weekend. Everyone who completes the race receives a medal featuring a unique Carl Milles design. Photographers are stationed along the course and at the finish, with photos available to purchase after the race. The course profile and elevation gains are presented by Garmin, with the PacePro™ feature for pace planning. Aid stations offer sports drink, water, pickled cucumber, buns and bananas. Lidingöloppet encourages environmentally friendly travel by public transport, bicycle or carpooling. Lidingöloppet weekend includes races for different ages and levels, from a 1.7 km children’s race.

name: Birken Gateløp 10 km
description: Birken Street Run in Lillehammer is a running festival in the heart of the city, offering distances of 10 km, 5 km and the BarneBirken Street Run. The race is for everyone, whether you’re chasing a personal best, trying your first 5 km race or looking for an active experience with family and friends. Music, cheering crowds and lively support along the course create a festival atmosphere for both fast runners and those taking a more relaxed pace. The start and finish are centrally located at Sigrid Undsets plass, and the 10 km course follows parts of the historic route of the Olympic Dayrun from the 1980s and 90s.
course_highlights: The course runs through central Lillehammer on paved city streets
The 10 km course follows parts of the former Olympic Dayrun route
Music, bands and cheering crowds bring the course to life
additional: Music, bands, drums, majorettes and a DJ create a lively atmosphere along the course. The race welcomes both fast runners and those who prefer a more relaxed pace. BarneBirken Street Run supports a charitable cause by collecting donations for Right To Play. The 10 km distance is open to participants who turn at least 13 in 2027. The course returns to the finish just south of Mesna Bru.

name: Hagemanns rundbaneløp 2027
description: Hagemanns Backyard Festival 2027 is a unique race held on Svelvik Cycling Club’s loop course. The challenge is to complete a 6.7 km loop within one hour, with a start every hour on the hour from 10:00. Participants who fail to finish within the time limit are eliminated, and the aim is to be the last one standing. A children’s race is also held, and participants can choose to run a single loop at any time. The festival offers medals for all participants, changing rooms, showers and refreshments. Reflective vests and headlamps are mandatory after 21:00.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop course, with a start every hour on the hour
Children’s race of approximately 400–500 metres around the school building
Changing rooms and showers at Ebbestadhallen available all weekend
additional: Reflective vests and headlamps are mandatory from 21:00 to 06:00. Pizza is served to participants at 19:30. The kiosk opens at 08:00 and is run by Svelvik Cycling Club. Buying and selling race bibs is possible. Changing rooms and showers at Ebbestadhallen are available all weekend. Children’s races are held on both Saturday and Sunday at 15:05. A children’s race is also held at Ebbestad Primary School. Information about course distance and elevation gain is from the 2025 edition.

name: Nattland Backyard Ultra
description: Nattland Backyard Ultra is a unique ultramarathon held in Bergen, Vestland. The race consists of multiple laps on a set course, with participants running for as long as they can in an effort to be the last one to finish. The event takes place on Saturday, 25 September 2027, and attracts local and international ultrarunners looking for a challenging and social running experience.
course_highlights: The race takes place on a set course repeated every hour
A demanding ultramarathon focused on endurance and tactics
Held in scenic surroundings in Bergen
additional: Registration is via Eqtiming.no. The race takes place on Saturday, 25 September 2027, in Bergen. No specific start times or price details were found on the available pages. Registration via EQTiming.no.
