description: Gjesdal Trailrun is a true trail race held in beautiful natural surroundings in Ålgård, starting from Gjesdal IL’s athletics facility at Solås. The race mainly follows trails in the terrain northeast of the facility, climbing Kodlifjellet and Håfjellet. It suits both those looking for an enjoyable mountain hike and those who want to compete. Three distances are offered: 10 km, 6 km, and a 1.3 km children’s race. The course follows regular hiking trails that can be challenging, with rocky and slippery sections, so good trail shoes are recommended.
course_highlights: Trail race on paths in the terrain northeast of Gjesdal IL’s athletics facility
The main course climbs Kodlifjellet and Håfjellet
Challenging sections with rocks and slippery areas
additional: Race bib collection opens at 10:00 at the Gjesdal IL clubhouse. The children’s race starts at 11:30. Both timed and untimed starts are available for the 6 km and 10 km distances. The 10 km has a time limit, with participants required to pass Kodlifjellet within approximately 35 minutes and the junction between the 6 km and 10 km courses within 40 minutes. The online registration fee of NOK 20, plus any NFIF one-time licence, is additional. Previous editions have featured 10 km, 6 km, and a 1 km children’s race. Good trail shoes with good grip are recommended. The 2027 distances have not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Neskollen Frontyard 2027

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: inkludert servering av snacks, drikke, frukt og pizza

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Barneløp med inntil 5 runder rundt tjernet

description: Neskollen Frontyard 2027 is a unique race organized by Hvam IL, where participants run 3 km laps that must be completed faster and faster. The race combines competition with a family-friendly, social atmosphere, with indoor breaks at Nes Arena where snacks, drinks, fruit, and pizza are served, included in the price. Frontyard challenges both running capacity and tactics, and prizes are awarded to the best woman, the best man, and the fastest overall time after 15 laps. The start and finish are at Nes Arena, with convenient facilities such as toilets and parking right outside.
course_highlights: 3 km laps that must be run faster with each lap
Start and finish at Nes Arena, with indoor breaks
The course consists of approximately 700 meters of gravel, with the rest on asphalt
additional: Snacks, drinks, fruit, and pizza are included in the price. The start, finish, and breaks are indoors at Nes Arena, with 12 toilets and parking right outside. The course consists of approximately 700 meters of gravel, with the rest on asphalt. Remember to wear your race bib visibly on the outside of your clothing. The children's race starts at approximately 10:01. Previous editions have served snacks, drinks, fruit, and pizza during breaks at Nes Arena.

name: Täby Halvmarathon
description: Täby Half Marathon is a fast, easy-to-run half marathon in scenic surroundings, starting and finishing at Näsby Castle. The course offers coastal views along the shores of Värtan, a scenic loop around Lake Rönninge, and a finish back by the sea with views towards Bogesundlandet. The course is officially measured and the race is organized by Täby IS Friidrott. It is ideal for runners looking to end the season on a fast and beautiful course. The race has been very popular in previous years, with limited places, so the organizers encourage early registration.

name: Täljemilen
description: Enhörna IF presents Täljemilen—perhaps autumn’s fastest officially measured 10K, at Geneta Sportfält in Södertälje. The course runs entirely on cycle paths and footpaths and is fully paved, making it very fast and suitable for those chasing a personal best. Water is available at 5 km and at the finish. Instead of medals, the organizer donates a sum to the Swedish Childhood Cancer Fund for every registered runner. Prizes are awarded to the top 3 in both the women’s and men’s categories, and there is also a draw for approximately 20 prizes.

name: Skövdeloppet
description: Skövdeloppet makes a comeback in 2026 with a new, city-adjacent course that mainly follows walking and cycling paths through several of Skövde’s residential areas. Race day is October 18, and the races are designed as easy-to-run urban courses suitable for both recreational and competitive runners. Three distances are offered (21.1 km, 10 km and 5 km), with a shared start and finish at Lillegårdens Fritidsområde.

name: Necon Vinterkarusell 27-28 løp 1 (18. okt)
description: Necon Winter Series is a winter running series consisting of 8 races held at Fana Stadium in Bergen from November to April. The races have a mass start and offer two distances, 5 km and 10 km. Participants can choose their distance during the race at the turnaround point. The start and finish are at Fana Stadium, and the races follow varied terrain, with intermediate times available along the way. The series is suitable for both recreational and experienced runners looking for a social and challenging winter series.
course_highlights: Mass start for the 5 km and 10 km, with the option to choose a distance during the race
The course starts at Fana Stadium, with turnarounds at Sandsli and Plantasjen in Kokstad
Intermediate times are recorded at 2.5 km, 5 km and 7.5 km for the different distances
additional: Start and finish at Fana Stadium from 18:45. Start waves are based on expected finish times to avoid crossing Grimseidvegen. Wave 0 starts at 18:45 for 10 km runners expecting to finish in over 55 min. Wave 1 starts at 19:00 for 5 km runners expecting to finish in under 22:30 min and 10 km runners expecting to finish in under 45 min. Waves 2–4 start at 2-minute intervals, based on expected finish times. Participants register for the 5 km when signing up; the distance is chosen automatically during the race at the turnaround point.

name: Älvsjöloppet night trail
location: Gamla Älvsjö IP, Älvsjö, Stockholm, Sweden
price_range: 250 kr; gratis för medlemmar i OK Älvsjö-Örby
description: Älvsjöloppet Night Trail is an exciting 5 km evening race through hilly terrain in Älvsjöskogen, with 150 metres of elevation gain. The start and finish are at Gamla Älvsjö IP, about a 15-minute walk from Älvsjö station. The course is marked with reflective markers and requires a bright headlamp, preferably at least 1,000 lumens, as well as good trail shoes to handle the terrain. After the finish, all runners are offered a sausage and a drink in a friendly atmosphere. The race is organised by OK Älvsjö Örby and is open to everyone, with free entry for club members.
course_highlights: 5 km reflective-marked course through hilly terrain, with 150 m of elevation gain
Start and finish at Gamla Älvsjö IP, near Älvsjö station
Requires a bright headlamp and trail shoes with good grip
additional: Race bibs and timing chips are handed out from 18.15 to 18.45. The chip must be returned at the finish. Toilets and changing rooms are available at the venue. Parking is available in the area and at Herr Stens väg 2, but walking, cycling or running to the start is recommended. Live results and the results list are available at alvsjoloppet.se. Sausages and drinks are offered to all runners after the finish; no other refreshments are available. The start and finish are at Gamla Älvsjö IP. The organiser's published information applies to 2026 and does not give confirmed details for 2027. For 2026, a headlamp of at least 1,000 lumens and trail shoes, preferably with metal studs, are recommended.

name: Rosa Sløyfe-løpet Oslo lørdag
organizer: Kreftforeningen og Brystkreftforeningen, i samarbeid med Springtime Group
price_range: 500 kr + 30 kr i administrasjonsgebyr og 3 % transaksjonsgebyr; Mini er gratis

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Distanse: Kort løype - Lørdag 23. okt - kl. 12.00 Deltakere kr 500,00 + Adm. gebyr (30 NOK + 3%)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Distanse: 5 KM - Søndag 24. okt - kl. 12.00 Deltakere kr 500,00 + Adm. gebyr (30 NOK + 3%)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Distanse: 10 KM - Søndag 24. okt - kl. 14.00 Deltakere kr 500,00 + Adm. gebyr (30 NOK + 3%)

description: Rosa Sløyfe-løpet Oslo is an annual race held in support of the Pink Ribbon campaign. On Saturday, the event offers a short untimed course from Nedre Foss gård to Nydalen. On Sunday, participants can choose between timed 5 km and 10 km races, starting and finishing at Rådhusplassen. The course passes through some of Oslo’s most iconic areas, including Aker Brygge, Tjuvholmen and Akershus Fortress, offering an urban and atmospheric experience. The event is for everyone, whether you want to race for a time, run with colleagues or simply be part of the sea of pink.
course_highlights: Course through Aker Brygge, Tjuvholmen and Akershus Fortress
Start and finish at Rådhusplassen in central Oslo
Urban, atmospheric course with beautiful views
additional: Saturday’s short course is untimed and suitable for anyone looking for a more relaxed experience. The race packet includes a race bib, neck warmer, bag and medal. Pacers will be available for Sunday’s 5 km and 10 km races at different paces to help participants maintain a steady speed. Race bibs can be collected in advance or from two hours before the start on race day. Participants are insured through a licence provided by the Norwegian Athletics Federation, and half of the entry fee goes directly to the Pink Ribbon campaign. Timing is available for the 5 km and 10 km. The free Mini Run, approximately 400 metres, is for children aged 3 to 9. The participant package includes a race bib, neck warmer, bag and medal.

name: Bergen Maraton- Maratonkarusellen
organizer: Maratonkarusellen i samarbeid med BFG Bergen Løpeklubb

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Prisene øker med kr 50,- to uker før løpsdagen

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Prisene øker med kr 50,- to uker før løpsdagen

description: Bergen Marathon will be held for the 40th time on Saturday, October 23, 2027, with the start and finish at Fana Stadium in Bergen. The race is part of Maratonkarusellen, which offers both full and half marathons, and aims to ensure that all participants enjoy themselves despite the challenges of the race. Maratonkarusellen works with BFG Bergen Running Club and places great emphasis on the quality of its events. The minimum age for the marathon is 18.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Fana Stadium
Events include both full and half marathons
Organized in collaboration with BFG Bergen Running Club
additional: Kondis members receive a NOK 50 discount. A year-round license from the Norwegian Athletics Federation can be provided to avoid the one-time license fee. Participants without a license must purchase a one-time license. The minimum age for the marathon is 18. The event offers a half marathon and a marathon. The minimum age for the marathon is 18. Listed prices apply to the 2026 edition and may change before the 2027 race.

name: Backyard Sandefjord Ultra

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Backyard Deltakere kr 750,00 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3% transaksjonsgebyr)

description: Backyard Sandefjord is a unique ultrarun being held for the 14th time in 2027. The race consists of a gently rolling loop of approximately 6.7 km, run on the hour every hour, with a maximum of 12 loops in total. Participants must start each loop to continue, and the last runner to start the final loop is declared the winner. The event has a social atmosphere and a low barrier to entry, with facilities including snacks, hot drinks and places to rest in the hall. Everyone who completes 12 loops receives a cup, and those who reach the ultradistance receive a Norwegian-made wooden medal.
course_highlights: Gently rolling loop of approx. 6.7 km
The course is marked with yellow arrow signs, red marker flags and white arrows on asphalt
Maximum of 12 loops, totalling 80.4 km if completed
additional: Bringing your own cup, headlamp and reflective vest is mandatory. Bib collection is Friday 17:00–18:30 and Saturday 08:30–09:30. Support is allowed outdoors only. Snacks, coffee, sweet tea, broth, cold/hot water and hot dogs are offered after the 7th loop. Participants must bring their own chair; there is no room for sun loungers. Enter through the large gate at the back of the hall; parking is available. Start and finish at Runarhallen, Klavenesveien 20. Maximum 350 participants. Bringing your own cup, headlamp and reflective vest is mandatory. Snacks, coffee, sweet tea, broth and water are offered.

name: Fredrikstad Multiconsult Maraton 2027
description: The Fredrikstad Multiconsult Marathon takes place in Fredrikstad and consists of three identical 14 km laps, followed by an extra 195-metre finishing section so that the kilometre markers are in the same place on each lap. The course starts and finishes at FIF-huset and includes asphalt, gravel and forest roads in Fredrikstadmarka. There are aid stations along the route with water, squash and sports drink, as well as cola and bananas on the final laps. The race has been held since 2001 and offers a varied, scenic course with marshals at important intersections.
course_highlights: The course consists of three 14 km laps, plus an extra 195 metres to ensure the kilometre markers are in the same place on each lap
The first half is on asphalt; the rest is on gravel and forest roads in Fredrikstadmarka
Three aid stations per lap with a range of drinks and food
additional: An early start at 10:00 is available for runners who expect to take more than 5 hours. The race office and bib collection open at 09:00 on race day at FIF-huset. Parking is at Stjernehallen, about a 5-minute walk from the start/finish. Changing rooms and toilets are available at FIF-huset. There are no pacers during the race. Online registration is open until 1 hour before the start. There are three aid stations per lap. The race office, changing rooms and toilets are at FIF-huset; parking is at Stjernehallen.

name: Snipsøyrvatnet Rundt
price_range: 100–200 kr, i tillegg til eingongslisens for dei utan heilårslisens

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Startavgift: 200kr for senior (født på eller før 31.12.2005)

description: Snipsøyrvatnet Rundt is one of Sunnmøre’s most traditional recreational races, organised by Hareid IL. The race goes around Snipsøyrvatnet, starting at Ward1 in Bjåstad, and marks the beginning of the autumn season. Participants register at Hareid Clubhouse before the race and can warm up with a 3 km jog to the start area. The race is open to both seniors and juniors, with a friendly and inclusive atmosphere.
course_highlights: The race goes around Snipsøyrvatnet
Start and finish at Ward1 in Bjåstad
A 3 km warm-up jog from registration to the start
additional: Registration takes place at Hareid Clubhouse from 12:00 to 13:45. Participants must make their own way from registration to the start area, either with a 3 km warm-up jog or by car. Changing facilities are available at Hareid Clubhouse. A one-time licence from the Norwegian Athletics Federation is an additional cost for those without an annual licence for road running. Parking is available at Ward1, Bigset Bedehus or Kulturoasen. Start time is 14:00; participants must make their own way approximately 3 km from registration to the start.

name: KNÆK CANCER LØBET AABYBRO 2026 & ØLAND AFD.
location: Aabybro, Jammerbugt Municipality, North Jutland, Denmark

name: Sydvest Crossløb 2026/27 - afd. 1 - Brørup ved Aquagain
Yxbacken Extreme Challenge by E2C
description: Yxbacken Extreme Challenge by E2C is one of Östergötland’s most unique and challenging running races, held at the foot of Pernilla Wiberg’s home slope in Yxbacken, Norrköping. The race challenges participants with five laps up a hill with 100 metres of elevation gain over 350 metres, for a total distance of approximately 7 kilometres. Whether you run fast or take it easy, everyone is welcome to take part, and the most important thing is to make it to the top. New this year is also a relay, adding an extra dimension to the race. Children can take part for free in the Lilla Yxbackenloppet by E2C, making it a family-friendly running festival.
course_highlights: Five laps up Yxbacken, with 100 metres of elevation gain over 350 metres per lap
Approximately 7 kilometres in a unique race setting in Östergötland
Start at the foot of Pernilla Wiberg’s home slope
additional: Race bibs can be collected at XXL on Friday 23 October from 14:00 to 18:00, or at the start and finish area no later than one hour before the start. The bib includes a timing chip, which must be used to record your time. All participants who cross the finish line receive a medal sponsored by Energi & Inneklimat. Companies can rent a partner tent at the race venue for team spirit and exposure through Rent a Tent. E2C was title partner for the fourth year in the 2024 edition.

name: VSM terräng

late_fee.price: 530 kr för seniorer och veteraner, 430 kr för juniorer och ungdomar

description: The Swedish Cross Country Championships are organised by Västerås FK and the Swedish Athletics Federation at Rocklunda IP in Västerås. The course is 2 km long and consists mostly of grass, with some other surfaces, including fast-running grass and gravel paths. The competition includes several categories, including seniors, youth, masters and para-athletes, with individual races and team competitions. The event also offers the option of pre-booked lunch and good accommodation options close to the venue.
course_highlights: 2 km course consisting mostly of grass, with some other surfaces
Fast-running grass and a 2–3-metre-wide gravel path, crossed four times per lap
Hay-bale obstacles on parts of the course
additional: Race numbers must be collected at the start/finish area at least 60 minutes before the start. Access to the start area opens 10 minutes before the start and closes 2 minutes before. Water is available at the lap point and finish, with Dextrosol at the finish. Changing rooms and showers are available at Expandia Arena. Free parking and local buses are available. Clubs may set up their own tents in the designated area. Pre-booked lunch is served at Good Morning Hotels near the venue. Doping tests may be conducted during the competition weekend. The 2026 event took place at Rocklunda IP in Västerås. The organiser’s website states that Västerås FK handed over hosting duties for the 2027 Swedish Cross Country Championships to Mora.

name: Linghem Dark Halfyard (Ultra) Trail
description: Welcome to the second edition of Linghem Dark Halfyard (Ultra) Trail, a unique and exciting running event in the autumn darkness of Kråksångsskogen. The race consists of 13 laps on a 3.5 km loop, with a maximum of 30 minutes allowed for each lap. After the sixth lap, runners change direction, adding an extra dimension to the competition. This is a small-scale race with a limited number of places, and a headlamp is mandatory because almost the entire race takes place in the dark. All participants who complete at least one lap receive a beautiful wooden medal, and the winners receive unique winner’s medals.
course_highlights: 13 laps on a 3.5 km loop, with a maximum of 30 minutes per lap
Running direction changes after the sixth lap
The course is marked with reflective markers and trail tape; the surface is mostly trails, with approximately 700 metres of gravel
additional: Energy is served during laps 7 and 8 (pizza from a local pizzeria), along with sweets, bananas, crisps, coffee, hot broth, sports drink and water. Facilities are very limited, with self-service energy, a warm fire and approximately 25 sq m of covered shelter. Toilets are outdoors in the forest. Maximum 70 places. Each lap starts every 30 minutes, and anyone who completes a lap faster can rest for the remaining time before the next lap starts. A headlamp and mobile phone are listed as mandatory equipment. The race website lists 70 places.

name: Halloween Night Trail
location: Friluftscentrum Karlsnäs, Ronneby, Blekinge County, Sweden
description: Halloween Night Trail is an exciting trail race in the dark in the Karlsnäs area north of Ronneby, with distances of 2 km, 5 km and 10 km. The race offers a unique Halloween atmosphere, with themed features such as Zombie Hill, Count Dracula’s lair and the Bat Cave along the course. The venue is at Friluftscentrum Karlsnäs, where the finish is indoors. After the race, grilled hamburgers and drinks are served and included in the entry fee. The race is organised by Ronneby Orienteering Club, which has extensive experience organising major orienteering competitions.
course_highlights: Run along small trails and through terrain, with reflectors showing the way in the dark
Themed features such as Zombie Hill, the Cemetery, Count Dracula’s lair and the Bat Cave
The finish area is indoors at Karlsnäs outdoor recreation centre
additional: Electronic timing for 5 km and 10 km; no timing for 2 km. Race bibs and timing chips can be collected from 17:00 at the venue. Freshly grilled hamburgers and drinks are served after the race and are included in the entry fee. The prize-giving is provisionally scheduled for 20:45. Shoes with good grip and a headlamp are recommended. Parents may run with children in the 2 km race without registering. A specially designed medal is given to all participants. The entry fee includes a hamburger and a drink. Electronic timing is available for the 5 km and 10 km distances, but not the 2 km. The finish area is indoors.

name: Ottestad løpsfestival
description: Ottestad Running Festival is organized by Ottestad Idrettslag and consists of three races: HOKA Ottestad Rundt over 17 kilometers, the Spenst Run over 5 kilometers, and the Sport1 Sprint for children, with distances of 400 meters, 1 km, and 1.8 km. The race starts and finishes at Ottestad Idrettspark, which has excellent facilities, including a café, refreshments, changing rooms, and showers. The course follows Ottestadstien, a scenic hiking trail through a cultural landscape of wooded areas and farmland, with beautiful views of Mjøsa. The event is family-friendly and offers both timed and recreational races.
course_highlights: The course follows Ottestadstien through a cultural landscape of wooded areas and farmland
Fantastic views of Mjøsa during the race
Start and finish at Ottestad Idrettspark, with a café and changing-room facilities
additional: The HOKA Sprint is a separate 430-meter segment on the 17 km course where participants can compete to be the fastest on Strava and win HOKA shoes. The segment has its own refreshment station, music, and spectators. A one-time race license is an additional cost for those without an annual license, and athletes up to age 12 are covered by NIF's child sports insurance. The 5 km and 17 km races can be run with or without timing. Listed prices apply to 2026, and a one-time race license is an additional cost where applicable.

name: Norgestesten 2027 3
description: Norgestesten is an efficient and inclusive running event held at Jessheim Athletics Stadium. The event offers distances ranging from an 800-metre children’s race to a half marathon, all with a mass start on a flat, fast 3,146-metre loop course. Many experienced pacers help participants find the right pace, and the event emphasizes convenient logistics, with parking and the train station nearby. Proceeds support sports for children and young people, and race bibs can be collected via self-service from 09:00 on race day.
course_highlights: Flat 3,146-metre loop course
Mass start for all distances
Many experienced pacers available
additional: The children’s race starts at 09:30 and is approximately 800 metres. Race bibs can be collected via self-service from 09:00 in the start area. Toilets are available at Jessheim Athletics Stadium and in the ice rink and multipurpose hall. A table for participants’ own drinks is provided at the start, along with water and sports drink along the course. The half-marathon cut-off is 2 hours and 30 minutes. The race is organized by volunteers, and proceeds support sports for children and young people. Information about dates and distances relates to different editions; the 2027 edition has not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Sønderjysk Crossløb 2026/27 - Cup tilmelding alle løb
Yddingeloppet
description: Yddingeloppet is one of Skåne’s largest cross-country races, held in the beautiful and challenging terrain of Bokskogen, Torup, outside Malmö. The race always takes place on the last Sunday in October, starting and finishing at Torups Friluftsgård. There are recreational 6 km and 12 km races, as well as a 6 km walk/power walk, and competitive classes for different ages, including veterans’ classes. All participants receive a race bib with a timing chip and a medal at the finish. Prizes are awarded to the top finishers in the competitive classes, and winners in the veterans’ classes have their prizes sent to them.
course_highlights: Cross-country race in autumn-coloured Bokskogen, Torup
Two distances: 6 km and 12 km
Start and finish at Torups Friluftsgård
additional: Race bibs with timing chips are provided to all entrants except those taking part in the walk and power walk. Bibs can be collected at the race office during the week before the race or on race day from 8:30 a.m. until one hour before the start. Prize-giving for places 1–3 in the women’s and men’s 6 km and 12 km competitive classes is at approximately 12:30 p.m. The start and finish area has parking and good public transport connections via buses 150 and 148. Carpooling is recommended. The race has previously been held in late October. The date and practical information for 2027 have not been confirmed in the available information.

name: Sjögarpslunken 2026
description: Sjögarpslunken is a long-running running race celebrating its 50th anniversary in 2026. The race is organized by Boxholm-Ekeby Ski Club and takes place at Boxholm ski stadium. It is a popular event for runners of all ages and abilities, with a scenic and challenging course. More information and registration will be available closer to race day.
course_highlights: Scenic route around the Sjögarp area
Challenging 14 km course with a course profile available
The race takes place at Boxholm ski stadium
additional: The race celebrates its 50th anniversary in 2026. Links to the invitation, race information, start list and preliminary results from previous years are available. A course profile and map are available for runners. The race celebrates its 50th anniversary in 2026. The gathering is scheduled for 09:30.

name: Hindås Trail
description: Hindås Trail is a running festival held on beautiful recreational trails in Hindås. Participants can choose between a 1 km race for children and 5 km or 15 km races for adults. It is a competition for those who want to run fast, and an enjoyable run for those who prioritise the experience. At the finish, participants are served coffee and chocolate biscuits, and hot dogs and an enhanced fika are also available for purchase. All proceeds go directly to the popular skiing activities in Hindås.
course_highlights: Beautiful recreational trails in Hindås
A 1 km children’s race on an easier course
A choice of 5 km or 15 km distances
additional: At the finish, participants are served coffee and chocolate biscuits. Hot dogs and an enhanced fika are available to buy at a good price. All proceeds from Hindås Trail go directly to the skiing activities. Coffee and chocolate biscuits are included after finishing. Hot dogs and an enhanced fika have been available for purchase. The proceeds go to Hindås Ski Club’s skiing activities.

name: Löfstad Slott Trail
description: Löfstad Castle Trail is an atmospheric trail race held in the autumn darkness around the historic Löfstad Castle. The race offers a unique running experience as participants run through the castle park, along forest trails and over unmarked terrain lit by headlamps. The event consists of two races: the Little Twilight Race for children in the park and Löfstad’s Darkest, a 7-kilometre night race for adults. Löfstad Castle Trail combines nature, history and community in a beautiful and challenging setting.
course_highlights: 7 km night race on gravel roads, trails and unmarked forest terrain
The course is marked with reflectors and course tape
Little Twilight Race: 1,000 metres in the park, with no timing
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 15:00 at the castle courtyard. Löfstad’s Darkest starts at 17:00 and requires a headlamp and trail shoes. The Little Twilight Race is a children’s race with no timing, and all participants receive a prize. The joint awards ceremony takes place after the races. On-site registration is available. Parking is available up to 500 metres from the castle. A headlamp is mandatory for the 7 km race, and trail shoes are recommended. The children’s race is untimed. The start and finish are at Löfstad Castle.

name: Kullamannen by UTMB
description: Kullamannen by UTMB is an adventure race along the rocky shores of Kullaberg and the Bjäre Peninsula on Sweden’s southwest coast. The races range from 22 km to 100 miles and offer challenging terrain through rocky hills, beech forests, and coastal trails. This is a tough and scenic trail-running experience that attracts adventurous runners from around the world. The races are part of the UTMB World Series and offer a unique combination of technical trails and spectacular views.
course_highlights: Technical singletrack on Kullaberg
Passage through 15 nature reserves and two hills (Ultra 100 Miles)
Coastal trails and beech forests along the Bjäre Peninsula
additional: The start and finish for Ultra 100 Miles and Sprint Ultra are in Höganäs, with bib pickup in Båstad. Drop bags are provided and can be collected at specific aid stations and after the finish. It is possible to transfer a registration to a shorter distance up to three weeks before the race. Minimum age varies by race, and parental consent is required for minors taking part in North Shore 20K. The event also includes an extensive schedule of activities during the week before the races. The race lineup includes, among others, 20K, 50K, 100K, and 100 miles. For the 100-mile race, bib pickup takes place at the EXPO in Båstad.

name: Kullamannen 100 miles
description: Kullamannen 100 miles is an extremely challenging A+ 100-mile race that takes you through 15 scenic nature reserves and two mountains in Skåne. The race starts in Höganäs and the course includes technical singletrack on Kullaberg, one of Sweden’s most popular nature reserves. After 66 kilometres, runners can refuel with hot soup before continuing north towards Ängelholm and Torekov, with the finish in Båstad. The race is known for its high DNF rate of 40–60% and the tough weather conditions in November, with Scandinavian coastal winds and long hours of darkness.
course_highlights: Passes through 15 nature reserves and two mountains
Technical singletrack on Kullaberg Mountain
Starts in Höganäs and finishes in Båstad, with a chance to refuel after 66 km
additional: The race starts in Höganäs, with buses departing from Båstad. Race bibs must be collected in person at the Expo in Båstad. Drop bags are provided and can be collected at the Båstad Aid Station and after the finish. Drop bags must be collected within two hours after the race ends. Bib collection by proxy is not permitted. The race is part of the UTMB World Series. Bibs must be collected in person at the EXPO in Båstad, with valid ID and a QR code. Participants receive an official UTMB World Series drop bag.

name: Walking Dead Ultra 100 Miles
description: Walking Dead Ultra 100 Miles is a challenging ultramarathon held in Paradiset Nature Reserve in Huddinge. The race offers a unique terrain experience, with scenic views and technical trails that test both endurance and mental strength. It is a well-regarded event for experienced ultrarunners seeking a long-distance challenge in a beautiful setting.
course_highlights: Running in Paradiset Nature Reserve with varied terrain
Technical trails and scenic views
A challenging 100-mile distance
additional: The race also offers 100 km and 65 km distances. According to the available race information, drop bags and toilets are available, along with water, tea, coffee and broth at Torpet Paradiset.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, halvmaraton
description: Perseløpet is a race focused on fast times, held at Ås school in Eidsvoll. The race takes place on a flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop, where participants can set out their own bottles and gels on their personal nutrition table. Seven distances are offered, from 3 km to 100 km, including 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon. Race numbers are collected from a self-service station at the school, and the venue has good facilities, including changing rooms, toilets and free parking. The race has a friendly atmosphere, with personal records celebrated by the ringing of a bell at the finish area.

Participants’ own nutrition tables along the course
Good venue facilities, including changing rooms, toilets and free parking
additional: Race numbers are collected from a self-service station about two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. The race uses a lap-time calculator to plan split times. At selected races, the 9th grade class at Feiring school staffs an official drinks station to raise money for their school trip. The weather forecast is updated four times a day using satellite data for the area around Ås school. Public transport to the venue is available by train and bus, with real-time departures. Race numbers are collected from a self-service station at the school from about two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. description: HA Ottestad Running Festival is an annual event held at Ottestad Idrettspark, with the start and finish in the same place. The festival consists of three races: HOKA Ottestad Rundt (17 km), the Spenst Race (5 km), and the Sport1 Sprint for children, with distances of 400 m, 1 km, and 1.8 km. The course follows Ottestadstien, a scenic walking trail winding through a cultural landscape of wooded areas and farmland, with splendid views over Lake Mjøsa. The event offers good facilities, including a café, food and refreshments, changing rooms, and showers in the clubhouse.

Start and finish at Ottestad Idrettspark, with good facilities

Athletes up to age 12 are covered by NIF’s child sports insurance. The festival features HOKA Ottestad Rundt (17 km), the Spenst Race (5 km), and the Sport1 Sprint for children. description: Fagerstrand Backyard Ultra Marathon 2026 is organized by Fagerstrand IF at Myklerud, Fagerstrand. name: Guldfeber Aarhus — Golden Fever #1
description:
Gold Fever — Denmark’s first SplitRace tournament. A free running game in the streets of Aarhus: 12 segments (0.4–1.9 km) are mapped around the city, and 7 of them form a hidden “golden chain” — nobody knows which ones, or in what order. Find them. Run them. Chase the times.

No mass start and no entry fee: run whenever you want, as often as you want, throughout 17 October – 1 November. The app measures your times via GPS. You earn points for each golden segment based on how close you are to the fastest time — women are scored against the fastest woman, men against the fastest man. Extra points go to the first runners to unlock a golden segment — and the tournament’s biggest bonus goes to the first to complete the whole chain in the correct order.

This is the first edition — a pilot for a maximum of 30 runners. Your feedback will shape the game.

(EN: A free city-wide running game in Aarhus. 12 segments, 7 of them secretly form a golden chain — find them and beat the clock. No mass start: run anytime 17 Oct – 1 Nov. Free entry, GPS timing in the SplitRace app. First edition, 30 pilot spots.)
additional: No start line and no start groups — all segments are on public, lit routes around Aarhus, and you can run them whenever you want during the event window. Participation requires the free SplitRace app (iOS / Android) — download it via splitrace.app, join the “Guldfeber Aarhus” tournament, and all 12 segments will appear on your map. Limited to the first 30 runners. Open streets: follow normal traffic rules. Questions? Write to support@splitrace.app or Instagram https://www.instagram.com/split_race/

description: Jämjöhalvan is a mass-participation race organized by Team Blekinge LF, with distances ranging from a children’s race to a half marathon, as well as a relay (Jämjöhallenstafetten). The half marathon and other races take place on a fast, spectator-friendly loop course around Jämjö and can also be used as qualifying races for events such as Göteborgsvarvet. The event centre and finish are at Jämjö Kunskapscentrum, and in 2026 the Swedish Veterans Championships in the half marathon will be held alongside the race. Runners of all abilities are welcome—the event emphasizes running community and clearly marked laps.

additional: The start, finish and event centre are at Jämjö Kunskapscentrum. Start locations vary by distance. The half marathon and Jämjöhallenstafetten start at 10:30, the 10 km at 10:40, the 5 km at 10:45 and the children’s race (500 m) at 12:45. Runners must keep to the right and pass on the left; runners who are not running at a fast pace are asked to keep right. In the relay, teams hand over a baton in the exchange area near the lap point; late registration is not available for Jämjöhallenstafetten. Late registration for other distances is open on race day from 08:00 to 10:00 at Jämjö Kunskapscentrum. Payment is accepted in cash or via Swish. Start times: 21.1 km and Jämjöhallenstafetten 10:30, 10 km 10:40, 5 km 10:45, 5 km youth class (ages 12–16) 10:45, children’s race 12:45. Start locations vary by distance. There is no late registration for Jämjöhallenstafetten. The start and finish are at Jämjö Kunskapscentrum. The course is a loop with water stations every 5 km, in cooperation with Umara. Changing facilities and showers are available at Jämjö Kunskapscentrum from approximately 09:00. Free open training sessions are held on 17 September and 15 October before race day.

name: Skanneloppet
price_range: Fram till 7 oktober: 17,3 km 200 kr; 7,6 km 150 kr; 3,9 km 100 kr. 8 oktober – 24 oktober: 17,3 km 300 kr; 7,6 km 200 kr; 3,9 km 150 kr. 25 oktober – 5 november: 17,3 km 400 kr; 7,6 km 300 kr; 3,9 km 250 kr.
description: Skanneloppet is organised by IS Skanne and takes place on Saturday, 7 November 2026, starting and finishing at Tingvalla Nöjespalats in Åstorp. The race is run individually, with approximately ten runners starting per minute, and offers three courses for both elite runners and recreational participants. The courses are hilly and run mostly on gravel roads, with sections of asphalt and off-road trails. The race is suitable for both young and old. Information about registration and start lists will be published on the organiser’s website.
course_highlights: Three distances: Red 17.3 km, Blue 7.6 km and Green 3.9 km
Hilly terrain—mostly gravel roads, with sections of asphalt and off-road trails; particularly hilly at the beginning
Water stations are marked on the map (yellow circles)
additional: Bib collection from 08:00 on race day; find your bib number in the start list inside Tingvalla and collect it yourself. No on-site registration. Registration closes on 5 November. Those who register before 24 October will have their name printed on their bib. Start times are between 10:00 and approximately 11:05, with around ten runners starting per minute. The courses are hilly; the 17.3 km and 7.6 km courses include sections of off-road trails, asphalt roads and gravel roads, while the 3.9 km course is entirely on gravel roads and off-road trails. No showers or changing facilities; toilets are available. A commemorative plaque is awarded to everyone who finishes; commemorative medals are awarded after 5, 10, 20, 30 and 40 completed races. Contact: skanneloppet@isskanne.se, Diana Nilsson 070-847 73 47, Torbjörn Persson 0702-90 23 40.

images.alt_text: IS Skanne-logotyp från inbjudan till Skanneloppet.
Löpare vid start och mål för Skanneloppet i Åstorp.

name: Höstrusket
description: Höstrusket is a trail and road race in Norra Djurgården, Stockholm, taking place on 7 November 2026. Choose from 10 km, half marathon (21.1 km) or marathon (42.195 km), with the start and finish at Fisksjöängsvägen. The race is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners, and features encouraging pacers, well-stocked aid stations and an atmospheric end to the running season in the Royal National City Park. The event is organised by Marathongruppen together with local athletics clubs, and the surplus goes back to sport.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Fisksjöängsvägen in Norra Djurgården (approx. 800 m from Ropsten metro station)
Certified courses, mostly on asphalt with some gravel; 10 km: +103.9 m, marathon: total elevation gain +439 m
Well-stocked aid stations and lap support, as well as clearly marked kilometre signs
additional: Start/finish at Fisksjöäng (approx. 800 m from Ropsten metro station). Bib collection, pacer tent, food and coffee sales, bag drop for warm-up clothes and toilets at the event area. Changing and shower facilities are available at a nearby venue for a fee, a few hundred metres away. Chip timing by RaceTimer; pacers are available for several finish times (lists by distance). Cut-off times: 10 km 2:00, half marathon 2:30, marathon 5:30 (cut-off at the final lap point at 13:40). Minimum ages: 10 km from age 15 (age 13 when accompanied by a guardian); half marathon and marathon from age 17. Some aids and vehicles (poles, inline skates, strollers, bicycles, handcycles and racing wheelchairs) are not permitted; special conditions apply for guides and wheelchair users. The surplus goes back to sport. Registration is open.

name: Finalloppet Göteborg

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Parvelbanan, ca 250 m, anmälan endast på plats tävlingsdagen. 40 kr

description: Finalloppet is western Sweden’s largest cross-country race. It has been organised by Göteborgs Skidklubb since 1968 and is held at Skatås Motionscentrum in Gothenburg. The event offers several distances (19 km, 10 km, 5.3 km, 2.3 km and 1.9 km, as well as Paraloppet and Parvelbanan) for both competitive and recreational runners. The courses alternate between technical trail sections and wider forest roads, and are marked with clear arrows and kilometre markers. The organiser brings the finish area and services together at the event venue at Skatås and provides water stations, medical care and a sweep crew on all courses.
course_highlights: The 19 km course has an advanced trail section of approximately 2,500 metres
The 10 km course includes a trail section just over 500 metres long that is often wet, muddy and rocky
The courses are marked with orange arrows and coloured kilometre markers; the leading groups are guided by a cyclist
additional: Registration is handled via RaceID (payment by card, Swish or Google Pay and Mobile BankID). You can register several people at the same time and buy gift cards via RaceID. The organiser offers Startklar insurance as an optional add-on, which reimburses the entry fee in the event of illness, injury or pregnancy. The event venue is at Skatås Motionscentrum, with finish and service tents, a medical tent at the finish, and medical staff at certain water stations (Ugglemossen and Svarttjärn). The sweep crew sets off after the last start for each course and is responsible for runners still on the course. Donate 50 kronor to Jontefonden when registering; a GPX file is available to download for the 19 km course.

description: Kroppefjäll Trailrun is an evening race at Kroppefjäll B&B in Dals Rostock, offering runners three main distance options (42 km, 21 km and 10.5 km) in two-person teams, as well as a children’s race around the pond. The course is technical terrain with plenty of singletrack and natural trails, and the race has a relaxed, adventurous atmosphere with no official timing. After the finish, participants can use the large sauna and take a refreshing dip in the pond. Accommodation can also be booked at Kroppefjäll B&B with discounts. The organisers welcome both experienced trail runners and younger participants (Lilla KTR) in a friendly setting.
course_highlights: Approx. 60% singletrack/off-trail, 35% gravel road/forest road and 5% oil-gravel road
Race format: trail running in two-person teams
Lilla KTR: children’s race around the pond (approx. 900 m), with the option to run 1–3 laps
additional: Bus to the start from Kroppefjäll B&B; GPX file for 21 km; bring your own fluids; bib pickup in the days before the race or the evening before; accommodation discounts via Trailrun1/Trailrun2; the Lilla KTR race takes place on 7 November at 18:00; registration deadline: 4/11.

name: Iron Backbone Ultra
description: Iron Backbone Ultra is a trail adventure in Kristinehamn built around the Järnleden and offers three distances (15, 30 and 50 km). The race takes place on varied and characterful terrain—deep forests, bogs, small lakes, pastures and old trails—putting both mental toughness and the joy of running to the test. The start and finish are at Hultets friluftsgård, and the 15 km course partly leaves the Järnleden. The organiser, Topp & Dröm, welcomes both experienced trail runners and those who want to try trail running for the first time.
course_highlights: The course largely follows the Järnleden through varied terrain (forests, bogs, lakes, pastures and old trails)
Start and finish at Hultets friluftsgård, Kristinehamn
The 15 km course partly leaves the Järnleden
additional: Three distances are offered: 15 km, 30 km and 50 km; start and finish at Hultets friluftsgård; from 1 October, places are limited to ensure a specially designed medal for every participant; organiser: Topp & Dröm (contact person Lasse / telephone 073-853 75 21), and the information pages have sections on aid stations and equipment. Start times: 30 km and 50 km at 17:00; 15 km at 17:30. No cups are provided at the aid stations; bring your own cup. Start and finish at Hultets friluftsgård, Kristinehamn. Entry fees are updated over time, and from 1 October, places are limited to secure a specially designed medal for every participant.

name: Jätten Bule-löpet
description: Welcome to the 57th Jätten Bule Run on 31 October 2026 at Bulevallen in Österbymo. The race offers an enchanting forest setting, with trails and gravel roads winding through the area. There are recreational race classes for 10 km, 5 km and 2.4 km, where everyone can enjoy a challenging run surrounded by beautiful scenery. IFK Österbymo warmly welcomes all runners to a well-organised event with timing and excellent service.
course_highlights: The 10 km course runs along floodlit trails, forest paths and gravel roads across hilly terrain
The final 4 km take you through an enchanting forest on winding trails with both climbs and descents
The 5 km course is a miniature version of the 10 km course, marked in blue, while the 2.4 km course follows the floodlit trail
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 09:00 at the IFK Österbymo clubhouse by the start area. Timing is chip-based. Changing rooms are available in the clubhouse. Refreshments, including coffee and hamburgers, are available at the start area. Payment by Swish or cash. Bulis will lead a warm-up at approximately 10:00 before the children’s race starts. Start and finish at Bulevallen, Idrottsvägen, Österbymo.

name: Mustaschmilen Göteborg
description:
Mustaschmilen takes place at Åbytravet in Gothenburg, where the horses make way for runners for a day. We’re looking forward to a festival on 7 November. We’ll fill the stadium with runners of all ages, and welcome you whether you’re an elite runner or a recreational runner. Together with the spectators, sponsors and activities, we’ll make it an unforgettable stadium experience.

Mustaschmilen in Gothenburg has three distances: 5 km, 10 km and a 1 km children’s race. The two longer races will be run on a loop course, with upbeat music and an enthusiastic announcer along the 1,000-metre course.
additional:
10:00 – Bib pickup opens
Be sure to pick up your bib well before the start.
11:00 – 5 km start, all paces
12:15 – Children’s race start, 1 km
12:45 – 10 km race start
14:00 – 10 km recreational start

About 10 minutes before each start, Runacademy will lead a group warm-up.

name: Höstmilen
description: Höstmilen is a trail race in the Kolmården forests outside Åby, north of Norrköping, taking place on 1 November 2026. The course follows trails between Sörsjön and Lillsjön and offers scenic, challenging terrain for both competitive runners and recreational participants. The event is organised by OK Kolmården and has three main race options: the classic 10.6 km, Höstfemman 5.2 km, and races for children and young people.
course_highlights: Trail race on paths between Sörsjön and Lillsjön
Höstmilen 10.6 km (Sörsjön → Lillsjön) and Höstfemman 5.2 km (start/finish at Lillsjön)
Running through the scenic, hilly terrain of the Kolmården forests
additional: Online registration closes on 29 October at 23:00; after that, it is possible to register on 31 October from 11:00 to 14:00 at XXL and at the start area on 1 November. For the classic Höstmilen, a bus runs from Jurslaskolan to the start at Sörsjön. The race information sheet will be published approximately one week before the event. The adult races have just two prize categories: Men and Women. A complete list of registered participants will be published on the “Registered” page. Distances and competition formats are 10.6 km, 5.2 km and children’s races (1.4 or 2.0 km); team, company and school competitions. The Höstmilen race information sheet and registration are available via hostmilen.nu.

name: Energiruset
organizer: IF Göta Karlstad och Karlstads Energi
description: Energiruset is an evening race in Mariebergsskogen, organised in collaboration between IF Göta and Karlstads Energi. The race takes place on Thursday, 5 November 2026, and is family-friendly, with a choice of distances of 2 km and 5 km. The 5 km distance has a competitive category for those who want to test themselves; much of the course runs through woodland, and some sections are unlit. After finishing, all participants are treated to a hot dog by the organisers.
course_highlights: The course runs through Mariebergsskogen, including woodland.
Some sections of the course are unlit; a headlamp is recommended.
Distances: 2 km and 5 km; the 5 km has a competitive category.
additional: Date and location: Mariebergsskogen, Thursday, 5 November 2026. You can buy a headlamp when registering. Practical information (chip collection and exact start times) will be published on the organiser’s website. A previous race briefing is available as a PDF: https://ifgota.se/files/PM_ER_2025.pdf. After the race, IF Göta and Karlstads Energi will treat participants to a hot dog. The course will be open during the evening for non-competitive participants, who can start within a specified time window. The start times are tentatively around 18:00.

name: Nyårsloppet
description:
For the 43rd time, Vallentuna Friidrott invites everyone—from elite athletes to recreational runners and children—to take part in a winter race on the streets and squares in central Vallentuna. Participants and spectators may be met with challenging ice, slushy snow, wonderfully crisp winter weather or a fast asphalt course.
Nyårsloppet is a great way to get a little active before the New Year’s meal and the year’s reflections. And as some people say: “What you do on New Year’s Eve sets the tone for the rest of the year!” So take the opportunity to get active, bring a friend and run or jog around the course.

name: Craft Idre Fjällmaraton
description:
Become unbeatable
We believe everyone has the right to feel unbeatable at some point. Not in relation to anyone else, but in relation to yourself. Unbeatable because you achieved something you didn’t think was possible. Because you dared to do something you didn’t think you could. Because you ventured into unknown territory and won. You won over that little voice telling you that you can’t.

name: Nyårsloppet Vallentuna
description:
The New Year’s Race is a perfect way to get active during the days between Christmas and New Year. For the 42nd time, Vallentuna Friidrott is inviting runners to take part on New Year’s Eve, with everyone from elite athletes to those who prefer a more relaxed pace. A winter race can mean challenging conditions or fast asphalt—we never know until race day. Keep an eye on the weather forecast and read our information. Statistically, conditions have been favourable for running in most years, as the results from previous years show.

Above all, the New Year’s Race is a lovely way to get together to round off the old year and have something to talk about at the celebrations later in the day.

You’re welcome too—we’ll see you there!
additional: Please remember that the New Year’s Race is a winter race, and conditions can vary from year to year. In some years, spiked shoes may be recommended.

name: Österlen Spring Trail
description: Österlen Spring Trail was founded in 2015 and can be described as a recreational race where nature, camaraderie and the experience take centre stage, while performance and time are secondary. The race offers all runners, regardless of ability, a fantastic opportunity to take part in one of three distances: 60 km (Simris Alg Ultra), 30 km (Duo Trail) and 22 km (Teleservice trail). It takes place amid the beautiful natural surroundings of Christinehof Castle in Andrarum, Skåne County, and has 500 metres of elevation gain.

You run four laps.
If you choose the half marathon, you run two laps, and if you choose the quarter marathon, you run one.

name: Uddloppet
description:
Uddloppet is a spring race in Karlshamn, Blekinge, for both recreational and elite runners. It’s a perfect start to the running season and a great way to check your fitness after winter training.
uddloppet.ifudd.se

Distances:
4 km (09:45)
10 km (11:00)
Half marathon (11:00)
Children’s race, 400 m (10:30)
Walking class, 2.5 km (between 09:00 and 13:00)

Course: A scenic, gently hilly route along the sea and through the forest east of Karlshamn. Start and finish at Vägga sports ground.
uddloppet.ifudd.se

Practical information: Parking at Vägga IP; changing facilities and showers at Väggahallen. Race numbers can be collected at Intersport in Karlshamn from Wednesday to Saturday, or at the race-day secretariat.
uddloppet.ifudd.se

Quarter marathon 12:00
Half marathon 13:00

name: STHLM Trail Marathon
description:
A warm welcome to the second edition of STHLM TRAIL MARATHON
All races take place on a very scenic course, approximately 15 km long. Each lap will offer you nearly 500 metres of elevation gain. Expect beautiful views and challenging running, mostly over hilly terrain and mostly on trails, sometimes off-trail, but also on a couple of gentler sections where you can stretch out and run for a few hundred metres.

New for 2026
• Be on the start line as early as April! This time we’re holding the event in early spring, so mark 18 April in your calendar now.
• Kids Trail, a free race for our younger runners (born in 2014 or later).
• Hjärnloppet, a virtual race lasting 18 days, where the entire entry fee goes directly to Hjärnfonden and vital research into epilepsy.
• Course preview runs. On two occasions, we’ll run through the first and second parts of the course.
• Virtual running sessions in the Heyey app to help you stay in shape all the way to the start line in April.

What’s not new for 2026
• The course, a challenging and very scenic route in the area around Lake Flaten.
• Sprint and Ultra, two trail races that challenge you a little extra.
• Grit, the ultimate test, which we don’t think anyone can complete. If you prove us wrong, you’ll win both honour and fame, as well as some prize money.
additional: All information on the organiser’s website

name: Billingen Trail
description:
We invite you to enjoy running on Billingen. This year, the start and finish will be at the Stadium in the Billingen Recreation Area.
The long course is just over 47 km with approximately 930 metres of elevation gain. It goes all the way around northern Billingen, along beautiful trails by the edge of the mountain. As a runner, you’ll experience varied terrain, including deciduous forest, mountain ravines, meadows and spruce forest, as well as beautiful views across the landscape from several places. The surface varies from easy-to-run sections and approximately 6 km of asphalt to some more challenging parts.

The middle-distance course, 21 km, follows the northern section of the Billinge Trail and has approximately 500 metres of elevation gain. The course includes a mix of trails, meadows and roads.

Our shortest distance, 12 km, has just over 200 metres of elevation gain and follows trails of varying difficulty, with some short sections on roads.

Information about the courses and markings may change.

Start:

47 km, 10:00, Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.
21 km, 10:45, Björnasäter, Lerdala. Bus departs from the Billingen Recreation Area at 10:05.
12 km, 11:30, Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.

Finish:

At the Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.

All finishers cross the finish line at the stadium.

name: MRC Finspång Loop Trail Ultra
description: A tough and challenging low-key trail ultra on a 10 km loop with 400 m of elevation gain. After five loops, you’ll have covered the ultra distance of 50 km and 2,000 m of elevation gain. Technical trail running on singletrack and animal trails through dramatic forest! Welcome!
course_highlights: Very technical terrain on animal trails and narrow single tracks
Five loops of 10 km with ~400 m climb per loop (50 km / ~2000 m total)
Possible thin morning snow that thaws as the sun rises (seasonal conditions)
additional: More information is available on Instagram

name: Isaberg500
description:
Isaberg 500 is the race we love running ourselves and the foundation of the entire trail weekend. It’s a perfect mix of trails, hills, sweat and tears that brings to mind spectacular races in both the Swedish mountains and the Alps. Isaberg 500 also features switchbacks, long, enjoyable downhill stretches and fantastic views. In between, you can enjoy winding trails through enchanting forests. Isaberg 500 includes at least 500 metres of elevation gain and is perfect for anyone training for a mountain marathon or similar race.

NEW FOR 2025!
When Isaberg500 started, Jättestigen was a big talking point. A few years later, it was closed due to the risk of landslides. In 2025, Jättestigen returns as part of Isaberg500, but under a new name — Jättetrappan...

Isaberg500 is a race in the Outnorth Trail Tour 2025.
course_highlights: Trail race with varied trails and hills, with a technical character reminiscent of races in the mountains and the Alps
Multisport around the Isaberg summit: kayaking, mountain biking and trail running — Solo and Duo categories
Isaberg Gravel: a circuit of approximately 45 km, starting and finishing in Åsenhöga; Elite/up to age 50: 3 laps, older riders/sport recreation: 2 laps, recreational: 1 lap
additional: Contact GI by mobile at +46 703 815 118 or email at gimulti@gmail.com. Organisers: GI Folkestad and Martin Jepson. Guided rides for cycling groups can be booked; the organisers have ready-made routes that can be adapted to the group’s needs. Main distance: approximately 10.5 km (Distans Trailtour); Kids Trail: approximately 2 km with approximately 150 metres of elevation gain; start time: Sunday at 12:00; location: Isaberg/Anderstorp; contact: niklas@isabergtrail.se.

name: Landehof 4-Årstider Höstloppet 2026
description: Landehof 4 Seasons Autumn Race 2026 is an orienteering event held at Landehofstugan, Landvetter, on November 3. The race offers a challenging autumn setting with darkness, rain, wind and slippery roots, providing an authentic autumn experience in the forest. Participants can enjoy an exciting, traditional orienteering experience in beautiful surroundings. Start lists and live results will be published well in advance of and during race day.
course_highlights: Orienteering in an autumn setting with darkness and slippery roots
Challenging terrain in the forest around Landehofstugan
Traditional autumn race with a long history and a strong sense of community
additional: The start list will be published from Friday, October 30, and updated until the registration deadline. Live results and the results list will be available. Register by logging in with your personal identity number on OK Landehof's registration page. QR codes are available to easily share the invitation and registration details with colleagues or training partners. Start and gathering point at Landehofstugan in Landvetter. A headlamp is recommended. Registration is open until November 1, 2026.

name: Hörby Marknadslopp
description:
Frosta OK is organising an evening race for the 53rd time during Hörby Market, with three different distances:

Marknadsloppet 12.6 km: the competitive class starts at 18:30, and the recreational class starts at 18:40.

Bil-Månsson loppet 6.1 km: everyone starts at 18:50.

CAN-CAN loppet 3.4 km: everyone starts at 19:00.

The race starts and finishes in central Hörby, with much of the route running through woodland.
Varied surfaces: asphalt, gravel roads and trails. See maps.

Don't miss this opportunity!
additional:
Register at www.marknadsloppet.nu — right up until the race starts.

Late registration is available at the entrance to Lågehallarna (Byggmästaregatan 4) after 16:00 on race day.

Parking for runners is available at Lågehallarna from 16:00.
Signposting from National Road 13. 55.8552,13.6528

All information about preparations, registration, the course and directions is available at the link:
https://marknadsloppet.nu/information/

name: Mariestads Marathon
description: The race follows the shore of Lake Vänern along a cycle path. It is a lap race: the 7 km distance is one lap, 21.1 km is three laps, and 42.2 km is six laps.
additional: Information will be available on the website.

name: Saucony Djurgårdsvarvet 10K
description: Saucony Djurgårdsvarvet is the most generous race of the year, where the joy of running meets the beautiful scenery of Djurgården. The course winds along gravel and asphalt roads, offering a wonderful mix of challenge and enjoyment. The first 600 people to register will receive a specially designed T-shirt, and after crossing the finish line, a relaxing After Run awaits with a barbecue and non-alcoholic drinks from Bryggmästarens. A portion of the registration fee also goes to Sweden for UNHCR, so every step counts—for you and for someone in need.

name: Kretsloppet i Borås
description: Experience Borås at its best—run Kretsloppet! On September 19, we’ll once again fill the streets of Borås with runners of all ages for a running festival you have to experience. Sign up with family, friends and colleagues, and cross the finish line to the cheers of the crowd in the heart of Borås city centre. All courses are on asphalt, relatively flat and in central Borås. A warm welcome to the running festival!

name: Backyard Ulötra Sölvesborg
description:
What is Backyard Ultra?
Backyard Ultra takes place on a marked 6,706-metre loop, and each participant has one hour to complete it. A new start takes place at the top of every hour, and as long as you can complete the loop within an hour, you remain in the race. You win by being the most enduring and ultimately getting to run one final lap alone! A fun race and concept with a very welcoming, community-minded atmosphere, where many participants set their distance records!

name: Mattila Trail Run
description: On Saturday, September 26, 2026, the Mattila Trail Run will take place, following its successful debut in 2025. The race runs through the beautiful Finnskogen forest in Värmland, across marshes, over boardwalks, and through a mix of old-growth and managed forest. Some sections take you past cultural sites, as much of the route passes through the historic cultural heritage of Finnskogen. Enjoy a memorable trail-running experience with plenty of challenging climbs and, in some places, technical trails. Welcome to a true adventure!

MiniSpringtime is a 1 km race for children born in 2016–2020. Alla Kan Springa is a race for people with disabilities (all ages) and follows the same course as MiniSpringtime.

name: Fredsloppet
description: Fredsloppet 2026 is a peace and solidarity race held at several locations in Sweden, including Stockholm, between 15 August and 18 October 2026. The event is more than a running race; it is an expression of peace, justice and solidarity, supporting Palestinian and Cuban organisations. Participants can choose from different distances, including 5 km and 10 km, as well as walking categories and mini peace races for children. The event encourages people to organise their own Fredsloppet races, and the surplus goes to peace and solidarity work.
course_highlights: Several locations in Sweden, including Stockholm
Distances for all ages and levels, including children’s and family races
Focus on peace, solidarity and justice, supporting Palestinian organisations
additional: 75% of the proceeds go to Palestinian aid, and the event celebrates its 40th anniversary in 2026. Participants can register via fredsloppet.se. The event includes water stations, medals and the option to register on the day.

description: You run or walk 7.3 km through beautiful scenery on gravel roads and along a section of the Finnskogleden trail. The race has received a lot of praise for its scenic course.
additional: Prizes will be awarded, including a perpetual trophy from Magnor Glassworks (one for the men and one for the women), as well as first, second and third prizes in each class. A “mountain prize” will also go to the first woman and the first man to reach the course’s highest point. Those who prefer to take it a little easier won’t go home empty-handed either. All participants receive a certificate, and there will be a draw based on race numbers.

name: Ultra Caballo Blanco Suecia
description:
Only the 100-mile race starts on Friday (08:00); the 100 km and 50-mile races start on Saturday (06:00).
All three races have their own routes (they have nothing in common with CBMR, which takes place on the same day). The 50-mile and 100-mile races have some staffed aid stations, which are also shared with the 100 km race, which has its own stations as well. The 100-mile race is virtually entirely unsupported, apart from a few unmanned water stations. You also pass a well-stocked country store and a church with water and toilets.
All three races offer the option of a drop bag.
The courses are completely unmarked, so you navigate using a downloaded GPX file...
additional:
We don’t have paper cups, so bring a cup!
Hot food, drinks, coffee and cake are served after the finish.

The entry fee includes 120:-, which is sent to a children’s race in Urique, Mexico!

name: Caballo Blanco Memorial Run (CBMR)
description:
This is the route that Caballo Blanco (aka Micah True) and I ran on 2011-09-26, when he was visiting Sweden at my invitation. In spring 2012, we received the news that he had died. We then organised a memorial race on 2012-09-22. It became a tradition, and eventually the race offered 1, 2 or 4 laps of the route, which is approximately 11 km and has approximately 150 metres of elevation gain.
See also Ultra Caballo Blanco Suecia — an ultra race held at the same time.
An article I wrote quite a while ago, when we introduced the 50-mile race:
https://redsports.se/CBM/TheStory.html
additional:
The 4-lap race starts at 12:00, while the 1- and 2-lap races start at 15:00.
Please note that you must bring your own cup/mug.
The entry fee includes drinks, energy products, and a hot meal with coffee and cake after the race.

name: GUM - Gotland Ultramarathon
description:
One of Sweden’s most beautiful ultramarathons. The race starts at 9:00 at Hallshuk in northern Gotland, and the course heads south along the coast, with the sea on your right all the way to Visby. The route is approximately 50 km, with very varied terrain.

name: XC-race Linköping
description: Linköping XC-race is an annual cross-country race organised by Linköpings OK in Vidingsjön, Linköping. The race offers a marked 5 km loop through varied terrain, including trails and marshland, and is open to both recreational runners and competitive classes. Participants can choose between 5 km, 10 km for men and women, and a 5 km recreational class. The 10 km races cover two laps. The event is known for its challenging, muddy terrain, and the start and finish are at Vidingsjö Motionscentrum.

name: Västerås Marathon
description:
NEW RACE 2026

Västerås Marathon offers three distances — 42 km, 21 km and 10 km — on a flat, fast course through the heart of the city and along the beautiful shores of Lake Mälaren. The course is a loop course, with 10 km per lap.
Experience the joy of running in a well-organised race for all levels.

The race is for everyone who enjoys running, from beginners to elite athletes. All ages and paces are welcome, and generous time limits will be set for completing the race.

A warm welcome!

description: Are you among those who prefer trails to asphalt? Whether you’re a curious beginner, a recreational runner, or an elite runner, Kilterrängen is for you. The course is just as suitable for running at full speed as for jogging, walking with poles, or hiking. You can also choose to run 6 km, with the same tough finish as the longer course.

name: Löparfesten
description:
The running festival offers several different races, with something for everyone!

Whether you’re looking to set a personal best in the half marathon or prefer a walk with good friends, there’s a great race to choose from!

EKO ½Maran is for experienced runners, FORMTOPPEN Milen is a wonderful challenge, and the slightly shorter Here We Go 5an is for happy recreational runners or those who prefer to run fast but short. For those who want to take it a little easier, perhaps bring walking poles or a stroller, or simply enjoy nature, there’s Here We Go 5an – Promenad!

There are also races for younger participants—Papricaloppet—for everyone up to 12 years old! We also have Rulleruset for everyone with a disability! At Rulleruset, you can choose between a shorter 1.4 km race and a slightly longer 5 km race!

As we said, there’s something for everyone!

name: Uppsala Marathon
description:
UPPSALA MARATHON
17 OCTOBER 2026
Through centuries of history – one step at a time
MARATHON • HALF MARATHON • MARATHON RELAY
Celebrate 10 years with us!
Challenge yourself and experience one of Sweden’s most popular races in beautiful autumnal Uppsala. Run the marathon or half marathon, or gather family, friends or colleagues and take part in the marathon relay.
Uppsala Marathon is turning 10!
Over 42,195 metres, the course takes you through some of Uppsala’s most historic, scenic and remarkable surroundings. From the castle and Carolina Hill to the River Fyris, the city centre and leafy green spaces – a unique combination of running, history, culture and a festive atmosphere.
Whether you’re an experienced marathon runner or taking part for the first time, you’re warmly welcome to help write the next chapter in the race’s history.
All participants are invited to enjoy a post-run gathering, and all finishers receive a technical T-shirt and this year’s exclusive 10th-anniversary medal.
More information and registration:
https://www.uppsalamarathon.se/

name: Änglamilen
description: Änglamilen is a long-established fun run in the heart of Ängelholm. Participants experience the town, the sea and the forest all in the same 10 kilometres. The 5 km race begins with a lovely run through the park in the charming Hembygdsparken. After approximately 2.7 km, the course crosses the Rönne River and continues along the beautiful riverside path in Nybroskogen. Finally, the course turns back across the river, with a sprint to the finish at Tullakrok. The 10 km course starts the same way as the 5 km route, but turns north after about a kilometre. Runners are treated to beautiful views over Skälderviken and its harbour, with Kullaberg visible in the background. After approximately 7.7 km, the courses join again, and runners can enjoy the beautiful riverside path in Nybroskogen.
additional:
The deadline for standard registration is 18 May, but late registration is available until one hour before the start of each race.

Stay up to date by following us on Facebook and Instagram
